Those hell-beings, in this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, are burned, cooked, and thoroughly rotted; they are dispersed and melted away until their accumulated evil karma is exhausted and destroyed, and they become breathless and putrid; only then do they manage to escape from that hell.
In that hell, the Yama-wardens rebuke the sinners and speak these verses:
"Bound by the snare of wife and children, you are brought to the abode of hell;
for what reason were you deceived by your own mind as to commit such evil karma?"
For the sake of your wife, children, friends, and kinsmen, you committed various evil deeds; you were not a wise person.
You truly did not love yourself when you arrived here in this place of hell.
For what reason, as a son, have you committed evil deeds to such an extent?
If, deceived by wife and children, one commits various evil deeds and later feels no remorse in the heart, that person enters hell.
You alone shall be scorched in hell, consumed by your own evil karma;
wife, brothers, and other kinsmen cannot save you.
If you are deceived by delusion and fail to perform wholesome deeds, [you will suffer thus].
Later you shall find no joy; now you grieve in vain.
If one follows desire and hatred, the deluded mind is the ultimate deceiver;
for the sake of the pleasures of wife and children, all things lead downward.
"One's own karma bestows its own fruit; through the karma of sentient beings, they arrive here.
By performing wholesome karma one is born in heaven; by performing evil karma one comes to this place.
Thus, the Yama-wardens there rebuke the hell-beings in such great numbers, reproaching them with these various words of censure:
"If you yourself have committed evil deeds, whom do you wish to make eat such food now?
If you perform good deeds yourself, you will receive good in return;
if you perform unwholesome deeds, you will receive the unwholesome for yourself."
"What is not done is not obtained; what is done is never lost.
You performed these actions in the past, and now you receive this retribution.

Thus, that person in hell remains for a long time in the Saṃjīva Great Hell, undergoing constant burning and boiling for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted—having delighted in and frequently committed such acts of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct—the resulting fruit of retribution inflicts suffering upon them at all times without ceasing.
When their evil karma is exhausted, they may finally escape from that hell.
If, due to the ripening of virtuous karma from long ago in past lives, they are not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet if they are born among humans, they will be poor and short-lived, obtaining an inferior wife, or even if they obtain a good one, she will have illicit relations with other men.
If one is without a wife and obtains a common, lowly body, being made to serve by others, this is the residual retribution of the power of that karma.
Having obtained such [conditions] through such evil karma, one is able to delude and mislead people, causing them to enter hell.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the sixteen distinct locations of the Saṃjīva Great Hell. What are these sixteen?
First is the location called the Place of Suffering from Vast Quantities;
second is the location called the Place of Carving and Evisceration.
Third, the place where the three channels are severed;
fourth, the place of evil views;
fifth, the place of the sphere.
Sixth is named the Place of Much Suffering;
seventh is named the Place of Enduring Suffering;
eighth is named the Place of Zhu-zhu-zhu-zhu.
The ninth is named Wherever and Whenever;
the tenth is named Source of Tears and Fire;
the eleventh is named Place of the Extinction of All Faculties.
Twelfth is the place of suffering called "Without a Far Shore";
thirteenth is the place called "Padma";
fourteenth is the place called "Mahāpadma."
The fifteenth is named the Place of Fire Basins;
the sixteenth is named the Place of Iron Fire Dust.
There are sixteen such distinct locations within the Great Hell. By what karma are sentient beings born in those places?
That bhikṣu reflects and observes:

"If a person commits three kinds of evil and unwholesome karmas—namely, killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct—and delights in practicing them and does so frequently, they will certainly undergo rebirth in the Saṃjīva Great Hell, a place of suffering and affliction."
"By what karma are sentient beings born into the first great place of suffering? He sees:

there are those who engage in sexual misconduct when it is improper, who lack correct observation, and who delight in perverse desires; they are born within that hell, the great place of suffering, where they undergo intense torment, namely: [the following]..."
Blazing, sharp iron spikes pierce them through and through; these iron spikes are driven upward from below, emerging from their backs;
they are pierced again, emerging from their bellies;
they are pierced yet again, emerging from their waists.
Again he pierced him, and [the blood] came out from his shoulder;
again he pierced him, and it came out from his side;
again he pierced him, and it came out from his throat.
Again he pierced him, and [the pus] came out from his mouth;
again he broke open his skull, and it came out from there;
again he pierced him, and it came out from his ear.
Those hell-beings, being thus impaled, have all their limbs and members completely pierced and torn apart; they undergo great agony as every part of their bodies is burned and boiled.
Having already undergone such various sufferings and afflictions, they are further subjected to even more grievous suffering, namely:
their testicles are pincered out with glowing iron tongs;
or they are plucked out and eaten by iron vultures.

In this way, as long as the accumulated karma they have created has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they will experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
and if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma as the third type of person—namely, eunuchs and the like—that is the residual karmic fruit of those unwholesome deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell: what other places are there?
Through seeing, hearing, and knowledge, he perceives another distinct place called the Place of Flaying and Carving; this is the second secondary location within the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and are born in the Section of Carving and Flaying.
The karmic actions of killing and stealing, along with their retributions, are as previously described.
What is sexual misconduct? It is as follows:
In a place where sexual intercourse with women is forbidden, he commits sexual misconduct by way of the mouth.

Because of this unwholesome karmic cause and condition, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, he falls into an evil destination, the Great Universal Hell, and is born in the Section for Carving and Eviscerating, where he undergoes great suffering and affliction. As for that suffering:
the Yama-wardens drive hot iron nails into his mouth, which emerge from his head; once they have emerged, they pull them out with violent force.
Furthermore, their mouths are nailed shut, and [the nails] emerge from their ears;
moreover, iron bowls filled with molten copper are poured into their mouths. The molten copper, blazing with heat, burns their lips, and next it burns their tongues.
Having burned the tongues, it next burns the eyes; thus it burns the throat, then the heart, then the abdomen, proceeding in this sequence until it reaches the anus and exits from below.

Thus, for those who delight in and frequently commit such wrong conduct, the retribution for their evil karma lies in hell. There they undergo various sufferings in this manner for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of years, constantly being burned and boiled. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be released from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one’s mouth will always have a foul odor like that of rotting gas, and this will permeate others such that all detest it—this is the residual retribution of that former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell to see what other locations exist therein.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is another distinct location called the "Vein-Severing Place" (Nāḍī-nāḍī-cchedana), which is the third secondary section of the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell at the location where the veins are severed.
The karmic actions of killing and stealing, along with their retributions, are as previously described.
What is sexual misconduct? It is as follows:

If one engages in sexual misconduct with a woman through an improper orifice, and she does not consent, yet he uses his own strength to coerce her, that person, by reason of such evil karma, at the breaking up of the body after death, falls into the evil destination of the Great Universal Hell (Sahāmahānaraka), specifically into the Section of Severed Veins, where they undergo great suffering.
That is to say: a hot tube filled with molten copper is placed in their mouth until it is full; they cry out and shriek, making these words:
"I am now all alone.

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be released from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet, if one is born among humans, the wife one obtains is so enamored with others that the husband is unable to restrain her—this is the residual karmic retribution of that evil deed.
The karmic fruits of the actions he has accumulated do not perish; he must still experience them.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, next examines the Great Universal Hell (Saṃjīva) to see what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place called the Place of Evil Views (*dur-dṛṣṭi-sthāna*), which is the fourth secondary location of the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees: there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in and frequently practicing these acts, who fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and are born in the place of evil views.
The karma of killing and stealing, as well as their retributions, are as previously described.
What constitutes misconduct?
It is as follows:
there are those who seize another's child and forcibly commit misconduct with them; being themselves physically superior, they cause the child to weep and cry out.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, the Saṃjīva Great Hell, and are born in a place of wrong views where they undergo great suffering and distress. Specifically, they see their own sons and daughters;
because of their evil karma, they see their own children within the hell, and they give rise to a heavy, affectionate love for those children, just as they did when they were in the human realm.
Having seen this, the Yama-wardens either pierce his private parts with iron staffs or iron awls, or they drive iron hooks into his private parts.
Having witnessed such suffering of his own son, he himself gives rise to great anguish; his love-stricken grief is so overwhelming that it cannot be endured.
This suffering born of love does not equal even one-sixteenth part of the suffering caused by being burned by fire.
Having been thus tormented by mental suffering, that person further undergoes physical suffering, namely:
seized there by the Yama-wardens, with his head and face downward, they pour molten copper from a red-hot iron bowl into his anus; it enters his body and burns his small intestine (*pakvāśaya*);
having burned the small intestine, it next burns the large intestine (*guda*).
After burning the large intestine, he next burns the small intestine;
after burning the small intestine, he next burns the stomach;
having burned the stomach, he proceeds in this sequence:
Next, his throat is burned;
once the throat is burned, next his gullet is burned;
once the gullet is burned—
Next, the tongue-root is burned;
once the tongue-root is burned, next the tongue is burned;
having burned the tongue, next the gums are burned.
Having burned the gums, it next burns the head;
having burned the head, it next burns the brain;
having burned them in this manner, it exits from below.

Those who practice such wrong conduct undergo such suffering; for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years, through the transformation of their karma, they see their own sons, and their bodies and minds suffer as they fully experience these two kinds of suffering—bodily and mental. For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years, they constantly endure great agony; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they will suffer without ceasing at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be released from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet if one is born among humans, one will have no children. Even if there is impurity, it does not form a seed, and the people of the world all say:
"This person is not a man."
Everyone despises and loathes him; this is the residual karmic retribution of that evil deed.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, next examines the Saṃjīva Great Hell to see if there are any other distinct locations within it.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called the "Ball-shaped Place" (Gola-sthāna), which resembles a tightly rolled ball; this is the fifth secondary location of the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees: there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and are born in the Piṇḍa region.
The killing of living beings, the stealing, and their karmic retribution are as previously described.
What constitutes misconduct?
It is as follows:
suppose there is a person who, upon seeing a cow or a mule and having observed their sexual organs, gives rise to conceptual discrimination in his mind:
"Since this place is no different from that of human women," having thought thus,
he immediately conceived the notion of them being human women and engaged in sexual intercourse.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into the Avīci Great Hell, being born in the Section of Spheres (Piṇḍa-sthāna) to undergo great suffering and affliction. That is to say:

because of their evil karma, they see in the hell what appears to be an ox or a horse; through the discrimination of their own minds, they perceive them as human women just as they previously recalled, and whether it was originally a cow or a mare, upon seeing them, they immediately conceive the thought that they are human women. Their lustful mind becomes intensely inflamed, and they immediately rush toward such oxen or horses.

Within the bodies of the oxen and horses, there is a fire of iron flames. When that person approaches the private organs of the oxen and horses, due to the cause of their evil karma, they enter those organs; having entered, they fall into their bellies, which are filled with hot fire. There they undergo suffering, being constantly burned and boiled for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, their bodies so thoroughly cooked and rotted that they cannot utter a sound.

Within that dark interior of the belly, they are tormented by suffering; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they are constantly being burned at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that hellish place.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will be born in a country lacking propriety and benevolence, where one’s own wife is violated by others, and one does not feel jealousy—this being the residual fruit of the causes of such perverse actions.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell to see if there are other distinct locations within it.
Through seeing, hearing, and knowledge,
he perceives another distinct location called "Great Affliction" (Bahuduḥkha), which is the sixth secondary region of the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell, a place of manifold suffering and affliction.
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing and stealing are as previously explained;
what, then, is sexual misconduct? It is as follows:
A man engages in male [sexual misconduct].

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when his body breaks up and his life ends, he falls into an evil destination—the Great Earth Hell, a place of manifold suffering and affliction—where he undergoes great torment.

By the power of accumulated karma, he sees his original male companion within the hell; with hair ablaze with flames and his entire body likewise engulfed in fire, his form is as hard and solid as a diamond, and he comes to embrace him.
Once they have been embraced, all their limbs and members completely dissolve, like a clump of sand;
though dead, they revive again due to the causes of their former unwholesome and evil karma.

Filled with extreme terror toward those flaming people, they flee and run away, only to fall over a precipitous cliff. Before they have even reached the ground while still suspended in mid-air, flaming-beaked crows peck and tear them apart piece by piece until they are like mustard seeds; these parts then immediately rejoin, and only after that do they reach the ground.
Once they have arrived at that ground, there are further jackals with flaming mouths (*jvālāmukha*) that devour them until only bones remain; yet the flesh grows back again.

Once the flesh has grown back, the *Yama* messengers take them and place them in flaming cauldrons to boil them once more. In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years, they are boiled and eaten, divided and scattered. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of manifold suffering.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will lose countless wives and fail to obtain even a single wife—this shall be the ultimate outcome.
Even if one has a wife of one's own, one becomes weary of her and takes pleasure in others;
this is the residual fruit of the causes of such unwholesome actions.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines whether there are other distinct locations within the Great Hell.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called the Place of Enduring Suffering, which is the seventh subsidiary division of the Crushing Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and are born in the place of enduring suffering.
The karmic actions of killing and stealing, along with their retributive fruits, are as previously described.
What constitutes misconduct?
It is as follows:

there are those who, having defeated another's army or nation and captured their women, either engage with them themselves or give them to others, whether by way of the proper path or not by way of the proper path.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body breaks up and life ends, they fall into the evil realm of the Saṃjīva Great Hell, born into the place of enduring suffering and undergoing great torment. As for what constitutes this suffering:
the Yama-wardens suspend them upon a tree with their heads and faces downward and their feet upward; a great fire blazes below, burning their entire body, rising up from the face.

The fire of that hell is of such extreme and blazing heat, and the body of that sinner is so fragile, tender, and soft—especially because the eyes are most delicate—that it is completely consumed without remainder; yet, once the body of that sinner has been burnt away, it is born again.
That person thus experiences extreme suffering and torment, which is harsh and unbearable.

Thus born in that hell, that person undergoes great anguish, crying out, shouting, groaning, and weeping; as they cry out with their mouth agape, the fires of that hell enter through the mouth. Once the fire has entered, it first burns the heart;
having burned the heart, it next burns the lungs, proceeding in this sequence to the stomach, the large intestine, the vital organs, and the anus.
Having been burned in this manner, they are next burned at their feet.
Having already endured such suffering from being burned, crows further come to devour their bodies.
Experiencing these two kinds of great suffering, they cry out and shriek, yet the burning does not cease.
In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they undergo extreme suffering and affliction within the hells.
Such suffering is without parallel or comparison.

For immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, as long as their evil karma has not decayed or perished and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times.
When their evil karma is exhausted, they may finally escape from that place in hell.

If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past of previous lives, they are not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals, but are born among humans in a place of similar karma, even if they obtain a beautiful wife of peerless elegance, she will be destroyed and plundered by the army of officials; because of the power of their evil karma, they will wail and cry out, their hearts shattered with anguish.

In that manner, within those hells and among humans, such a person undergoes great suffering and affliction at two times and in two places—the agony of wailing, crying out, lamenting, and so forth—which is the remaining retributive fruit of the causes of their own wrong actions.
*Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna Sūtra*, Fascicle Six *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna Sūtra*,
Fascicle Seven Translated by the Bactrian Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Yuan Wei Dynasty.
Chapter on the Hells, Part Three:
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next further examines the Saṃjīva Great Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
Furthermore, there is another location; that place is named Zhu-zhu-zhu-zhu (Cucūcū), which is the eighth distinct sub-region of the Saṃghāta Hell.
Those who habitually engage in and frequently commit the acts of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct fall into the Zhu-zhu-zhu-zhu section of the Saṃghāta Hell.
What karma causes sentient beings to be born in that place?
He knows through seeing and hearing:
if a person habitually commits and frequently engages in killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, they will fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and be born in the location of the Zhu-zhu Zhu-zhu Hell.
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing and stealing are as previously explained.
What is sexual misconduct?
It is as follows:

There are those who, failing to observe carefully, engage in sexual misconduct with sheep or donkeys because they perceive them as not being human women; such persons do not give rise to reverence for the Buddha, whether they are at a stūpa or near a stūpa.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, the Saṃjīva Great Hell, and are born in the Zhu-zhu Zhu-zhu hell-pit, where they undergo great suffering and affliction, namely:
being constantly bitten and eaten by iron ants, such that every part of their body experiences great suffering and affliction.
The fires of that hell fill the interior of their bellies; those hell-beings are scorched and boiled both inside and out, receiving this evil retribution for the evil karma they themselves sowed.
Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, there are always cruel insects called *zhuzhu* that devour their flesh within the hells and drink their blood;
having drunk the blood, they next sever their tendons.
Having severed the tendons, he next breaks the bones;
having broken the bones, he next drinks the marrow;
having drunk the marrow, he eats the large and small intestines.

Once those hell-beings have been thus burned, thus scorched, and thus devoured, they utter various cries of lamentation and wailing, weeping and sobbing bitterly. In this manner, as long as their unwholesome and evil karma—which is unpleasant and undesirable—has not been exhausted through experience, they will for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years constantly be burned, boiled, scorched, roasted, and consumed. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been spent, they will suffer without ceasing at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be able to escape that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will have many enemies and adversaries. Even if one resides in a royal capital, one will find no power there; one will be constantly impoverished, lacking the means of subsistence, and will not enjoy a long life.
This is due to the power of that wrong conduct and evil karma, whereby one receives the remaining residual retribution among human beings.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma,
next examines the Saṃjīva Great Hell to see what other places exist therein.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place called Kha-kha-he, which is the ninth distinct sub-region of the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what kind of karmic retribution and accumulated karma does one fall into this Kha-kha-he region of the Saṃghāta Hell, having fully and universally perfected those deeds?
He sees, hears, and knows:

if a person kills living beings, commits theft, or engages in sexual misconduct, and delights in practicing these acts frequently, they will fall into the Saṃjīva hell, in the region called Kākhāṭika.
The karmic actions of killing and stealing, along with their retributions, are as previously described.
What is sexual misconduct?
It is when people from frontier regions engage in sexual desire with sisters and others—those who are improper objects for such acts.
It is the natural law of that realm that those born there suffer the consequences of their transgressions.

Due to the causes and conditions of such evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they are reborn in the Saṃghāta Hell at the location known as Kha-kha-khi, where they undergo great suffering and distress.
That is to say: within that hell, they are constantly burned and boiled, beaten by the Yama-rogues, and let out agonizing shrieks whose sound pervades five thousand yojanas.
Before those hell-beings have reached the hell, while still in the intermediate state (*antarābhava*), they hear that roaring sound.
The roar is extremely terrible and unbearable to hear.

Because of their perverted perceptions, they hear those wails as the sound of singing, the clapping of hands, and various kinds of conversation; due to the power of their evil karma, they find pleasure in hearing them and give rise to such thoughts:
"May I reach that place of such sounds.
Having thought thus, he is swiftly reborn in that place.
By what causes and conditions does this occur?
Existence arises conditioned by grasping.
Within that intermediate state (*antarābhava*), wherever the mind conceives of and desires to grasp, there one is born.
Once the mind has grasped that [object], one is born in that place.

Once born in that place, at the very moment of birth they experience the suffering of hell; they hear the naturally horrific sounds of hell, which are characterized by urgent and violent agony, beyond comparison and indescribable, as they undergo great torment.
Having heard these evil sounds, their minds are further shattered, and they undergo great suffering and affliction, namely:
there is an iron mountain named Mount Kukūla; that mountain is ablaze with flames, and those flames reach an extreme height of five thousand yojanas into the realm of space.
There are iron trees there, upon which are iron crows; their bodies are ablaze as they fill the tops of those trees.
That mountain is set on fire, with no empty space between the flames; due to the power of their evil karma, these blazing fires are constantly burning without ceasing.
Due to their evil karma, they see lotus groves filling that mountain; having seen the lotuses, those hell-beings call out to one another, saying:
"Come here! Come here!"
"Thus, upon this mountain there are many cool forests and lush, verdant groves; let us go there together.

The *yama-puruṣas* strike the hell-beings while raining down knives and stones from above. Out of fear, the sinners run toward that mountain, hoping for rescue and exemption, looking for a master and seeking a refuge.

When such a sinner reaches that mountain, the mountain is entirely filled with hot flames and many flaming crows with extremely sharp iron beaks; having seen this, those hell-beings, the crows swiftly fly toward them.
Those hell-beings have flaming crows come to split open their heads;

furthermore, there are crows that come to take their brains, crows that come to take their eyes, crows that come to take their noses, crows that come to take their cheeks, and crows that come to take their skin. Furthermore...
Crows came to take his ribs; further crows came to take his feet; further crows came to take his tongue;
further crows came to take his neck; further crows came to take the skin of his head;
further crows came to take his throat; and further crows came to take his heart.
Furthermore, there were crows that came to take his lungs; others came to take his small and large intestines;
others came to take the skin of his abdomen; others came to take the area below his navel and his private parts;
others came to take his thighs; and others came to take his calves.
Furthermore, there are crows that come to take the skin of the heels; others come to take the skin of the soles of the feet;
others come to take their toes; others come to eat them piece by piece; others come to take the ribs piece by piece;
others come to take the bones of the flanks; and others come to take only [the remaining parts].
From the bones on one side of their hands, crows come and take them entirely along with all the other limbs;
furthermore, crows come to extract the marrow. Thus these many crows devour the hell-beings, eating them limb by limb;
yet, due to the power of their karmic offenses, they are reborn even as they are being eaten.

Because they give rise to fear toward those *kukūla* fires and the *yama-rākṣasas*, they run hither and thither throughout Mount Kukkula, seeking rescue and seeking refuge, and climb up Mount Kukkula.

Having climbed that mountain, due to their evil karma, blazing fires fill the space and come to cover their bodies; thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they are burned and yet reborn. Because of the power of the evil karma they have accumulated, they undergo such great suffering and affliction.

If one ascends further to the summit of Mount Kukūla, there is again a mass of flames at the mountain peak reaching five thousand yojanas in height; those flames blow upward into the air and burn, like the burning of flying insects.

Thus they undergo great suffering for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, yet they do not die; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times.

Only when the evil karma resulting from their frequent and habitual practice of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct has been fully exhausted will they finally be released from that hellish realm.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, all parts of one's body will be putrid and foul-smelling, one will contract malignant leprosy or suffer from delusional illness, one will constantly face many adversaries, remain perpetually impoverished, and be born in an evil land—
these are the remaining residual fruits of the karma they have accumulated.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell to see what other locations exist there.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is another distinct location called "Tear-Fire-Emergence," which is the tenth subsidiary section of the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, practicing and frequently committing these acts, and thus fall into the Saṃghāta Hell, the Place from Which Tears and Fire Emerge.
The karmic actions of killing and stealing, along with their retributions, are as previously described.
What is sexual misconduct?

If a bhikṣuṇī has previously engaged in impure conduct with another person and thereby violated her prohibitions, and if someone subsequently commits such an act with that bhikṣuṇī, that person, by reason of these causes and conditions of evil karma, at the dissolution of the body after death, will fall into an evil destination—the Saṃjīva Great Hell, the Place from Which Fire-Teardrops Emerge—where they undergo great suffering and affliction. Specifically, they experience suffering corresponding to their own past deeds; that suffering is harsh and produced by unwholesome karma, namely:

Enveloped by a great conflagration that burns everywhere, fire issues from their eyes as tears; those tears are fire that immediately consumes their bodies, and thus those beings in hell undergo such various kinds of suffering and affliction.
Furthermore, they undergo other various sufferings:
the Yama-wardens split open their eye sockets and fill them with *khadira* charcoal, splitting the bones of their eyes as if splitting bamboo.
In that hell, such is the terror of its evils.
Furthermore, with iron hooks, iron pestles, and iron shackles, they hook, slice, strike, and pound them until their bodies are scattered;
with hot iron tongs, they split open their anus and fill it with molten white tin, thus burning them from within.

Furthermore, there is a great fire that burns his body from the outside; thus, burned intensely by these two kinds—both internally and externally—he experiences the foremost suffering, urgent and terrible anguish, and undergoes such immeasurable varieties of manifold sufferings in their entirety.
The Yama-wardens rebuked him with this verse:
“Filled within with molten white tin, Burned on the outside by a great fire,
Tormented intensely and undergoing great suffering— Such is the person of evil karma in hell.”
If karma gives rise to bitter fruits, one receives the retribution of evil suffering and affliction;
within the three realms, there is no analogy that can describe it.
The three types of karma and their three fruits arise within the three realms.
Three transgressions give rise to three states of mind, and the retribution of suffering ripens in three places.
Such karmic retribution as this arises within the three realms;
through the conjunction of causes and conditions, such diverse phenomena emerge.
As the mind acts, so it turns; in such and such ways it revolves.
The virtuous person performs virtuous deeds, while the evil person creates evil karma.
The mind exercises mastery over the creation of karma, and through the mastery of karma, existence arises once more.
This mind arises from karma; thus is one deceived by craving.
One who performs evil deeds with an evil mind comes to this place;
if they are boiled in hell, that person has been deceived by craving.
It is not that one person commits evil while another receives the retribution for suffering;
one receives the fruit of one's own karma, and all sentient beings are thus.
What you have done with your own mind—all such things are deceptive.
"Now you are being burned by a great fire; for what reason do you groan and wail?
Thus the Yama-wardens rebuke the hell-beings, saying:

"You have created these actions yourself, and now you must experience them yourself; there is no escape. Bound by all such fruits of karma, you receive the retribution for all those actions here within this place."
In this manner, the Yama-wardens rebuke that hell-being.

For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years, the Yama-wardens thus burn and boil the hell-sinner; as long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its karmic potency has not been exhausted, they inflict suffering upon him without ceasing at all times.
Only when the evil karma is exhausted does he finally escape from that place of hell.

If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals; yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma,

one will constantly suffer from chronic ailments within the abdomen, or the body will be withered and emaciated, and the physical appearance will be hideous, or like that of a gatekeeper whose bodily form resembles a scorched forest—
this is the residual karmic retribution of accumulated actions.

Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell: what other places exist within it? Through seeing, hearing, and knowledge, he perceives another distinct place;
that place is named Sarvendriyaniruddha (The Extinction of All Faculties), and it is the eleventh location within the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and are born in the region of the Hell where All Faculties are Extinct.
The karmic actions and their results regarding killing and stealing have been explained as previously stated;
now, the practice of sexual misconduct is discussed, specifically when one takes pleasure in it and engages in it frequently.
If a person is driven by excessive desire, they may engage in sexual intercourse with a woman in her mouth or through the anus—places other than the female organ.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the "All-Sense-Roots-Extinction" section of the Saṃghāta Great Hell—where they undergo great suffering and affliction, namely:
having their mouths filled with fire, and being made to drink molten copper from hot iron bowls.
An iron fork is thrust into their mouths, beaten and poked until they are wide open, and molten copper is poured inside.

Furthermore, there are hot iron black insects there; their bodies are ablaze, and these eleven locations are all set on fire, forming a garland of flames that burns them within. Though they burn, they still live, being thus constantly scorched.

Hot, flaming iron ants gnaw at their eyes; hot molten tin is poured into their ears until they are full; flaming, sharp knives cut off their noses, and with sharp knives they next cut off their tongues; raining down hot, sharp knives, they burn and slice their bodies.

All their faculties experience great anguish and extreme suffering, receiving a retribution of displeasure; those hell-beings are without parallel and cannot be compared to anything else. Now, I shall describe a small portion of this: it is like using a lamp as a metaphor for the sun; likewise, the suffering experienced in that hell is such that there is no comparison.
The excellence of the pleasures in the heavens is beyond comparison; likewise, the suffering endured by those hell-beings in the hells is also beyond comparison. Why is this so?
The pleasures in the heavens are supreme, while the sufferings in the hells are heavy; such suffering and pleasure, I shall now describe in brief.

The torments endured in those hellish places are firm and exceedingly severe; as long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, one will experience uninterrupted suffering at all times.
Only when that evil karma is exhausted will one finally be liberated from those hellish places.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from long ago in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals,
but is instead born among humans in a place of similar karma, one’s wife will be unchaste and share herself with others; one will incite others to kill,
either by reporting them to officials or by framing them falsely to cause their execution.
Whether one kills by mixing poison into medicine,
or waits for the victim to sleep and kills with a blade or other means—

this is the residual fruit of the power of the evil karma they have accumulated; as long as the retribution for the power of that accumulated karma is not exhausted, there can be no escape, and it must inevitably be experienced.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Place of Suffering Without a Shore (Apratisthāna), which is the twelfth location within the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and are born in that place of suffering called "No Shore."
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing and stealing are as previously explained.
What is sexual misconduct?
It is as follows:
Suppose there is a person who gives rise to a mind of lustful desire; while thinking of his own wife, he commits adultery with another woman.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body breaks up at the end of life, they fall into an evil destination, the Saṃjīva Great Hell, being born in a place of suffering from which there is no shore beyond. There they undergo great torment, experiencing such suffering through the power of the accumulated karma as follows:

they suffer the pain of being burned by fire, the pain of being cut by knives, the pain of hot ashes, and the pain of various diseases. Thus, no further shore can be found, and there is no one to offer comfort.
As thus described, the various sufferings and afflictions they undergo are beyond analogy, just as it was said regarding their experience of suffering.
Those hell-beings, deceived by their own minds, undergo such suffering.

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they are constantly scorched and roasted, or boiled and beaten; as long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
Only when that evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, then one will be constantly impoverished, living in desolate and evil places or in perilous mountain regions as a slave to the indigenous tribes, and will always suffer from illness.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell to see what other places exist there.
He perceives through seeing and hearing that there is another distinct place named Padma, which is the thirteenth location within the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who have accumulated the acts of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, and thus fall into the Padma section of the Saṃghāta Hell.
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing and stealing are as previously described.
What is sexual misconduct?
It is as follows:

A śramaṇa knows for himself that when he was formerly in the secular world, he previously engaged in sexual desire with women and experienced its flavor; although he has become a bhikṣu, his mind still recalls it, and while lying down at night, he sees those women in a dream. Failing to correctly contemplate the unwholesomeness of the flavor of sexual desire, he immediately engages in sexual intercourse with them.

Once that person has awakened, their mind immediately becomes attached to unchaste conduct; they contemplate and recollect it with a heart of sympathetic joy, praise its merits to others, laugh with delight, and take pleasure in repeatedly performing various such acts of sensual enjoyment.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the *Padma* section of the Saṃjīva Great Hell—and undergo great suffering. As for what this suffering is:
the entire environment of that hell is the color of the *padma* lotus, resembling the hue of a *padma*; it is everywhere a pervasive crimson color, with red radiance.
The Yama-wardens seize the hell-beings and boil them in cauldrons, or place them in iron chests and pound them with iron pestles.
If they escape from that place, those people see lotus flowers (*padma*) in a clear pool from afar.

Having escaped from the two sufferings of the wooden boxes and the cauldrons, the denizens of hell, hoping for rescue and seeking refuge, run swiftly toward those lotus flowers in the clear pool, giving rise to this thought:
"I shall go there; I will surely find peace and happiness."

Those hell-beings, tormented by hunger and thirst, gaze longingly toward the *padma* lotus. Thus they run back and forth, perhaps a hundred times or a thousand times; on the path they traverse, there are many iron hooks that wound and break their feet.

Once their feet are broken, they lay their chests upon the ground, where the iron hooks of that place wound and break their chests; if they lie on their backs, the iron hooks pierce their backs; if they lie on their sides, the iron hooks pierce their flanks; and if they sit down, the iron hooks enter upward through them. Thus those people call out to one another, being burned and boiled, their bodies withered by hunger and thirst; they call out to one another, wailing and lamenting in anguish.
All these sinners gaze with one mind upon the padma; behind them stand the Yama-wardens, wielding great sharp swords, axes, or hammers, cutting, hacking, and beating them.
Those hell-beings, employing various means to seek rescue and a place of refuge, reach the *padma* tree;

having reached it, they climb up in hopes of finding coolness. That *padma* tree is like a *khadira*, filled with great fires and possessing leaves as hard as adamant; once the sinner has climbed up, the leaves curl back down like hooks.

Due to their evil karma, those people of evil deeds remain in the Padma section of the Saṃghāta Hell for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of years. Because of their evil karma, they are boiled there yet do not die; as long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or rotted away and its residual force has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
Only when that evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, in the distant past of former lives, there was maturation of wholesome karma, one will not be born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, that person will possess distorted vision—whether male or female—and will be without precepts, impoverished, and short-lived, all resulting from the power of accumulated karmic actions.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Mahāpadma, which is the fourteenth location within the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and are born in the Mahāpadma location.
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing and stealing are as previously explained.
What is sexual misconduct?
It is when one is not actually a śramaṇa yet claims to be a śramaṇa, while being deficient in the precepts.
Why is this? Although they practice the holy life (brahmacarya), they do not seek nirvāṇa.
Their practice is like the sound of a conch shell; it is a practice that laughs at nirvāṇa, thinking and saying thus:

"By this holy life of mine, may I be reborn among the gods; if I am reborn elsewhere, in a place similar to the heavens, may I be born in that heavenly world, amidst the assembly of celestial maidens."

"Such a śramaṇa and such a holy life (brahmacarya) are not the vow of the holy life; rather, they are a practice of craving, a practice that is the cause of birth and death, a practice conditioned by craving, and a practice of defilement."

By such a holy life, one does not attain liberation from these evils: sickness, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, weeping, beating the breast, striking the head, and the resulting grief, suffering, and despair.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, being born in the Great Earth Prison within the Mahāpadma Hell, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.

This includes a river named Kṣāravāhinī (Ash-Wave), five yojanas wide and one hundred yojanas long, which flows constantly without ceasing; there is not even a space the size of a needle’s eye that is not completely filled with ash.

Those hell-beings in that river undergo the most intense and agonizing suffering. Once they fall into that river, their bodies disintegrate; their bones become stones, their hair becomes aquatic moss, and their flesh becomes mud. The water in the river is molten white tin. The bodies of the hell-beings, having been scattered, reassemble and become fish within the river, drifting along its current.
Having drifted, they are cooked. On both the right and left banks, there are crows with flaming beaks that devour them. If they hope for rescue and flee from that river, [they are pursued].
The Yama-wardens, using iron tongs blazing with flames, cast them into the river. When they wish to emerge, their feet become scorched and cooked;

the sinews are cooked, the thighs are cooked, the calves are cooked, and the hips are cooked. The hip-bones are cooked, the skin of the hips is cooked, and the flesh of the hips is cooked. The flesh of the back falls away as the flesh of the back is cooked; the flesh of the head falls away as the flesh of the head is cooked; the skull falls away as the skull is cooked, and finally the cranium falls away as the cranium is cooked.

In that river, those hell-beings are thus scorched, boiled, and roasted in this manner for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years; only after enduring such extreme agony in that evil river do those hell-beings finally obtain release.

Although they have escaped that place, they again see a clear pond with full-blown *padma* lotuses; seeking rescue, seeking refuge, and desiring peace and happiness, those hell-beings run toward that *padma* grove.

Those iron lotuses have a touch like a sharp blade; when the bodies of those hell-beings touch them, the iron lotuses slice, cut, hack, and chop them, shattering their bodies until they fall away bit by bit.

The *Yama* demons inflict much suffering upon them, forcing them to climb quickly onto the lotus grove. That lotus grove is filled with blazing fire, and its flowers have iron petals. Once the sinner has climbed up, the petals close together; the hell-being remains within the petals, scorched by the blazing fire. Thus it continues for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years due to their evil karma.
There are crows therein that devour their eyes, pull out their tongue-roots, cut off their ears, and dismember their bodies;
such crows are the fruit of their own karma.

Those hell-beings in that Mahāpadma hell are constantly burned and boiled; until their accumulated evil and unwholesome karma is destroyed and decomposed, and its residual force is exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish place.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, then one suffers from illness, is constantly hungry and thirsty, and is frequently prone to anger—this is the residual karmic retribution of that former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Fire Pit (Agnikuṇḍa), which is the fifteenth location within the Saṃghāta Hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in and frequently practicing these deeds; they fall into the Saṃghāta Hell and are born in the Fire Basin location.
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing and stealing are as previously described.
What is misconduct?
It is when one is not truly a śramaṇa, yet claims to be a śramaṇa.
Having become a śramaṇa, when he recollects his former life as a layman in white robes, he recalls associating with women, indulging in laughter, dancing, and play.
Such a person, failing to observe correctly, recollects those pleasures and gives rise to conceptual discrimination, repeatedly thinking and discriminating in this way:

it is not a wholesome reflection; it is not a reflection on realizing the Dharma through right mindfulness; it is not a reflection on the noble truth of the cessation of the accumulation of suffering; it is not the reflection of one in training—failing to cultivate or practice the reflection of one in training; it is not the reflection of right mindfulness that tames the mind; it is not the reflection on the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha; it is not the reflection on the mark of death; it is not the reflection on detachment from birth and death; and it is not the reflection that views even a tiny speck of fault with fear.

One should not take an excessive amount of bedding, medicine, food and drink for the sick, or requisites and their causes; yet such a person takes an excessive amount of bedding, medicine, food and drink according to the illness, and requisites and their causes.

Because that person thus took excessive amounts of bedding, medicinal requisites for illness, food, drink, and other necessities, by reason of those evil karmic causes and conditions, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they fall into an evil destination—the Saṃghāta Great Hell—being born in the Fire Basin region and undergoing great suffering. As for what that suffering is:

that fire basin region is filled everywhere with hot flames; there is not even a space the size of a hair’s tip that is not pervaded by flame and heat. In that hell region, the bodies of the hell-beings resemble lamp-trees, and the hot flames of those lamps merge into a single mass of flame.
Those hell-beings groan, shriek, and wail; as they shriek and wail, their mouths gape open, and hot flames fill their mouths.
Those hell-beings undergo extreme great suffering, repeatedly crying out, groaning, and weeping, as the flames enter their ears;
because they have entered the ears, they further groan, cry out, and shriek, and the flames again enter their eyes.
Once it has entered the eye, they further groan, wail, and shriek aloud.
As their entire bodies are thus engulfed in flames, the glowing-hot iron garments further burn their tongues.
Having already broken the precepts, they consume the food and drink of others, and thus their tongues are scorched;
because they violated the prohibitive precepts and failed to observe with propriety, looking upon the wives of others, their eyes are scorched;
because they did not guard the precepts, singing, laughing, and calling out with other women, and listened to their voices with a mind stained by lust, molten white tin fills their ears.
Because he violated the prohibitions and took the incense of the Saṃgha to perfume himself, his nose was cut off and burned with fire.

Thus, that person, having violated the precepts through these five faculties, falls into hell; experiencing the retribution of suffering that accords with his original karma due to his practice of evil deeds.

In that hell, for such immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they are constantly burned and boiled; there are many garlands of flames everywhere throughout the Saṃghāta Hell, which is named the Fire Basin Place.
As long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its karmic force has not been exhausted, suffering will continue without ceasing at all times;
only when that evil karma is exhausted will one finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one obtains the body of a dwarf, is blind and deaf, is impoverished and short-lived, and constantly suffers from hunger and thirst—this is the residual karmic retribution of that former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the Saṃghāta Hell to see what other locations exist there.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is another distinct location called the Iron Dust Fire Place (Loha-cūrṇa-agni-sthāna), which is the sixteenth location within the Saṃghāta Hell.
What karma causes sentient beings to be born in that place?
He perceives through seeing, hearing, and knowledge:
if a person habitually commits and frequently engages in killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, they will fall into the Iron Dust Fire region of the Saṃghāta Hell.
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing and stealing are as previously described.
What is sexual misconduct?
It is as follows:

There are those who are not truly śramaṇas, yet claim to be śramaṇas; if they hear the sounds of women singing, dancing, laughing, playing, or wearing ornaments, and having heard these sounds, fail to examine them wisely, their minds give rise to lustful attachment. Hearing those sounds of song, laughter, dance, and play, they discharge impurity, and their minds become suitably addicted to the flavor of them.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body disintegrates and life ends, they fall into an evil realm—the Iron Dust Fire Section of the Saṃhāta Great Hell—where they undergo great suffering and affliction. That is to say:

there is the Hot Iron Four-Cornered Hell, with iron walls five hundred *yojanas* in circumference, where iron fires constantly blaze without ceasing, burning the hell-beings. Created by their own karma, fire rains down from above without ever pausing; likewise iron falls, and likewise fire rains down.
Because of the rain of iron, all the limbs and bodies of those hell-beings are pulverized;
because of the rain of fire, they are constantly boiled and constantly burned;
thus they perpetually undergo the suffering of these two kinds of rains.
Those hell-beings suffer in this manner; indeed, only those in hell undergo such suffering, for there is nothing else by which it can be compared.
The torment they endure is so solid, intense, and cruel that all such evil suffering is feared, neither desired nor enjoyed, being produced solely by their own karma.
Thus they undergo suffering until the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has been destroyed and decomposed, and its force has been exhausted; at all times, their suffering does not cease.
Only when that evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of common karma—such as a location on a great river where people cross—one will constantly experience fear, or suffer from chronic illness, or be like an elephant and other such creatures that, despite having miserable lives, are always terrified of death: these are the residual karmic fruits of that former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu observes each of these individual locations within the Great Universal Hell; there are exactly sixteen such places, and he sees no seventeenth location beyond them.
Together with the sixteen sub-locations of the Great Hell, these are always filled with vast multitudes; thus he observes the reality of the retribution for karmic actions.
That bhikṣu, observing in this way the various evil karmas and their sovereign fruits of retribution for those sentient beings, becomes weary of and seeks detachment from birth and death.

Furthermore, the practitioner reflects within the mind—contemplating the course of phenomena in accordance with the True Dharma—and having thus observed them with discernment, that bhikṣu penetrates the fruits of karma; he thus knows with precision the three great hells, along with their various locations and the retributive results of karma.
Having observed and understood this, he attains penetration through focal objects and takes no pleasure in dwelling within the realm of Māra in the midst of existence.

When the earth-dwelling yakṣas see that bhikṣu practicing such diligence, they immediately report it upward to the space-dwelling yakṣas; the space-dwelling yakṣas report it to the Four Great Kings, as previously described, in succession up to the Heaven of Immeasurable Light, until it is said:

"In Jambudvīpa, in such-and-such a country and such-and-such a village, one has thus successively shaved off hair and beard, donned the dharma robes, and gone forth with right faith; that bhikṣu has thus attained even to the ninth stage."
Upon hearing this, the gods of the Immeasurable Light Heaven were filled with joy and said to one another:
"O gods, you should know!
The faction of Māra is diminishing, while the assembly of the True Dharma is increasing."
"Furthermore, after that bhikṣu has thus observed the three hells, he next observes the fourth great hell, Raurava.
By what karma are sentient beings born therein?"
He sees, hears, and knows:

namely, that there are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, and drink intoxicants, delighting in such practices and performing them frequently; having fully perfected these four types of karma through repeated accumulation, at the dissolution of the body after death, they are born in this Great Hell of Screaming.

The acts of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, along with their karmic retributions, have been explained as previously stated; now it shall be explained that if one habitually indulges in and frequently commits the act of drinking alcohol, one will be reborn in the Great Hell of Screaming.

If a person gives alcohol to an assembly of monks, or to those who observe the precepts—whether they be ordained bhikṣus, those who dwell in tranquility, those whose minds are extinguished, or those who delight in meditative concentration—their minds will become turbid and disturbed because of that alcohol.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Great Hell of Screaming—where, amidst intense heat, they undergo great suffering and affliction.
What kind of suffering do they undergo?
It is said:
with iron tongs, their mouths are forcibly pried open, and molten red copper liquid is poured into their mouths to be drunk; first, it burns their lips.
Once the lips have been burned, the teeth are burned next;
once the teeth have been burned, the tongue is burned next;
once the tongue has been burned, the throat is burned next.
Thus it burns the throat, and next it burns the stomach; in this sequence, it burns the small intestines;
having burned the small intestines, it further burns the large intestines, and likewise the stomach (āmāśaya), followed by the receptacle for digested food (pakvāśaya);
having burned the receptacle for digested food, it exits from below.
Thus, due to the unwholesome karmic action of drinking alcohol, that person receives such a retribution: they wail, shriek, lament, and weep aloud.
After that person has thus cried out and roared, the Yama-wardens rebuke them and speak these verses:
"Having committed unwholesome karma, You now experience the fruit of suffering."
What was done out of a deluded mind will later result in being burned and boiled;
such unwholesome karma was committed with an evil heart.
Now that you must undergo the consequences, do not groan; what is the use of lamenting?
If a person commits evil deeds, they will all receive their retribution in the form of suffering.
If one desires personal happiness, one should not associate with evil in this way.
Even if one commits but a small evil deed, one will suffer greatly in hell.
Because the mind of delusion holds sway, one continues to commit evil even after having attained liberation.
One must not trust in evil karma, for it leads people to hell;
just as a small spark can burn down mountains and all the forests and trees.
The deluded person conceives thoughts of evil and takes no delight in the wholesome Dharma;
seeing that the retribution for unwholesome conduct arises entirely from causes and conditions,
why do they not take pleasure in the Dharma?
Why does one not abandon evil?
If a person is free from evil karma, they will not see hell;
yet if a person’s own mind is deluded, they do not know the fruit of evil karma.
That person received this evil, and you now receive it likewise.
Evil karma leads to birth in hell; one is scorched by evil karma.
Evil does not lead to Nirvana; no enemy exceeds evil karma.
Deceived by one's own past evil karma, one is now consumed by that very same karma;
had one not committed evil deeds, one would never have suffered such affliction.
If a person can restrain craving, this path is supremely tranquil.
One who thus abandons attachment to people dwells near Nirvāṇa.
Having already committed evil karma and never having practiced virtue, one is thus scorched by that evil karma; therefore, let the mind not engage in evil karma.
One who commits evil deeds finds no place of peace and happiness;
if one desires personal joy, one should delight in the Dharma.
If a person delights in evil, they will suffer the most bitter of sufferings.
If one cannot endure suffering, one should not commit evil deeds.
It is easy for the virtuous to perform good; it is difficult for the wicked to perform good.
It is easy for the wicked to commit evil; it is difficult for the virtuous to commit evil.
“After the *yama-rākṣasa*s in that hell have thus rebuked the hell-beings, they inflict various kinds of suffering, namely:

two mountains. These mountains are extremely solid and ablaze with iron flames; as they both exert force and come together at once, they crush the hell-beings. Having crushed them, they grind them until their bodies are completely scattered and nothing remains to be seen.
Once thus ground, they are born again, and the two mountains crush and grind them as before. In this manner, after being born, they are crushed again; after being born, they are ground again.”

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, as long as their evil karma is not exhausted, once they have escaped that hellish place, they flee toward other regions, seeking rescue and seeking refuge, longing for liberation.

The Yama-wardens then seize him again, placing him head-downward into an iron cauldron. Thus, with his head and face downward in the iron cauldron, he is boiled by the fire of boiling water for hundreds of thousands of years; yet, even after this, his evil karma is still not exhausted.
Once he has escaped from that place of boiling cauldrons, he runs toward another location, seeking rescue, seeking refuge, and desiring peace and happiness.

Before that person stands a great iron crow, its body ablaze with flames; it seizes his body, tearing and rending it apart, dividing it into hundreds and thousands of parts—vein by vein and joint by joint—and devours him as he is thus scattered piece by piece. This continues for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, yet his evil karma remains undiminished.

Once they have escaped from that place of iron crows, seeking rescue and seeking refuge, they run toward another location; tormented by hunger and thirst, they see clear water in the distance, such as a pond or a pool, and hasten toward it.
In that place, there are only pools filled with molten white tin. Desiring to bathe, they immediately enter them;

once they have entered, due to their evil karma, a great tortoise seizes them and submerges them, boiling them in the molten white tin until they are thoroughly cooked. This continues for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, until their unwholesome and evil karma is exhausted and their vital energy is spent; only then does the great tortoise release them.

Once they have gained release from that, those people, tormented by suffering and seeking rescue and refuge, run toward another place. Before them appear the henchmen of Yama, holding iron spikes; these spikes are ablaze with flames, and with such spikes they pierce their heads. They pass straight through, some being pierced so that they emerge from the back, some being pierced so they emerge from the ribs, and some being pierced so they emerge from the head. Those hell-beings undergo great agony, crying out and wailing. Because of the power of their own past karma, the other hell-beings hear this wailing and mistake it for the sound of singing; they all run toward it together, seeking rescue and refuge.
The Yama-wardens then seize them once more, piercing, cutting, and hacking them with iron hammers, swords, and axes that are all ablaze.

Thus they remain for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, until the accumulated evil karma is exhausted, their strength is spent, and they are completely decomposed; only then do they escape from that hellish realm.

Seeking rescue and seeking refuge, he ran toward another place. Seeing a village in the distance with complete dwellings and many rivers and ponds, he proceeded directly with focused intent, running swiftly to reach it, wishing to enter that village;
yet that entire village was ablaze, filled everywhere with black insects having diamond-like mouths and sharp fangs, their bodies all burning with fire.
Once they have entered the village, the gates are immediately closed; those hell-beings are then devoured by black insects with adamantine mouths and sharp fangs.

Thus they remain for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, until their accumulated evil karma is exhausted, their vitality is spent, and they are utterly decomposed, at which point they emerge from this great ocean of suffering.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from long ago in past lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, the mind will suddenly forget [one's former merit], becoming poor and destitute of possessions, constantly dwelling in streets and crossroads selling base and foul goods to earn a living and seek profit.

They act as if they were children, feigning laughter and play; their teeth and mouths are foul, and their feet are cracked and split. They are constantly tormented by hunger and thirst, and have no wife, no father, no mother, and no brothers or sisters. This is the remaining karmic retribution for the evil deeds of drinking alcohol and giving it to others.

One who observes such precepts yet commits the karmic offense of giving alcohol shall fall into this Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava) to undergo the retribution of suffering; one should understand it thus.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, further examines the Great Hell of Screaming: what other distinct regions does it contain?
He perceives through seeing, hearing,
and knowledge that within the Raurava Hell there is a distinct location called Mahāraurava.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, and take intoxicants, practicing and frequently committing these acts; they fall into that hell and are born in the Place of Great Roaring.
The actions of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, along with their karmic retributions, are as previously described.
What is the drinking of intoxicants?
It is as follows:

If one gives alcohol to those observing the *upavāsa* fast or to those who are pure, that person, by reason of these causes and conditions of evil karma, will, at the dissolution of the body after death, fall into an evil destination—the Great Roaring Hell—and be born in the place of Great Shrieking, where they undergo great suffering and affliction. As for what this suffering is:

first, molten white tin is placed in their mouth; because of the evil karma of having previously given alcohol to those observing the fast or to those who are pure, it is poured from a flaming iron bowl into their mouth. Tormented by great agony, they let out a loud, roaring cry.
Such was the sound of their roaring; it was not so in the other hells.
Those sinners, giving rise to great suffering and grief, cried out and wailed, the great sound of their roaring filling all of space.
The Yama-wardens are wrathful by their very nature; yet, due to the power of the karmic offenses of those hell-beings, when the wardens hear their roaring cries, they become even more enraged.
Those who drink alcohol do not guard against various evils; they feel no shame or remorse for any unwholesome act.

To give someone alcohol is to bestow upon them all manner of unwholesomeness; because of drinking alcohol, the mind is neither focused nor upright, and one fails to protect wholesome dharmas, resulting in mental confusion.
Such a person with a confused mind does not distinguish between good and evil, and feels no shame or remorse for any unwholesome deed.
If a person gives alcohol, they provide the cause; because there is this cause, one is able to commit unwholesome deeds.
Just as a similar cause yields a similar fruit, by these causes and conditions, one will undergo great suffering for a long time—various afflictions and immeasurable sufferings.
Why is it called the Hell of Great Roars?
Because the beings there undergo immeasurable and manifold sufferings and utter great roars; for this reason, it is named the Hell of Great Roars.
When sentient beings in such places have thus had their unwholesome and evil karma destroyed, rendered breathless and utterly decomposed, they may finally escape from those hellish realms.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will be dull-witted and lack mental acuity, being prone to forgetfulness and unable to recall things for even a short time.

Such a person, dull-witted and ignorant, possesses no wealth and is neither respected nor loved by others; being destitute and lacking possessions, they cannot acquire wealth even when seeking it. Should they contract even a slight illness, they immediately meet their end; this is the residual karmic retribution of their evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again observes the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava) to see what other places exist there.
