He sees that this Hell of Screaming has sixteen locations. What are these sixteen?
First is named Great Roar;
second is named Universal Sound;
third is named Flowing Fire from the Hair.
The fourth are named fire-fragment insects;
the fifth are named hot iron fire-mallets;
the sixth are named rain of flaming fire-stones.
The seventh is named Killing the Killer;
the eighth is named the Iron Forest Wilderness;
the ninth is named Universal Darkness.
The tenth is named Yamalocaka-āṭavī (The Wilderness of Yama’s Obstruction);
the eleventh is named Sword Forest;
the twelfth is named Great Sword Forest.
Thirteen is named the Forest of Plantain Smoke;
fourteen is named the Forest with Smoke and Fire;
fifteen is named the Fire Cloud Mist.
The sixteenth is named Vibhaṅga-duḥkha (Differentiated Suffering).
These sixteen locations are the various sub-regions of the Raurava Hell.
By what karmic retribution do sentient beings take birth in those places?
Having thus observed the Great Roaring region of the Raurava Hell, that bhikṣu next observes the second, named the Universal Sound region. He sees:

there are people who habitually engage in and frequently commit killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and the drinking of intoxicants; such persons fall into the Raurava Hell and are born in the Universal Sound region.
The actions and karmic results of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct are as previously described.
What is the consumption of intoxicants?
It is when a person takes pleasure in drinking alcohol and does so frequently, or gives alcohol to others who have newly received the precepts and causes them to drink it.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body disintegrates and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, being born in the Universal Sound section of the Howling Hell, where they undergo great suffering. This is known as the "Pounding with Mortars":

those hell-beings let out cries and roars, and their voices pervade that hellish region, as well as the Iron Ring Mountains, all the rivers, the four continents, Jambudvīpa, and so forth. For those situated there, the sound of their roars emerges and consumes everything; the sound of that person’s weeping, lamenting, and crying out accords with their own past actions.

Those hell-beings thus shriek and cry out; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they are subjected to unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in previous lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will be born in a wilderness land with little water.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava) to see what other places exist there.

He perceives through hearing and knowledge that within the Great Hell of Screaming there is another distinct location called Flowing Fire from Hair (Keśāgnisravā), which is the third separate sub-region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who habitually engage in and frequently commit the acts of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking intoxicants; such persons fall into the Hair-Fire-Flowing section of the Raurava Hell.
The acts of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, along with their karmic results, are as previously described.
What is the drinking of alcohol?
It refers to speaking of the merits of alcohol to those who observe the five precepts of a lay follower (*upāsaka*), saying such things as:
"Is alcohol also a precept? [Thinking thus, they] cause him to drink alcohol.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when his body breaks up and his life ends, he falls into an evil place—the Hell of Wailing, in the Section of Flowing Hair-Fire—where he undergoes great suffering. That is to say, there is a rain of fire; those hell-beings are constantly burned and boiled, their hair set ablaze, and even down to their feet, hot iron dogs devour their feet. Flaming-beaked iron vultures split open their skulls to drink their brains, while hot iron jackals eat within their bodies. Thus they are constantly burned and thus they are constantly devoured.
"Having committed unwholesome and evil karma for himself, that person wails in grief and pain, speaking verses of lamentation and addressing the messengers of Yama, saying:
'Why do you have no heart of compassion?'"
"Why is it that you are not at peace?
I am a vessel for compassion; why do you have no compassion for me?
The Yama-wardens replied to the sinner:
"Covered by delusion, you committed many evil deeds yourself;
now you undergo this most grievous suffering—it was not I who created this cause."
The deluded person does not study the precepts, And thus accumulates much evil karma;
Having accumulated much evil karma, They now receive such a fruit as this.
This is what you yourself have done; It is not due to my causes or conditions.
If a person commits evil deeds, those deeds are the cause.
Having been deceived by the snare of craving, they perform evil and unwholesome actions;
now that they receive the retribution for those evil deeds, why do you harbor anger and resentment toward me?
One does not suffer the consequences of what one has not done; it is not said that evil has no cause.
If a person intentionally commits evil, that person shall receive its fruit for themselves.
Do not take pleasure in drinking alcohol; alcohol is the most poisonous of poisons.
One who constantly delights in drinking alcohol is able to destroy wholesome dharmas.
If one always takes pleasure in drinking alcohol, that person lacks right intention;
when the mind is disturbed, the Dharma cannot be attained. Therefore, one should always renounce alcohol.
"Alcohol is a loss that causes further loss; this is what the wise have said.
Thus, do not take pleasure in alcohol, for it ruins oneself and ruins others.
One who constantly delights in drinking alcohol will obtain unlovely and evil states."
Thus it may be called "evil," and for this reason one should abandon drinking alcohol.
When wealth is exhausted, one is despised among men; it is the foremost root of indolence.
Since there are faults in drinking alcohol, one should thus abandon liquor.
"Alcohol can inflame desire; the mind of hatred is likewise so.
Delusion also increases because of alcohol; therefore, one should abandon alcohol.

Thus, in this place of flowing fire from hair in hell, which is obtained by the hell-beings through their own karma, they remain until the accumulated evil karma is exhausted, destroyed, and they have become breathless and utterly decayed; only then do they escape that hellish place.
If, in the distant past of previous lives, there was maturation of wholesome karma, one will not be born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, that person will be born in a land where there is no wine, and all provisions lack color and flavor, such that they do not know color or taste—this is the residual fruit of retribution for former evil karma.
*Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna Sūtra*, Scroll Seven;
*Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna Sūtra*, Scroll Eight.
Translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Chapter on the Hells, Part Four:
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the great hell of Raurava to see what other places exist there.
He perceives, hears, and knows:
Furthermore, there is another place called the Fire-Dust Worms; this is the fourth distinct location within that hell.
By what karma do sentient beings are born in that place?
There they see:

If there are those who kill, steal, or engage in sexual misconduct, practicing these acts with delight and frequency, they will fall into the Fire-Dust Worms (Vālukā) section of the Raurava Hell; their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, regarding those who sell liquor by adding water and other substances while charging the price for pure alcohol—selling liquor in such a manner constitutes the transgression of theft.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Hell of Wailing, in the place of the Fire-End Worms—where they undergo great suffering and affliction. The so-called sufferings are these:
the four hundred and four diseases.
What are called the four hundred and four illnesses?
There are one hundred and one wind-illnesses, one hundred and one bile-illnesses, one hundred and one phlegm-illnesses, and one hundred and one miscellaneous illnesses.
Those hell-beings experience results that correspond to their causes.
Whether in Jambudvīpa, Uttarakuru, Aparagoyānī, or Pūrvavideha—in these four regions—by the power of a single person’s illness, they could all be made to die within a single day and night.
In that hellish realm, there are these four hundred and four diseases, and furthermore, there are other various afflictions. As for what constitutes suffering:

worms are born upon the bodies of those hell-beings; they break through their skin, flesh, fat, blood, marrow, and bones to feed upon them. Experiencing such suffering, they cry out with loud shrieks, solitary and without rescue.

Furthermore, they give rise to extreme fear toward those Yama-wardens; they are scorched and boiled by great fires, their bodies ablaze as they undergo various sufferings until the evil karma they have accumulated is exhausted, their vital breath ceases, and they are completely decomposed, only then attaining liberation from that hellish realm.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a former life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, suffering from poverty and affliction, this is the residual retribution for the evil karma of selling alcohol in a previous life.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again observes the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava): what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Hot Iron Fire Hammer, which is the fifth secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; such persons fall into the Hell of Screaming and are born in a distinct region of the Hot Iron Hammer.
Karma and its retribution have been explained as previously stated.
Now, furthermore, regarding alcohol:

if a person deceives animals—such as lions, tigers, bears, starlings, or jīvañjīvaka birds—with alcohol, causing them to become intoxicated so that they lose their strength and are unable to escape, and then seizes them, whether he kills them or not.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the separate location within the Raurava Hell known as the Hot Iron Hammer—and there they undergo great suffering and affliction.

The blazing iron pestles are produced by their own evil karma; they strike them until they are crushed into fragments like sand, and all their limbs are utterly shattered and destroyed. They undergo great suffering, wailing and crying out as they run toward one another;
as they run thus, the blazing iron pestles strike and crush them from behind, causing them to experience universal suffering.
The Yama-wardens further seize them and, with sharp iron knives, pare their bodies; having pared them, they cut them; having cut them, they hack them; and having hacked them, they split them asunder.
As long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its karmic force has not been exhausted, suffering will continue without ceasing at all times;
only when that evil karma is exhausted will one finally escape from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma and contracts a disease of wind and blood, this is the residual fruit of that evil karma.

Being born in a wretched land where there are no physicians, medicines, or attendants to care for the sick, and being impoverished and distressed, and further being born in an evil country abounding in various kinds of weeds, thorns, and brambles, in a place of great heat and little water, constantly harboring fear—this is the remaining power of that evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava) to see what other places exist there.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is another distinct place called Rain of Blazing Fire-Stones; this is the sixth secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; those people fall into the Howling Hell and are born in a distinct location called Rain of Blazing Fire Stones. Their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, if a person thinks to themselves:
"When an elephant is intoxicated, it can kill many people; if it kills many, I shall be victorious," they will give the elephant wine to drink in order to incite the fight.
Due to the retribution of this karma, they fall into an evil place—the separate region of the *Raurava* (Screaming) Hell where flaming stones rain down—and there they undergo great suffering.

As for that suffering: by the power of their sinful karma, great elephants arise within that hell whose bodies are entirely ablaze; with all their limbs, they strike and touch [the beings]. Having seized those people, they crush and break all their limbs until they fall apart, inflicting great terror. Thus the person cries out and screams loudly, their limbs completely shattered.
Once they have been released from that, they are again seized by the *yama-puruṣas* and placed in cauldrons filled with boiling, molten copper.

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they are constantly burned and boiled; their bodies are decomposed and destroyed until their evil karma is neither diminished nor exhausted, and the force of that karma has not run its course. At all times, their suffering does not cease;
only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

and if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, that person will be born into a family of elephant-killers and be killed by elephants. They will be constantly afflicted by poverty, their complexion will be unsightly, their hands and feet will be rough and stiff, and their body will always have a coarse touch—this is the residual fruit of retribution for that evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the great hell of Raurava to see what other places exist there.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is another distinct place called the Place of Slaughter (Vadha-vadha-sthāna), which is the seventh secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are people who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, practicing and frequently performing these acts; such persons fall into the Raurava Hell and are born in the Place of Slaughter, where the karma and its retribution are as previously described.

Furthermore, if a person gives alcohol to another woman who is chaste and virtuous, causing her to become intoxicated so that her mind is disordered and improper, and she no longer maintains celibacy, and then engages in sexual misconduct with her.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Raurava Hell—and are born in the place called Sūcīvaśa, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:

red-hot flaming iron hooks pull out their male organs; once pulled out, they grow back again, and having grown back, they are pulled out once more. As they grow back tender and soft, they are pulled out yet again, undergoing extreme great suffering and crying out in wailing screams.

When that person of evil karma escapes from such a place and runs toward another location, as he runs, he sees before him a precipitous cliff. Upon that cliff, there are crows, vultures, jackals, owls, and eagles, their bodies made entirely of iron with mouths and claws of blazing fire, scattered everywhere across the precipice.

Having seen this, those hell-beings give rise to great terror; with contorted faces and distorted mouths, they look for rescue and a refuge. Falling onto the edge of a precipice, they are torn limb from limb and devoured by crows, vultures, jackals, owls, and eagles, whose beaks and claws are ablaze and whose bodies are made of iron; once they have been eaten, they are born again.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.

If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals, yet follows the sequence previously described—being bound by royal law, having an unwholesome complexion, an ugly countenance, and dying in prison—this is the residual fruit and retribution of that former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again observes the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava): what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Iron Forest Wilderness (Ayas-tāla-kāntāra), which is the eighth secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who commit killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, delighting in and frequently practicing them; such persons fall into the Iron Forest Wilderness of the Raurava Hell, where the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, if someone mixes poison with wine and gives it to an enemy to drink,

that person, by reason of this evil karmic cause, will at the dissolution of the body after death fall into an extremely terrible place— the Iron Forest Wilderness of the Raurava Hell— where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
That is to say:
an iron wheel with blazing heat spins rapidly; the Yama-wardens bind the hell-beings with hot iron cords as they are whirled swiftly and violently upon that iron wheel.
The Yama-wardens shoot their bodies with hot iron arrows until not a single spot remains intact, even as small as a mustard seed;
yet, due to the power of their sinful karma, they do not die.

When the causal conditions for that iron wheel are exhausted, he flees to another place; yet, by the power of his sinful karma, he is again seized by iron snakes and devoured for hundreds of thousands of years.
As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they will experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when that evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in previous lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one is born into a family that catches snakes and takes pleasure in seizing them by the head—then, through the residual force of that evil karma, one will be bitten by a snake and die. This is the residual fruit of that evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the great hell of Raurava to see what other places exist there.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is another distinct place called Universal Darkness Fire (Samantatamondhakāra), which is the ninth secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who engage in and frequently practice killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct; such persons fall into the Universal Darkness Fire region of the Raurava Hell, where the karma and its retribution are as previously described.

Furthermore, if there is a person who sells liquor for a livelihood, and a buyer of liquor does not know its price, that seller of liquor sells a small amount of liquor at a high price and takes many goods.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Hell of Universal Darkness and Fire within the Howling Hell—where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:

within the hell of the Universal Darkness Fire, the *yama-rākṣasas* do not recognize or know who these beings are, yet they beat them in the dark; those hell-beings undergo great agony, not knowing who is beating them.
They enter into the Dark Fire, a fire that possesses not even the slightest glimmer of light, as small as a hair-tip; within that fire, those hell-beings are scorched, boiled, and utterly destroyed.
Furthermore, there are iron saws that split their bodies apart, starting from the head and tearing them into two halves.

The sinners suffer in agony, crying out with loud wails; as long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its force has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish place.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will constantly suffer the affliction of hunger and thirst, lack wealth and possessions, be born in a cramped and narrow place, or be born in a place of constant scarcity where one resembles those who are not of the true human race—this is the residual fruit and retribution of that evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again observes the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava): what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Yama-lañcaka-araṇya (The Wilderness of Yama’s Snare), which is the tenth secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, practicing and performing these acts with delight; such persons fall into the Raurava Hell and are born in the Yama-raja-cāyaka wilderness, where their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Now, alcohol is further discussed:

if a person forcibly gives alcohol to a sick person or a woman who has recently given birth—whether for the sake of wealth, or for the sake of clothing, food, drink, and so forth—and thus gives such alcohol, whether it be for the purpose of taking wealth, or taking clothing, or food and drink, and so forth.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Raurava Hell—and are born in the Yama-raja-chedaka-vana (the Wilderness of Yama’s Chopping), where they undergo great suffering and distress.
What is called suffering is as follows:
from the toenails burning up to the head burning;
the Yama-wardens, with flaming iron blades, hack or pierce from the feet to the head; having thus hacked and pierced them, they further inflict extreme torment with flaming, sharp iron spears.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they are constantly burned, cut, split, and beaten at all times; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the force of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish place.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, that person will be born in an evil country, an evil location, or a remote borderland, as a low-born person who raises pigs—such a birth is the residual karmic fruit of that former evil deed.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again contemplates the great hell of Raurava: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Sword Forest (Asipatravana), which is the eleventh location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who habitually engage in and frequently commit killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct; such persons fall into the Raurava Hell and are born in the Sword Forest (Asipatravana) section, where the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Now, wine is further discussed:
Suppose a person deceives others with wine, saying to those wishing to travel through a wilderness, "This is the finest *asava* wine; it will not cause one to become intoxicated."

He gave them bad wine; they took the wine and, having entered a desolate and perilous wilderness, drank it. Having drunk it, they became utterly intoxicated and lost all awareness. Thus, all the wealth and treasures belonging to those intoxicated men were taken by the thieves, or even their lives were snatched away.
The flavor of *āsava* liquor is like that of curd-milk, like fine water, or like horse-curd; it is prepared by blending excellent and wondrous medicinal herbs.
When a person does not give this, but instead gives foul wine to cause intoxication, those who provide such wine are spoken of by the people of the world as follows:
Like a thief seized by the throat, this is the most wicked of thieves.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body breaks up and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Raurava Hell—and are born in the Sword Forest (Asipatravana) section, where they experience great suffering as a result of the karma they have committed and accumulated.
As for what is called suffering:
there are many dense showers of flaming stones that burn the entire body; thus being hacked and split, one falls to the ground and spits out the tongue.
In that place there is a river named the River of Boiling Heat, filled with molten blood and water, which constantly engenders terror.
That river boils with heat, and within it are mixed molten copper and molten white tin; thus they are constantly burned and boiled for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years.

The Yama-wardens, using flaming swords and shackles, either hack or strike them; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they are subjected to unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that hellish place.
If, due to the ripening of virtuous karma from a long time past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, that person will be black in color no different from ink, prone to anger and jealousy, stingy by nature, and constantly poor—this is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again observes the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava): what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Great Forest of Swords (Mahā-Asipatravana), which is the twelfth location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, and engage in sexual misconduct, practicing and frequently committing these acts; such persons fall into the Great Sword Forest within the Raurava Hell, where the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Now, regarding the discussion of alcohol:
suppose there is a wilderness where no people dwell, and there is only a road frequented by many travelers, upon which someone sells alcohol for profit.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Great Sword Forest within the Howling Hell—where they undergo great suffering and distress.
That is to say:

there are many great and formidable sword-trees one yojana in height, with extremely sharp blade-leaves, trunks ablaze with fire, and emitting intense, poisonous smoke; these are produced by the evil karma of [giving] alcohol in a previous life.
If one has not yet reached the trees even after traveling a single yojana, one’s body is already completely rotted, yet one does not die.

In this manner and that, one approaches the Great Forest of Swords; that forest is three thousand yojanas in circumference, filled with hundreds of thousands of layers of fire, smoke, poison, and blades, where one undergoes great suffering and torment, yet still does not die.

When the hell-beings reach the Great Forest of Swords, the *yama* wardens strike and kick them so that they must enter. Beneath the trees, swords rain down everywhere, shattering all their limbs, all their sinews, all their joints, and all their marrow, dispersing them into fragments.
Furthermore, there are blades and hammers; the hands of the Yama-rogues grasp these blades and hammers as they surround the forest of swords.
When the sinners emerge, they see them and immediately retreat back inside.
Within that great forest of iron sword-trees, when the sinners see the Yama-rogues, they give rise to extreme terror; some hide behind the trees, some climb the trees, and some are seized.
Once they have been captured, they are hacked and cut with knives. Those whose heads are split open experience this as the karmic retribution for their past evil deed of giving alcohol.
If they hide behind trees, iron vultures peck at them, piercing their eyes and drinking the blood; this is the karmic retribution for their past evil deed of giving alcohol.
If they climb trees, they fall from the branches onto the ground, their bodies broken into a hundred or a thousand pieces; this is the karmic retribution for their past evil deed of giving alcohol.
If there are sinners who do not take refuge in the trees, they fall into the River of Ashes, where they are swept away by hot ashes and their bodies and bones are melted and rotted.

In this way, they undergo great suffering for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years; this is but a brief description. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the force of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer without ceasing at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish realm.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, the mind will be improper, and as a retribution one will suffer from malignant diseases—whether it be a major illness, heart disease, *cilāsa* (leprosy), swelling of the feet, or blindness of the eyes—these are the residual karmic fruits of that evil action.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava) to see what other places exist there.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is another distinct place called the Forest of Smoky Plantains (Kadalī-dhūma-vana), which is the thirteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He perceives and knows through hearing and wisdom:

if a person habitually commits and frequently engages in killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, that person will be born in a specific sub-region of the Raurava Hell known as the Smoky Forest of Plantains (*kadalī-dhūma-vana*). The nature of the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Now, alcohol is further discussed:

if a person, out of a lustful mind, provides alcohol to a chaste and virtuous woman in secret, desiring to make her intoxicated so that she will no longer maintain her dignified deportment, her mind becomes agitated and altered, and she hopes to engage in unrighteous conduct.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the separate location within the Raurava Hell known as the Smoky Forest of Plantains—where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:
that place of hell is five thousand yojanas in circumference and breadth; it is filled everywhere with smoke, possessing fierce, scorching fires and further enveloped in darkness.
Within that dark fire, there are glowing iron blocks three *krośas* thick, consisting entirely of burning charcoal, hidden by the darkness so as not to be seen.

Those hell-beings are swiftly submerged and enveloped by the black fire; they are unable to cry out. Thus, all the sense-faculties (*indriya-mukha*) of these sinners are completely filled with fire; this is the karmic retribution for their evil deed of giving intoxicants.

If they escape from that place, their root-entrances will be filled with the smoke of plantains; having experienced the suffering of the smoke, they again recall the pleasure previously found within the fire, for the power of such smoke is fierce and sharp.
If they escape that place, there are further iron birds called *dhūmapattramālā* (Smoke-Leaf-Garland), whose beaks are extremely sharp; they peck through their bones and drink the marrow.
As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the force of that karma has not been exhausted, they are subjected to unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when the evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that hellish realm.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will frequently suffer from ailments of the ribs, poverty, and a short lifespan—these being the residual karmic retributions of that former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again contemplates the Great Hell of Screaming (Raurava). What other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Place of the Forest of Smoking Fire (Dhūmāgni-vana), which is the fourteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He perceives and knows through hearing and wisdom:

if a person habitually commits and frequently engages in killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, that person will fall into the Scream Hell (Raurava) at the location of the Forest of Smoking Fire; the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Now, alcohol is further discussed:
if a person wishes to cause the ruin and affliction of an enemy, they give alcohol to a thief or to an official, intending for it to bring suffering upon that enemy.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body breaks up at the end of life, they fall into an evil destination—the Smoky Fire Forest section of the Raurava Hell—where they undergo great suffering and distress.
That is to say:

the hot winds are like knives and like fire; due to their evil karma, such winds arise, blowing those offenders into the air where they strike and collide with one another, unable to find any autonomy. Their bodies are shattered like balls of sand, yet by the power of their evil karma, their bodies are restored once more.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, until their evil karma is neither destroyed nor decayed, and until the potency of that karma is exhausted, they undergo all manner of suffering.
As for what these sufferings are:

the suffering of fire, the suffering of blades, the suffering of being split by sharp knives, the suffering of disease, the suffering of iron, the suffering of hot ashes, and so forth; they undergo such foremost, most extreme, most evil, and most urgent sufferings as these.

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of virtuous karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, with three protrusions on the neck that rise up extremely high and are constantly afflicted by the disease of lameness, this is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the great hell of Howling (Raurava) to see what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Cloud-Fire-Mist (Abhra-jvālā-nīhāra), which is the fifteenth location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He perceives through seeing and hearing:

if a person habitually commits and frequently engages in killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, they will be born in that hell known as the Cloud-Fire-Mist region; their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Now, alcohol is further discussed:

if a person gives alcohol to one who observes the precepts or to a non-Buddhist practitioner, causing them to become intoxicated, and then mocks and ridicules them to make them feel ashamed, while feeling joy and pleasure within their own mind.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Cloud-Fire-Mist region of the Howling Hell—where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:

that hell is filled with hell-fire two hundred cubits thick. The *yama* beings seize the hell-beings and force them to walk through the fire; from their feet to their heads, they are entirely melted away, yet as soon as they are lifted up, they are restored to life.
Because of their evil karma, a wind of fire arises, blowing the hell-beings about like scattered leaves, tossing them in the ten directions as if they were twisted ropes.
Those hell-beings are thus burned until not even so much as a particle of ash remains, yet they are born once again.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they are constantly burned; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer without ceasing at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

and if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, that person will be born in the land of Yama or the land of Bālika. Because they constantly carried people for others, their necks are perpetually swollen; this is the remaining karmic fruit of the evil deed of drinking alcohol.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the great hell of Screaming to see what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Distinguishing Suffering (*Vibhaktaduḥkha*), which is the sixteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He perceives and knows through hearing and insight:

if a person habitually engages in and frequently commits the acts of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, that person will fall into the Section of Suffering within the Raurava Hell; the nature of the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Now, alcohol is further discussed as follows:

Suppose there is someone who, wishing to carry out an undertaking, gives alcohol to slaves and laborers so that they may drink it and their physical strength will not fail; thus, when going on a hunt, they can run swiftly and kill deer and other game.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination—the Scream Hell, the Section of Suffering—where they undergo great agony and distress.
As for what is called suffering:

according to the various and manifold conceptualizations of those sinners, the Yama-wardens inflict upon them great agonies—hundreds of times, thousands of times, hundreds of thousands of times, or hundreds of billions of times. They undergo all the various and diverse sufferings previously described, as well as all the various sufferings found in other hells; all these sufferings are experienced here in double measure.
The Yama-wardens rebuke the sinner and speak this verse:
"By means of the three types of evil karma, It ripens throughout the nine locations;
One undergoes suffering in forty layers, Obtained through the practice of evil deeds."
Alcohol is the root of evil; it brings laughter and leads one into hell.
It causes the destruction of all faculties and is a cause for disadvantage.
Excessive joy leads to much speech, increasing greed and causing others to fear.
Verbal transgressions consist of self-aggrandizement and boastfulness; double-tongued speech is the foremost among them.
Alcohol can disturb the human mind, making one like a sheep that does not know what should or should not be done; thus, one should renounce alcohol.
One who is intoxicated by liquor is no different from one who is dead;
if one wishes never to die, that person should abandon liquor.
Liquor is the source of all faults and is perpetually unbeneficial.
The stairway to all evil realms, the abode of darkness;
drinking alcohol leads to hell and likewise to the realm of hungry ghosts;
one performs the karma of animals—this is the deception wrought by the fault of alcohol.
"Alcohol is the poison among poisons, The hell among hells, and the great disease among diseases; Thus it is said by the wise.
Alcohol destroys wisdom and destroys the faculties; It can utterly extinguish the treasure of the Dharma."
Alcohol is the primary cause of conception; it is an enemy that destroys the holy life (*brahmacarya*).
Drinking wine makes one contemptible, such that even kings do not hold one in high regard, let alone other ordinary people, who are thus toyed with by alcohol.
The great axe that cleaves all dharmas, Causing one to be without shame or modesty;
If a person drinks alcohol, They will be held in contempt by all.
Lacking wisdom and skillful means, Both body and speech become useless.
None understand anything at all, because alcohol has plundered their minds.
Those who drink alcohol have no cause for joy,
no cause for anger, and no cause for committing evil.
Delusion toward the Buddha destroys both worldly and world-transcending affairs;
it burns liberation like fire—this is the single dharma known as alcohol.
If one can renounce alcohol and practice the Dharma and precepts correctly, [one shall attain peace].
He has reached the foremost place, the realm where there is neither death nor birth.
You abandoned virtuous conduct and were deceived by liquor;
having fallen into the evil places of hell, what is the use of lamenting?
Though the first taste of drinking wine is sweet, the retribution one receives is the foremost suffering;
its fault is like that of the *kimpāka* fruit—thus it has been spoken by the wise.
The wise do not trust in wine, for it cannot corrupt their resolve.
Contacting cold, one receives the retribution of heat; through alcohol, one arrives at hell.
If one who commits evil deeds feels light-hearted and rejoices in their mind, they will experience the foremost suffering as retribution; such a person is a fool who later regrets their actions.
Do not take pleasure in the mind of desire; desire is the foremost deceiver of men, binding them in the evils of saṃsāra and serving as the cause for all hells.
If a person delights in desire, that person’s suffering will be boundless.
For those bitten by desire, happiness cannot be found.
You originally intended for desire, yet you have come to this evil hell to undergo extreme suffering and affliction; now you regret it in vain.
In the past you committed evil deeds, deceived by desire and delusion;
why did you not repent then? What is the use of repenting now?
The karma you have accumulated is firm; now you see the fruit of those evil deeds.
One should not commit evil; having committed evil, one now suffers its pain.
Evil karma brings an evil retribution; the doer of evil receives it himself.
Since evil does not bring calamity upon the virtuous, one should thus abandon evil.
"If one abandons evil people, one will have no fear of evil;
having created it oneself, one suffers its consequences alone—it is not to be consumed by anyone else.
Thus do the Yama-wardens rebuke the sinners in hell.

Having been thus rebuked and censured, they are further subjected to immeasurable varieties of suffering and affliction; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, with a parched body and an extreme state of anger that is difficult to subdue, this is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.

Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again contemplates the Great Hell of Screaming; in that Great Hell there is only this single location, and no other distinct place can be seen, nor is any other distinct karmic fruit to be found.

In this Great Hell of Screaming, as well as in its sixteen subsidiary locations, all the various sufferings found in the Sañjīva, Kālasūtra, Saṃghāta, and other hells are fully present, becoming increasingly heavy and intense.
The suffering experienced in that hell is ten times greater than all the sufferings in those other hells. Why is this?

Because the evil karma they have committed is firm, heavy, and abundant—namely, the fourfold evil karmas of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and giving alcohol to those who observe the precepts—the various sufferings they undergo in this hell are firm, harsh, and manifold. Their lifespan is extended, and they experience the bitter retribution of the fruits of those fourfold karmas for ten times longer.
When that bhikṣu has thus observed the retributive fruits of suffering from these fourfold evil karmas and has reflected upon them, he becomes ten times more weary of and detached from saṃsāra.

Furthermore, the practitioner reflects within his mind—contemplating the course of dharmas in accordance with the True Dharma—and having thus observed these various hells, that bhikṣu develops a profound fear of birth and death and attains the tenth stage.

The yakṣas of that realm, having learned this, rejoiced. Likewise, they heard the yakṣas of the air, as previously described, continuing in succession up to the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, and Mahābrahmā devas. Having heard this, those Brahmās and others rejoiced, as previously stated:
"The faction of Māra within birth and death has been entirely diminished, and the True Dharma increases."
"Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next examines the other great hells. He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another hell named Great Wailing (Mahāraurava)."
By what karma are sentient beings born in that hell?
He perceives, hears, and knows:

if a person delights in, frequently practices, and fully indulges in killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying, such a person is born in the Great Howling (Mahāraurava) Great Hell.
Killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking alcohol—these actions and their karmic results are as previously described.
Now, false speech is discussed:
it is supremely satisfying yet the foremost evil, detested and despised by all virtuous people, and the gateway through which one enters all evil realms.

Regarding such actions: suppose there is a person—whether a king, one like a king, or among a host of soldiers—who is regarded as upright; when two people are disputing, he acts as a witness and speaks of the matter thus:
"This is what I know; this matter is exactly so; I am the authority."

When those two disputants have each finished speaking, such a witness, though knowing the truth in his heart, speaks falsely with his mouth—whether for the sake of obtaining wealth, or for the sake of acquaintances and friends, or out of a mind stained by desire—thus deceiving himself and bringing about his own ruin, as previously described.
A witness who has perceived the matter in this way thinks to himself:
"He previously spoke such and such, whereas I now speak differently.
What fault is there in this false speech? What sin is there in such a lie?"
That person who speaks falsely thinks in his heart that there is no fault, giving rise to this thought:
"I shall be without fault.
Yet, by speaking inconsistently between two people, that person incurs the offense of lying.

When one person receives a punishment, it may sometimes result in death, sometimes in the fear of death, sometimes in the imposition of a fine, or sometimes in the forfeiture of their home; according to those legal codes, they receive a corresponding punishment.

Such an evil person, by reason of these causes and conditions of false speech and evil karma, at the dissolution of the body after death, falls into an evil destination, namely, the Great Howling Great Hell.
"The lifespan there is long; by what measure is it reckoned?

Just as eight thousand years is the lifespan in the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, if one were to take eight thousand years according to the human world, that would constitute one day and night in that heaven. Thirty such days make one month, and twelve such months make one year.
If one were to live for eight thousand years in that heaven, that would constitute one day and night in that hell."

In that Great Howling Great Hell is the dwelling place of those people of evil karma and those who speak falsehoods; because they deceive both themselves and others, they are able to destroy all supreme roots of goodness, like a great darkness in which the great masses have no faith.
Such false speech is not permitted by virtuous people; it is censured by all sages—śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and samyaksaṃbuddhas—and is incompatible with all mundane and supramundane paths.
It is a great axe that hews down the bridge of all roots of goodness; it constantly afflicts others like a rotting corpse; it is fragile and destructive like the arising of a malignant poison;
and it is the cause and condition for rebirth in the world and the evil realms.
It is no different from excrement; it causes a putrid stench to arise within the mouth.
It constantly produces a web of suffering that cannot be enjoyed, acting as a messenger of great terror for this great hell.
When death is imminent, the mind is struck with great alarm, and one falls under the jurisdiction of the realm of the Yama-rogues.
This is a great enemy, capable of causing one to fall into the realms of hungry ghosts and animals as proof of one's evil karma;
it is the causal condition for poverty;
and it can bring about the great terrors of hell.
It can act as the causal condition for devouring one another in the form of animals;
it is the seed that has been revolving in birth and death since beginningless time.
As for the retribution for false speech, one is born in those places; in that great hell, there are eighteen locations.
What are the eighteen?
First is named Roaring Roar;
second is named Suffering Without Limit.
The third is named Enduring Unbearable Hardship and Affliction;
the fourth is named Pressing at Will;
the fifth is named All Darkness.
Sixth is named "Human Smoke";
seventh is named "Like an Insect Falling [into Fire]";
eighth is named "Life and Death, etc."
The ninth is named "Mutually Differentiated Transformation";
the tenth is named "Vain Expectation";
the eleventh is named "Double Oppression."
The twelfth is named Mutually Oppressing;
the thirteenth is named Vajra-beaked Crow;
the fourteenth is named Fire-Garland.
Fifteenth is named Receiving the Pain of Sharp Points;
sixteenth is named Receiving Boundless Suffering;
seventeenth is named Feeding on Blood and Marrow.
The eighteen are named the Eleven Flaming [Hells].
These eighteen locations are all sub-locations belonging to the Great Screaming Great Hell.
As for that Great Screaming Great Hell, by what karma do sentient beings take birth there?

Having fully completed the paths of karmic action through their accumulation, and having delighted in performing them repeatedly, they fall into the Great Hell of Universal Terror—the very essence of which is extreme dread—and there undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:

their tongues are exceedingly long, measuring three *krośas* in length; they are as soft as lotus petals and protrude from their mouths. The *Yama-rodha* hell-beings seize hot iron plows that blaze with fire and furrow paths into them;
furthermore, molten copper of a deep crimson hue, glowing with heat, is poured over their tongues.

Worms arise within the tongue; these worms have flaming mouths and devour the tongue itself. Due to the power of the karmic offenses of that person who spoke falsely, the tongue undergoes great suffering and cannot be put back into the mouth.
In the mouths of those hell-beings there is a worm called the *Mortar-Worm* (*ulūkhala-kīṭa*) that pulls out their teeth.

Furthermore, due to their evil karma, winds disperse their gums until they are crushed into powder like sand; winds with razor-sharp blades slice and cut their throats, while iron-worms with flaming beaks devour their hearts.
In that Great Screaming Root Hell, the bodies of those who have lied are thus intensely scorched.

Due to their evil karma, worms are born within their bodies and devour them; these worms’ bodies are ablaze with flames, and as they consume the person’s body from within, the denizen of hell suffers the agony of acute disease.
Thus, they endure two kinds of suffering: both internal and external.

In that hell, the Yama-wardens further inflict various torments upon the offenders, namely, striking their sinews, veins, and marrow with iron hooks, so that all parts of their bodies are shattered and scattered.
Furthermore, they undergo other various sufferings, namely having their entire bodies, including all limbs and even the bones, hewn by axes.
Because of such causes and conditions, that person who speaks falsely says:
"Not relying upon the bridge of all dharmas to proceed is a gateway to all that is unbeneficial, and it is hail for the grain of all virtues."

Such false speech is likewise a gateway to all evil realms, a treasury of all suffering and affliction, that which all sentient beings do not trust, and that which all noble ones discard like excrement; the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, Arhats, and others abandon it as they would poison;
if one practices worldly or world-transcending paths while engaging in it, it is like a great darkness;
no person will love it.
This is the primary cause and condition for hell, resembling nothing else but a vast, pitch-black darkness.
There are various such evils as these.
Whether a person has spoken, is speaking, or will speak of such karmic causes, they shall obtain a corresponding fruit.

In that Great Screaming Great Hell, there is further fire that burns like fresh ghee; flaming iron saws are used to saw their bodies, causing suffering and distress to both body and mind. That Great Hell boils them with a great fire; this is the hell-like state resulting from the causes and conditions of one who has witnessed and known [the truth] yet failed to cultivate great compassion.
There are all manner of grave illnesses—the names of such ailments are even difficult to utter—and those who suffer such diseases experience extreme agony.

Regarding these two kinds of great suffering thus described, there are immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of hellish torments. Until the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has been destroyed, decayed, and its residual energy exhausted, they shall be subjected to incessant suffering at all times.
When their evil karma is exhausted, they may finally escape from that hell.
If, however, there is matured wholesome karma from the distant past of previous lives, they will not be reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will be poor, short-lived, mentally deranged, or impotent, despised by all as wicked and base, and distrusted by others—this is the residual retribution for killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
“If a person transgresses even a single dharma, such a liar destroys their future lives; there is no evil they will not commit.”
Do not speak false words; all evil causes and conditions can bind one to birth and death, so that the path of the virtuous cannot be seen.
They bring no benefit in either of the two worlds, and result in universal hatred and malice.
One who speaks falsely can cause all dharmas to become empty and desolate.
For a person at the very moment of birth, there is a great axe within their mouth;
with it, they are able to cut themselves—this is what is called speaking falsehoods.
The banner of all evils, the rope for all evil realms,
the storehouse of the darkness of delusion— this is what is called speaking falsehoods.
If a person departs from truthful speech, they are abandoned by all virtuous people.
In this life one is like grass; in future lives one is burned in evil realms.
O steadfast one, do not speak falsely; false speech is exceedingly evil.
The breath from one's mouth becomes putrid and foul-smelling, and in a future existence one will surely feel regret.
If one abandons truthful speech, that person cannot attain the Dharma;
such a person who has forsaken the Dharma will experience boundless suffering in this world.
Truth is the lamp of all phenomena; virtuous people cherish reality as it is.
Attaining victory within the heavenly realms is what the one who has transcended feverish passion has taught.
Through the true path one gains birth in heaven; through the true path one attains liberation.
If a person departs from the truth, the virtuous describe them as being like a dog.
If a person lacks truthful speech, they are the lowest among the low;
truth is indeed the stairway to the Dharma, the foremost light among lights.
Truth is the path to liberation, the foremost wealth among riches.
The foremost among all rescues, as taught by the wise;
the foremost among all lights, the foremost eye among eyes;
even without any possessions, one is truly wealthy—the ornament of all ornaments.
Truth is the foremost treasury, which kings and others cannot seize;
the person who speaks the truth proceeds upon the supreme path.
Those adorned with various ornaments are not as truly beautiful as this.
If a person is truly adorned, their comeliness shall be like that of a deva.
Neither parents nor wealth, neither friends nor kin, can provide protection in the afterlife; only truthful speech can save.
The Sage has said that false speech is the foremost fire among fires, the foremost poison among poisons, and the first step upon the path to the evil realms.
False speech can burn a person; it is called the foremost burning.
Just as one avoids the touch of poisonous fire, so should one abandon false speech.
All such evils—heed not to speak falsely; for the wise declare that false speech is the source of all fears and evils.

That bhikṣu thus contemplates the karmic fruit of false speech with unobstructed vision, and likewise clearly perceives the merit of truthful speech. Thus contemplating the paths of wholesome and unwholesome karma, he observes the location of the Great Howling Great Hell; he sees therein a place named Hu-hu, which is the first distinct sub-region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:
if a person commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, or drinks intoxicants, they are born in that place; the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is false speech:

when, due to the influence of relatives or old friends, one is drawn into a faction and utters falsehoods during a dispute, yet afterwards does not repent, does not feel revulsion for it, does not condemn it, and takes pleasure in practicing and committing it frequently.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into that hell and are born in the Roaring Place, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what constitutes this suffering:
because they used their tongue to speak falsehoods, they receive punishment with their tongue.

The Yama-rodha attendants pierce the lower part of their jaws with sharp iron knives and pull out their tongues; they smear the tongues with foul muddy water. Their mouths blaze with flames and their tongue-roots rot and stink. Black insects with flaming mouths devour their tongues, and they undergo great physical suffering as previously described in the Saṃjīva and other hells.
As for the nature of that suffering: all the sufferings experienced in all the aforementioned hells are combined together, as briefly described before.
This continues until the person’s evil karma of false speech has been utterly rotted away and lost its potency; only then does one obtain release from that hellish place.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, being impoverished, insane, mindless, or having lost one's mind, short-lived, deficient in faculties, and despised by the world—all these are vessels of total non-benefit.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, contemplates the great hell of Raurava: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Place of Immeasurable Suffering, which is the second secondary location of that hell.
What karma do sentient beings perform to be born in that place?
He sees and knows through wisdom:

if a person commits and accumulates the acts of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking intoxicants, they will fall into that hell named Boundless Suffering; the nature of the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is false speech. What is false speech?
If a person utters false speech out of desire or out of a mind of hatred, or if, being sent by another, they speak these words:
"That person is my foremost acquaintance and one whom I love. If you love me, and since he is my friend, for my sake you should address that adversary with words intended to cause him harm."

If a person speaks such false words, at the dissolution of the body after death, they will fall into an evil destination, being born in that hell in a place of immeasurable suffering and affliction, where they undergo great torment.

As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: the sufferings experienced in the Reviving Hell and other such hells, all combined together, constitute the suffering of this single location in hell.
Why is this? Because the karma is heavy, the suffering experienced is also heavy; because the suffering is heavy, it demonstrates the retribution of karma.
Thus, the experience of suffering has no respite; karma and afflictions cause one to revolve in birth and death without end, like a spinning wheel.

Thus, all evil karmas of false speech—whether through various causes and conditions or various modes of operation—these manifold evil karmas, which are committed extensively and experienced extensively, all arise from false speech.
Furthermore, false speech can sever and destroy the pillar of fully cultivated roots of goodness; as the cause is similar, the fruit obtained is similar.
For this reason, this place in hell is named "Suffering Without Limit," which cannot be described.
The suffering and affliction they endure cannot be fully described; it has no parallel, for they are among the most wretched of all those who dwell in the hells, undergoing such evil torment.

What is called suffering: the suffering of being born as insects; the suffering of hunger and thirst; the suffering of great fire; the suffering of having no hope; the suffering of having no consolation; the suffering of darkness; the suffering of mutual contact; the suffering of encountering undesirable tactile objects, forms, sounds, and scents; the suffering of seeing one's former enemies arrive with iron blades to cut one; the suffering of crossing the River of Ashes and being pierced by iron hooks; the suffering of falling from steep precipices and being burned by great fires; and the suffering of having grass pulled out from one's body.
Regarding the suffering of plucking out grass:
they strike and cut [the skin] until it is wounded; they place the grass upon the wound and wait for it to adhere, and only then do they pull it out.
They undergo the suffering of being crushed by diamond-crushing grinders, and they undergo the suffering of being scorched by a wreath of all-pervading flames.

They experience such boundless suffering associated with these hells, which is similar to the fruit of suffering experienced by those who have fallen into great perilous places associated with the hell of lying.

In this manner, as long as that person’s evil karma of lying has not been destroyed or decomposed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times;
only when that evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

and if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, that person will be constantly ill—whether suffering from throat ailments or mouth ailments—and endure such sufferings as these. They will be impoverished and distressed, and though they constantly beg from the wealthy and those capable of giving, they receive nothing. Everyone knows this and everyone says:
"You are a person with a tongue for lying."
Therefore, he did not give [it], and he died of a malignant disease; this is the residual fruit of the evil karma of false speech from his previous life.
*Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna Sūtra*, Scroll 8 (and Scroll 9).
Translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Chapter on the Hells, Part Five:
"Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the Great Howling Great Hell; what other places are there within it?"
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place, called Enduring Unbearable Hardship and Torment; this is the third separate location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He perceives, hears, and knows:

if a person habitually commits and frequently engages in killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking alcohol, they fall into that hell and are born in the place of unbearable, solid suffering. Their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is false speech. What is false speech?

It is when one is held by a king, a royal official, or a government functionary; or due to another person, or due to one's own circumstances; or for the sake of obtaining release from fear by giving away property; or as testimony for others, or for the sake of livelihood—such is false speech.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination; born in that hell in a place of unendurable, solid suffering, they undergo great anguish and distress.
As for what is called suffering:

due to evil karma, snakes emerge from one's own body and move everywhere throughout the entire body, pulling at every tendon. By the causal conditions of hell, they devour the various parts of the body, eating the spleen, intestines, and so forth, writhing within; such torment is more grievous than the suffering of fire.
Thus, in that place, they undergo the suffering of great serpents and the suffering of virulent poisons; more fierce than fire, they experience such sufferings without end.
The torments endured in that hellish realm are so solid and unbearable that they cannot be fully described.

The suffering of that hell is unbearable, yet they do not die; at all times they undergo extreme and heavy suffering. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from long ago in previous lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, once within the mother's womb, the mother will constantly suffer from illness.

Due to the power of their evil karma, from the time they first enter the womb until their birth, the mother’s illness does not subside; once they emerge from the womb, they fall ill immediately, and no physician is able to cure them.
"This is the remaining karmic retribution of that original evil deed.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the Great Howling Great Hell: what other places are there within it?"
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called *Svairapīḍana* (Arbitrary Crushing), which is the fourth sub-region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
Having performed and accumulated such karma, one is born in that place. There, one sees:
a person who has delighted in and frequently committed killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking alcohol, and lying falls into that hell of being crushed at will.
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking intoxicants are as previously explained.
What is false speech? It is as follows:
There are those who claim another's field or seize another's field, engaging in disputes and false speech; they speak with devious turns rather than straightforwardly;
they rob others of their fields and, through their words, suppress others while claiming the truth for themselves.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination; in that hell, in the Place of Willful Crushing, they undergo the suffering of being crushed.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies suffered in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are experienced here in their entirety.
When the denizens of the Reviving and other hells see this hell, they all point and say, "That is a hell!"
What is called suffering is as follows:

there are two iron bellows filled with wind; the *Yama* hell-wardens place the sinner inside an iron furnace just as one would place iron, blow upon it intensely with the bellows, seize him with iron tongs and beat him on an iron anvil with an iron mallet. Having beaten him thus, they place him back in the furnace and blow upon him with the two iron bellows as before.

Due to their sinful karma, the evil heat is extremely fierce; having been blown [upon] again and again, they are pincered out and placed upon iron anvils, where they are struck with hot iron hammers—beating them intensely, continuously, repeatedly, and violently. Even after being beaten in this manner, they remain alive and do not die.
Furthermore, they are pincered and placed into boiling cauldrons, held upright and made rigid; this continues at all times without a moment's pause.
Only when their evil karma has been exhausted, decayed, and rendered breathless do they finally escape from that hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, being constantly thirsty, prone to much anger, and distrusted by others—this is the residual fruit and retribution of that former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the Great Howling Great Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Total Darkness, which is the fifth subsidiary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods; because they delight in and frequently commit these acts, they fall into that hell, the region of total darkness.
The actions of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking intoxicants, along with their karmic results, are as previously described.
What is false speech? It is as follows:
Suppose there is a person who has committed adultery with another's wife, yet in the presence of a crowd or before a king, he speaks falsely, saying:
"I have truly not violated this woman."
Thus, he causes that woman’s family to instead incur calamity and punishment.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, remaining in the "All-Dark" section of that hell to undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:

their heads are split open and their tongues are pulled out; once pulled out, they are sliced with knives; after being sliced, the tongues grow back again, and are then painfully cut once more with flaming blades.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed and the potency of that karma is not exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
When their evil karma is exhausted, they shall finally be released from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of virtuous karma from a long time past in a previous life, they are not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
and if they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will be born blind or deaf, constantly living by begging at crossroads or in four-way alleys.

I myself am thus; having obtained such people as my parents, I have lived by begging from house to house through immeasurable lifetimes, my lifespan not being long, and I have had neither wife nor children.
This is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, contemplates the Great Howling Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Darkness-Smoke, which is the sixth separate location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
Through seeing, hearing, and knowing, he understands:
if a person habitually commits and frequently engages in killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying, they will fall into that hellish realm called the Place of Dark Smoke.
The actions and their karmic results regarding killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking alcohol are as previously explained.
What is false speech? It is as follows:

There is a person who engages in livelihood and makes a pact with another, binding themselves by an incense offering as their covenant. While pursuing their livelihood in different places, they actually obtain wealth and property, yet speak falsely, saying:
"I have obtained no goods."
Yet they do not share it with one another.
Such a person is a great thief who plunders the wealth of others.

Due to the causal conditions of this evil karma, when their body breaks up at the end of life, they fall into an evil destination; they are in that hell, in the place of dark smoke, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies suffered in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are experienced here in their entirety.
Furthermore, there are even more severe ones, namely:
every part of one's body is completely cut to pieces.
Once cut, it grows back again; as soon as it has grown, it is tender and soft, and they cut it once more.
Having been cut, it grows back again; as soon as it has grown, it is even more tender and soft, and they cut it yet again. This is the coarse retribution of suffering for their evil karma:

when all the flesh is exhausted, only the bones remain. Vermin are born upon their own bodies; these vermin have diamond-like beaks, and being ablaze with fire and various colors, they devour their bodies.
Experiencing various kinds of suffering, they cry out with loud wails.

Those hell-beings remain thus for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, until their accumulated evil karma is exhausted, their vital energy is spent, and they have completely rotted away; only then do they manage to escape from that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
