yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, all parts of one's body will be putrid and foul-smelling, moist worms will grow on one's head, one will constantly lack clothing and suffer from poverty and hardship, whatever little one possesses will be patched together, one’s words will be entirely disbelieved, one will be unloved by others, and one will not know how to manage one's livelihood—these are the residual karmic fruits of that evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the Great Howling Great Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called "Falling Like a Flying Insect," which is the seventh secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods, delighting in such acts and committing them frequently; they fall into that hell and are born in a distinct location, like a flying insect falling into a specific spot.
The karmic actions and their retributions regarding killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking alcohol are as previously described.
What is false speech? It is as follows:
There are those who take the property of the Sangha—whether grain, robes, or any other such items—and trade them here and there, buying low and selling high;
having thus obtained profit, they do not give it to the Sangha, but instead deceive the Sangha by claiming they have gained no profit.
Such a person, driven by greed and speaking falsely, says:
"I have obtained only this, and nothing more;
my business dealings have yielded only this much."
Such a person speaks false words for the sake of livelihood.
Such a deluded person acts out of a greedy mind.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination. They are born in a separate location within that hell like a flying insect falling there, undergoing great suffering and affliction.

As for what is called suffering: there are iron dogs that gnaw through their bellies; having torn them open, they devour them—eating their intestines and eating their backs. The henchmen of Yama hold axes and hatchets; the axes are blazing with fierce heat, and they hack away the flesh of their bodies to weigh it out—one *liang*, half a *liang*—and give it to the dogs to eat.
The axes and hatchets are extremely sharp; they further hack at their bones to extract the marrow, because they intend to give it to the dogs.

With flaming iron hooks, they hook their jaws; once these have been split open, they use flaming iron tongs to pull out their tongues. They are then driven to stand up, whereupon flaming iron hooks hook their bodies, causing all the flesh to tear apart. In this manner, they pull out their tendons, hooking through every part of the body until it is completely pierced.
Thus, the person who has committed the evil karma of lying consumes the fruit of their own evil deeds.

When the karma of that liar has matured, even though they have escaped the henchmen of Yama, they find themselves in a hell filled with blazing fires so dense that there is not a single empty space between them. The sinner who lied enters this Fire Hell like an insect falling into a flame; thus they are constantly burned. Having been burned, they are born again; having been born, they are burned once more.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, until their accumulated evil karma is exhausted, their vitality is destroyed, and they have completely rotted away, they finally obtain release from that hellish place.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of shared karma, being born into a poor and lowly family, and is burned as soon as birth occurs—even if many people provide rigorous protection—one will inevitably be burned. This is the residual karmic fruit of that evil deed.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the Great Howling Great Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called "Alive-and-Dead," which is the eighth secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He perceives through seeing and hearing:

if a person commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking alcohol, and further engages frequently and with delight in false speech, they will fall into that hell, into places such as the "living-and-dying" area.
As previously described, all the sufferings experienced in the Saṃjīva and other hells are fully present here; furthermore, there is another distinct suffering:
namely, that one dies as soon as struck with a staff, yet revives as soon as the staff is withdrawn.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they die and are revived again, and having been revived, they die once more; such is the state of that person due to their evil karma.
Once they have escaped from that, they next see a forest of *utpala* lotuses and run toward it swiftly, seeking rescue and seeking refuge, seeing blue flowers filling the *utpala* grove.
What is the retribution obtained for such false speech?
It is as follows:

Suppose there is a person who is not a renunciant, yet puts on the robes of a renunciant for the purpose of committing theft. He sees a group of people intending to travel through a wilderness and asks them:
"Is there any bandit in that wilderness?
Knowing there was a bandit, he replied, "No."
When that person arrived, he was plundered by bandits and lost his wealth and goods.
Because he had deceived others with false speech, due to those causal conditions, he received a result corresponding to his karma.
He sees blue lotuses (*utpala*) filled with a blue light, yet they are entirely fire.
The *yama-puruṣas* seize him and force him into the midst of the lotuses; they burn him with fire, and because he has no feet, he is unable to descend.
By the power corresponding to such evil karma, the hands, feet, eyes, and all other limbs of those sinners are entirely destroyed.

In this hell, amidst the *utpala* lotuses, great fires fill the space; thus for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years they are constantly burned and boiled, dying and being revived again and again.
As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they will experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish realm.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from long ago in past lives, one is not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, all one’s speech will lack rational basis, consisting of spontaneous mental chatter and circuitous, evasive talk;
and even if one acquires wealth, it will be seized by the king, and one will die in prison.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, contemplates the great hell of Great Screaming (Mahāraurava): what other places are there within it?
He perceives through seeing, hearing,
and knowledge that there is another distinct place called *Vicitravartana*, which is the ninth separate location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods; having delighted in and frequently practiced these acts, they fall into that hell in its various shifting locations.
The actions of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking intoxicants, along with their karmic results, are as previously described.
What is false speech? It is as follows:
There are those who are deceitful and speak falsehoods, desiring to cause others to experience victory or defeat, decline or profit, life or death, and so forth.
That is to say:

there may be someone, such as a master of yin and yang, who is skilled in the arts of divination and whose prognostications always prove correct; or one who is a person of virtue, always speaking truthful words and thus trusted by the world. Furthermore, due to certain circumstances, when questioned by another, they harbor such an intention:
"I have never spoken falsely; everyone knows this, and all people believe me.
Now that I speak falsely, everyone will say it is true.
Having thought thus, he immediately utters a falsehood.
Because of false speech, one may cause the total ruin of a kingdom; if a superior person dies, it causes his enemies to plunder one another and lose their wealth and property.
That person who speaks falsehoods is trusted by all, and they believe his lies.
Though that liar maintains the appearance and dress of one who practices right conduct, he is in reality a thief.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when his body breaks up at the end of life, he falls into an evil destination; dwelling in various shifting locations within that hell, he undergoes great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:

in that place of hell, one sees from afar one's parents, servants, acquaintances, those with whom one shared incense and lamps, and virtuous friends—those very people previously seen in human life—who comfort one within the hell. Having heard these affectionate words, the hell-being runs swiftly toward them, hoping for rescue and seeking a refuge.

That person thus runs toward another place and enters into the midst of ashes and fire; like a stone falling into water, he sinks and then rises again, his entire body experiencing great agony as he cries out with a loud voice.

Furthermore, they see their parents, wives, children, incense, lamps, and virtuous friends and spiritual mentors; they run toward them once more, but due to their evil karma, iron hooks arise along the way that hook and tear at their bodies. Upon reaching them, they are seized by the *yama-rākṣasas*, who use flaming iron saws to split their bodies apart as if splitting wood.

When such a sinner is released from that place, he remains as nothing but bones; with all his limbs completely shattered, he flees toward another location, where he is again seized by other *yama-puruṣas* and cast into a wheel of flaming iron blades.
Those iron wheel-blades exist both above and below.

Due to their evil karma, these iron wheels are filled with sharp blades; they rotate rapidly, blazing with fierce flames, grinding those people who committed the evil karma of lying until they are pulverized like fine flour, yet once ground to powder, they are born again.

Once those hell-beings have escaped from the *cakra* (wheel) region, they again see their parents, wives, children, and their spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) with whom they shared the incense and lamps; longing for rescue and seeking a refuge, they run toward them with great speed. However, due to their evil karma, as they run along the path, many glowing iron hooks spring up, and there are fierce lions—born of their own evil karma—who seize those sinners and place them within their mouths, between their teeth. The *Yama-rākṣasas* then hook them out with glowing iron hooks. Once they are pulled out, they think of it and run once more.

As they run in this manner, their feet are split and cracked; the flames burn them intensely, and all their limbs are utterly destroyed, scorched and charred, yet they still do not stop running. Their entire bodies are covered in sores, and the very marrow of that sinner’s bones and sinews is completely exhausted.
This is because that person habitually practiced and frequently committed false speech; through such similar karmic causes, they receive a similar fruit.
As that person said: "I am one who speaks the truth."

Thus they speak false words, words with a deceitful and crooked mind, and words that slander others; in this way, those people perceive the existence of parents, wives, children, incense offerings, and spiritual friends.

That person who spoke falsely shall thus endure boundless suffering and affliction, as well as harsh and piercing pains, for an immeasurable number of hundreds of thousands of years. Constantly boiled and burned, constantly split and beaten, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times until their evil karma is destroyed and decayed, and until the residual force of that karma is exhausted.
Only when their evil karma is spent will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of virtuous karma from a long time past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of common karma as poor, lowly, and base—deprived of sense faculties, constantly ill, detested and envied by all people, distrusted by all, defiled and wicked by all, such that all one's efforts are in vain and one’s desires remain unfulfilled—this is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the Great Howling Great Hell and considers what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Vain Expectation (Tang-xiwang), which is the tenth secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees and knows through wisdom:

if a person commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking alcohol, and further engages frequently and with delight in false speech, they will fall into that hell, the Place of Vain Hope. The karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Now, false speech is being discussed. What is false speech?

It is when, toward those who are suffering—such as the sick, the hungry, the thirsty, the poor, the solitary, the lowly, the foolish, or the weak—if one has all manner of provisions such as rice and other foods, whether for eating or drinking, or clothing, bedding, dwellings, and so forth, and yet, whether they ask or do not ask, one promises them these things but does not give them; while they constantly hope for them, their hopes are later frustrated.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination; in that hell, the Place of Vain Hope, they undergo great suffering and affliction.

Because they previously promised food and subsequently failed to give it, due to that evil karma, they see in the midst of the hells various kinds of *khādaniya* (solid) and *bhojaniya* (soft) foods, as well as various exquisite and beautifully adorned places. Those hell-beings, suffering from extreme hunger and thirst, run swiftly toward those food locations. From afar, they see that food as being exceedingly fine, deeply desirable, pure, and abundant; yet upon reaching it, it has vanished, and they see only molten iron, blazing with fierce flames.

Having set out for that food, they run with great haste; because of their evil karma, iron hooks fill the path, which hook and tear at their bodies as they proceed. Having reached that place, following the sequence previously described, the food they see there consists entirely of molten iron, blazing with fierce flames, foul-smelling and loathsome in color—all produced by the evil karma of their false speech.
Once they see it from nearby, they immediately fall into it; if they smell its odor, their noses are scorched and they fall down.
If they touch it with their bodies, all parts of their limbs are set ablaze like fireflies, and molten iron burns their lips.
Once the lips have been burned, the throat is burned next;
once the throat has been burned, the heart is burned next;
once the heart has been burned, the spleen is burned next.
Once the spleen has been burned, it next burns the intestines.
Having burned the raw receptacle (*āma-koṣṭha*) in this successive order, it next burns the cooked receptacle (*pakva-koṣṭha*);
having burned the cooked receptacle, it exits from below.

Furthermore, having promised to give away bedding, mats, and other such requisites, if one later fails to provide them, that karma of lying will cause one to experience great suffering when oppressed by cold and heat, with no hope of relief.
In that hell, upon the ground of glowing copper plates, once the sinner has sat down, all his limbs and members completely melt away; having melted, they are burned, and thereafter he is born again.

If a person intends to give their house to a guest but, having promised it, fails to do so, that karma of false speech places them within the *hāṇavī* cauldron and the *anumodanā* cauldron. Such cauldrons are fifty *yojanas* in measure, filled with boiling molten iron.

Those people of evil karma enter with their heads downward; once they have entered the cauldron, they are thoroughly boiled and cooked whether moving upward or downward. When not yet cooked, they sink; when fully cooked, they float;
having floated out, they sink back down again.

Thus, having been boiled and thoroughly cooked by the heat, all parts of the body have their flesh stripped away; the sinews, skin, and bones are scattered, and all the joints are diminished and completely worn away.
That cauldron is extremely dark, filled with boiling iron that burns his body alive as he cries out and wails.
Once he has been boiled there, he enters another cauldron; being thoroughly cooked therein, he floats to the surface, just as he was in the first cauldron, and it is the same here as well.

Thus, moving up and down, emerging and entering, those offenders of sin are sometimes gathered together in one place and sometimes scattered; when they draw near, they touch one another with extreme heat. Thus they touch and fall a hundred thousand times, their bodies shattered into a hundred thousand pieces only to be born again.

Furthermore, they come into contact with other sinners who are intensely hot; thus they collide a hundred thousand times, their bodies shattering into a hundred thousand fragments. Bound by the noose of the evil karma of their past false speech, they undergo such suffering at all times.

In this manner, as long as that person’s false speech—this evil and unwholesome karma—is not destroyed, not decomposed, and its karmic force is not exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when that evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, in a past life long ago, there was ripening of wholesome karma, one will not be born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will be born as a slave belonging to those whom one deceived in a previous life, because in that former life one promised something but did not give it—therefore, it is thus.
Or again, one may become a slave bound to another person due to that other person’s distinct karma.

Why is this? Because since beginningless time, one has transmigrated through birth after birth, creating various kinds of evil and unwholesome karma from the very outset. Thus, encompassed by the cycle of worldly birth and death, one wanders everywhere; because it is difficult to encounter [one's former kin], and because one is bound by the ropes of karma born of craving and attachment, one revolves through various places. Due to these differences in the places of transmigration, it is impossible to encounter one another.

Due to these causes and conditions, at times he may again become a slave to others, constantly deprived of food, drink, bedding, dwellings, and medicine according to his illness; he is perpetually reviled and humiliated by others—this is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, contemplates the great hell of Great Screaming (Mahāraurava) and considers what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Double Oppression (Ubhayābhinirvartana), which is the eleventh location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, and drink intoxicants, delighting in such acts and performing them frequently; they fall into that hell of "Double Oppression," where the karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is false speech.
What is false speech? It is as follows:

Within a village community, a guild, or similar assembly, if one speaks falsely out of a sense of self-conceit, or due to anger, or out of mutual hatred, jealousy, or contention—deceiving both oneself and others and destroying both oneself and others—one takes pleasure in the fact that, by reason of such false speech, another person within that assembly is made to suffer punishment.

Having thus repeatedly performed and brought such karma to completion, that person, through the causal conditions of these evil deeds, at the dissolution of the body after death, falls into an evil destination. There, in the hell known as the Place of Double Oppression, they undergo great suffering and torment.

That person, having thus spoken falsely and wickedly within such social circles and the like, due to such causes and such conditions, at the dissolution of the body after death, falls into that hell, being born in the distinct location called "Twofold Oppression," where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:
it is as previously described regarding the various hells such as Sañjīva, Kālasūtra, Saṃghāta, and Raurava; here, however, it is even more intense.
Due to their evil karma, there are lions with flaming fangs in that place.
Those wicked lions seize the hell-beings who committed falsehoods and inflict upon them the various kinds of suffering and affliction as previously described.
Once they have escaped, they are seized and eaten by that lion; when he lifts them up to eat them, they die, but when he sets them down, they live.
Furthermore, he devours all their limbs; once eaten, they are reborn, and once reborn, they are eaten again.

Due to their evil karma, that mechanical lion’s teeth are filled with blazing flames; as these teeth devour the offenders, by the power of their sinful deeds, they are bitten and burned within the lion’s mouth, undergoing two kinds of suffering.

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they are constantly burned and crushed, undergoing great suffering and affliction. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish realm.
If, in the distant past of previous lives, there was maturation of wholesome karma, one will not be born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, due to the power of that evil karma, one may either be bitten by a snake to the point of death or be killed and devoured by lions, tigers, or bears—this is the residual retribution of that evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, contemplates the great hell of Great Screaming: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Mutually Oppressing, which is the twelfth location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are people who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods; because they delight in practicing and frequently committing these acts, they fall into that hell of Mutual Oppression.
The karmic actions and their results regarding killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking alcohol are as previously described.
What is false speech?
There are brothers and others, whether near or distant, who are engaged in a dispute between two factions.
Regarding those brothers—whether they share the same father, the same ancestor, are half-brothers, or are paternal uncles—they quarrel over the division of property.

There may come witnesses who belong to the same clan, even as distant as twenty-one generations; among such people, one tells a lie for the benefit of those who are closer to oneself. Knowing it is not true, one intentionally instructs them to adopt a biased perspective, employing skillful means and calculations to utter a falsehood.

That karma is pervasive, ultimate, and fully accumulated; by reason of those evil karmic causes and conditions, when that person’s body breaks up at the end of life, they fall into an evil destination, in that hell of Mutual Compression, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies endured in the Sañjīva and other hells are experienced here in their entirety.

Furthermore, there is something even more severe: due to the evil karma of deceiving one's own kin with false speech, there are iron shears in that hellish place. When these shears see those very relatives whom the person deceived in his human life, they shear the flesh from his body and place it in his mouth, driving him to eat it; yet because of his evil karma, his own flesh does not decay.
The Yama-wardens rebuke him with a verse, saying:
"Truthful speech brings peace and happiness; Truthful speech leads to Nirvana.
False speech produces bitter fruits, Which you now come here to experience."
If one does not abandon false speech, one will encounter all manner of suffering.
True speech need not be purchased; it is easily obtained and not difficult to find.
It does not come from another country, nor does it come from another person.
Why abandon truthful speech and take pleasure in speaking falsehoods?
Truth is the supreme protection for the mouth; through truth one attains all dharmas.
Truth is the most excellent among lamps—thus has the Tathāgata spoken.
It is truly the most excellent among medicines, Always able to destroy suffering.
To commit evil is not my teaching; You have created it yourself through a deluded mind.
You committed the evil karma yourself, And now you must experience its results yourself.
Only when karma is exhausted can one attain liberation; what is the point of wailing and crying out?
Deceived by one's own evil karma, your current lamentation is in vain.
To deceive oneself is folly; such wailing is not wisdom.

"Once the Yama-wardens have thus rebuked the hell-beings, they further inflict upon them immeasurable hundreds of kinds of suffering, such as the great torments previously described. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they will be subjected to uninterrupted suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that place of hell."
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from the distant past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will constantly be deceived and deluded by others, and all of one's wealth and possessions will be perpetually plundered by others. Subject to such afflictions, having acquired wealth, it is lost again, and one is distrusted by all people—this is the residual retribution of that evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the Great Screaming Great Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows that there is another distinct place called the Vajra-beaked Crows; this is the thirteenth location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:

if there are certain people who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink alcohol, and further practice and frequently commit false speech, they will fall into that hell and be born in a distinct location known as the Place of the Vajra-beaked Crows.
All the sufferings experienced in those previous hells, such as Saṃjīva and the others, are experienced here in their entirety.
The karmic actions and their retributions for killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking intoxicants are as previously described.
Now, false speech is explained as follows:

if a person, within the midst of the Sangha, promises to provide a sick person with medicine according to their ailment but subsequently fails to do so, that person, by reason of this evil karmic cause, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, falls into an evil destination. They are born in a distinct location within that hell known as the Diamond-Billed Crows, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:
although one has originally vowed not to commit evil deeds, vultures with diamond-like beaks peck at and devour the flesh of one’s body.

Once they have pecked away the flesh, it grows back again exactly where it was pecked; as it grows, it becomes soft and tender like a lotus flower, and because of this tenderness, one undergoes extreme great suffering.
In this manner they peck again; once pecked, the flesh grows back, even more tender than before, and they are pecked yet again, so that their suffering increases further.
Thus those hell-beings are devoured by the crows for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years.

Once released from that place, they are born in succession within iron sand blazing with fierce flames; as those hell-beings tread upon the hot sand, they are scorched by it until not even ashes can be found of any part of their bodies.
Furthermore, it grows back again, and he eats his own tongue; once eaten, it grows back again;
having been eaten and grown back again, because of the falsehoods of his tongue, it is devoured by others.
"Because that person who speaks falsehoods speaks with lies, they shall in turn consume their own tongue.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"The nectar of immortality and the poisonous drug Both reside within the human tongue."
Truthful speech becomes nectar; false speech is poison.
If a person requires nectar, that person abides in truthful speech;
if a person requires poison, that person speaks falsely.
Poison does not necessarily cause death, but lying is certain;
if a person speaks falsely, they are called a "dead man.
Lying brings no benefit to oneself, nor does it profit others.
If neither self nor others find pleasure in it, why speak such false words?
If a person makes evil discriminations and delights in speaking falsehoods,
they will fly down onto flaming blades and undergo such suffering.
Though poison is extremely evil, it can kill but a single body;
the evil karma of false speech destroys hundreds of thousands of bodies.
The wise speak words of truth; this is the true Dharma for ordinary people.
Morality is the adornment of a person; it can show the path to liberation.
Sentient beings create their own karma and are drifted by the waters of craving;
the Well-Gone One (Sugata) speaks words of truth, serving as the supreme boat and raft.
The world, without beginning or end, is bound by the snare of craving;
only the Truth can rescue and liberate it—thus has the Lord of Dharma spoken.
Truth alone can sever the afflictions, just as an axe can hew down a tree.
Though one may be cut by sword or axe, one remains alive; By speaking truth, one is not thus destroyed.
Truth benefits both worlds; Therefore, it is said that truth is inexhaustible wealth.
Its source cannot be exhausted, And among all dharmas, it is supreme.
It is said that this true merit can produce the fruit of great bliss;
therefore, the wise abandon false speech, for those who see with truth all abandon it.

"Those who abandon truthful speech are constantly burned and constantly devoured by vultures with vajra-beaks for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of the karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times."
When their evil karma is exhausted, they will finally be liberated from that place in hell.
If, due to the ripening of virtuous karma from long ago in a previous life, they are not reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

and if they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will frequently engage in strife, always suffer defeat, and their words will not be trusted by anyone in the world—this is the residual fruit of retribution for that evil karma.
“Those who are full of falsehood and untruthfulness go to the wretched place of the hell of extreme suffering and undergo its evil retribution.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, contemplates the great hell of Raurava: what other places are there?”
He perceives through seeing, hearing, and knowledge:
there is another place called the Fire-Wreath Place (*agnimālā-sthāna*), which is the fourteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees: there are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, and drink intoxicants; their actions and karmic retributions are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is false speech, namely:
Suppose there is a person who violates regulations and breaks the law during an auspicious assembly, and everyone says,
"You have committed an offense.
Fearing punishment, that person speaks falsely, saying:
"I truly have committed no offense.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person's body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination and are born in the Fire-Garland section of that hell, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering, as previously described, all the agonies experienced in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are fully endured here.
Furthermore, there are even more severe ones, namely:

iron plates blaze with fierce flames; the Yama-wardens seize the hell-beings and place them upon these iron plates, then lay another iron plate over the offenders and rub them with great force until their entire bodies become a mire of flesh and blood, their color intensely red like that of the *kiṃśuka*, the flaming-red tree.
It is because they were pressed by iron plates that they have become thus.
When those Yama-wardens of the hell lift away the iron plates, the marrow, fat, blood, and flesh of those hell-beings completely cover their bodies.

Having already undergone this suffering, they therefore feel great terror toward those Yama-wardens; fleeing toward another place in hope of rescue and refuge, they see a great river which, when they are experiencing such pain, is filled with hot ashes.
Because they were struck with terror by the Yama-wardens who had previously inflicted suffering upon them, they plunged straight into that river.
Once they have entered the river, all their limbs, joints, and constituent parts completely melt away like lumps of fresh butter; yet they do not die, due to the power of their evil karma.

In that hellish place, the bamboo groves are dense and entirely ablaze; yet, just as when a great wind arises in the human world and fire burns a dry forest without burning the sentient beings within it, so it is there.
In that place of Fire-Garlands, sentient beings fill the space, scorched and ablaze; there is not even a spot the size of a needle’s head that is not burning.
Being thus scorched and boiled, they cry out with loud voices, running in all directions, seeking rescue and seeking refuge.
As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is fully exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish realm.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one's speech will be slow, difficult to understand, and incorrect. Even within one's own family circle, one cannot clearly comprehend even a few words, let alone speak skillfully in a great assembly; this is the residual karmic retribution of that former evil deed.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the Great Screaming Great Hell: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Receiving the Pain of Sharp Blades; this is the fifteenth location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, and drink intoxicants; their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is false speech, namely:

someone first forms a thought in their mind and, regarding whatever object—whether much or little—promises to give it to the Buddha, the Sangha, or within the Dharma; yet at a later time, they say again:
"I truly did not promise."
If the community of monks constantly harbors expectations and later does not grant them what was promised, it obstructs and hinders the community;
if one promises something to others and then fails to give it, it creates an obstacle for them.

That person who speaks falsely accumulates sinful karma; when the body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination and undergo great suffering in that hell known as the Place of Sharp Torments.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies suffered in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are experienced here in their entirety.
Furthermore, there is something even more severe:

namely, that place has hot iron needles with fine, long points, blazing and extremely sharp; the *Yama* wardens seize these sharp needles and pierce those sinners. Thus, the sinners undergo every kind of suffering and cry out with loud screams.
Once they have cried out loudly, needles fill their mouths, piercing both the lips and the tongue together, just like arrows inserted into a quiver.
Having undergone this suffering, they are unable to call out or to weep.

The suffering from such needle-points that he undergoes is unsurpassed and has no equal; having obtained such suffering through the false speech of his own mind, because he deceived both himself and others, he suffers in hell with the points of all his limbs standing upright, as numerous as the roots of body hairs, such that his entire body is utterly destroyed.

Once that person suffering has endured the pain of the blades, they lean and fall; as they lean and fall to the ground in this manner, the many needles pierce them in competition. Thus the person undergoes further needle-pain and becomes increasingly breathless; though they strive to cry out, they cannot produce a sound. If the needles were pulled out, they would be able to call out, but as long as the needles are not removed, they cannot make a sound.
Having already undergone such suffering, they lie upon the ground of glowing-hot iron; they writhe and toss about, rising only to fall again, agitated without ceasing.
The henchmen of Yama, wielding great axes, as well as iron mallets, iron shackles, and iron pestles, hack, pierce, strike, and beat them.

Thus they undergo great suffering and affliction for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of years, consuming the retribution of their evil karma of false speech. As long as that evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times;
only when the evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will be impoverished and afflicted by suffering. Whatever words one speaks will not be trusted or accepted by others; one must beg everywhere, and even when given permission, nothing is granted. That person thus becomes extremely destitute—this is the residual fruit and retribution of that former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, contemplates the great hell of Great Screaming (Mahāraurava): what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Endless Suffering (Anantaduḥkha), which is the sixteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who commit killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and drinking intoxicants; their actions and the resulting retributions are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is false speech, namely:
when many people are at sea seeking their livelihood, the guide conspires with bandits. Those bandits say to the guide:
"Do not take that path; you should travel by this road so that we may obtain goods and share them with you."
Those merchants said to the guide, "Lead us to the place where the treasures are;
we shall give you your reward. The guide replied:
"I shall do so! I shall do so! they promised with firm resolve;
yet that guide led the merchants away from the path to the jewels and set out upon a road to the bandits.
The bandits had previously devised a plan: they erected poles and hung banners, those banners being blue in color. When the guides saw them, they did not mention the presence of the bandits.
Upon seeing the blue banners, the merchants asked the guides, "Where there is that blue banner, there must be bandits."
The guide replied that they were not thieves; believing his words to be true, the merchants offered no defense or protection.
Once they reached the place of the bandits, all their wealth was plundered by the robbers, and the guide took his share as well.

Due to these causes and conditions of the evil karma of false speech, when his body perishes and his life ends, he falls into an evil destination; born in a distinct location within that hell, he undergoes boundless suffering and experiences great torment.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies endured in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are experienced here in their entirety.
Furthermore, there are even more severe ones, namely:
the Yama-wardens use hot, flaming iron tongs to pull out the tongues; once pulled out, they immediately grow back, and being soft and tender, they are pulled out yet again.
Furthermore, there are those who pluck out their eyes with tongs; once plucked, they grow back again, and as soon as they have become soft and tender, they are plucked out once more.
Others have their bodies shaved all over with knives that are extremely thin and sharp, like hair-shaving razors.
In that place there are worms called "Severing Worms" (Cheda-kīṭa) which further devour their intestines.

Within that hell there is another distinct place where the ground is entirely blue and pitch black. When the sinners enter therein, due to their evil karma, makara fish with fire burning both inside and out devour those sinners.
Those makara fish have mouths of vajra-flame, claws of vajra-flame, and teeth of vajra-flame; they seize and bite the sinners, shattering and pulverizing every part of their bodies.

If they escape from the fish's mouth, they enter its belly; within that belly, which is ablaze with flames, they remain for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of years, constantly being burned. Their breath is either stifled or scant, and they are constantly scorched and boiled, undergoing harsh and agonizing suffering. This is the result of the evil karma created by their past false speech.

Because that tongue of his was the cause of his false speech, he is intensely scorched within the belly of a makara fish, his body destroyed; thereafter, he is again burned by the fires of hell, and subsequently burned once more by blue flames.
"Once they have been thus burned, the Yama-wardens further address them with verses, rebuking them as follows:
'The utterance of false speech is the cause and condition for this hell.
Since you have already created these causes and conditions in the past, what benefit is there in your wailing and crying out? "
False speech is the foremost fire; it can even consume the great ocean, let alone the person who speaks falsely, just as one burns grass and wood.
If a person abandons truthful speech and utters falsehoods, [they are consumed by their own words].
Thus do these foolish and evil people discard jewels to take up stones.
If one does not love oneself but loves hell,
one will burn one's own body here by the fire of one's own false speech.
Truthful speech is very easy to obtain, adorning all people;
yet abandoning truthful speech to speak falsely, one reaches this state through delusion.
Among all virtues, truth is supreme; it is nectar within the midst of poison.
How deluded is he who abandons merit only to take up poison within poison?
Committing transgressions, he reaps evil fruits and dwells perpetually in hell;
ruining his own merit, he arrives at the most wretched hells.
The wise declare that false speech is the seed of all suffering, while the root of happiness is foremost in truth; therefore, one should not speak falsely.
One who speaks words of truth is beloved by all people.
False speech is disliked by all; therefore, one should not speak falsely.
If a person speaks the truth, they will always be joyful like the gods;
if a person speaks falsely, they will constantly suffer the pains of hell.
If one does not perform wholesome deeds, but instead commits immeasurable kinds of evil, one will undergo immeasurable suffering and affliction; what can regret avail now?
Wholesome fruits are obtained from wholesome actions; by committing evil, one receives evil retribution.
The wise person abandons evil and delights in practicing the Dharma.
Truth is the foremost good; falsehood is the foremost evil.
He who abandons faults and adopts merit is the most excellent among men.
"Once the Yama-wardens have thus rebuked the hell-beings, they further inflict upon them various immeasurable sufferings.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of years, until their evil karma is exhausted, their strength is gone, and they are utterly decayed and extinguished, they finally gain release from that place of hell."
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will be poor and constantly distressed, always living in fear of others, becoming either a slave or a laborer, lowly among men, and such that no one believes or accepts one’s words.
Due to the causes and conditions of that karma, they constantly undergo suffering and affliction;
this is the fruit of false speech, contrasted with truthful speech.
*Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna Sūtra*, Scroll Nine [and] Scroll Ten.
Translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Chapter on the Hells, Part Six:
"Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, contemplates the great hell of Raurava; what other places are there?"
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called Blood-and-Marrow-Eater, which is the seventeenth location of that hell.
By what karma do sentient beings take birth in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:
if a person commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, or drinking intoxicants, their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is the accumulation of evil karma through false speech, namely:

When kings, royal officials, or village headmen who hold positions of authority have already collected taxes and tributes, yet later claim they are insufficient and take more, or take in excess, they violate the ancient laws of the king.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, remaining in that hell known as the Place of Consuming Blood and Marrow, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies found within the various hells such as Sañjīva and Kālasūtra are experienced here in their entirety.
Furthermore, there is another [type of] superior [suffering], namely:

at that place, the leaves of the trees are ablaze with flames. The Yama-wardens bind those sinners with flaming iron ropes and suspend them from those trees with their heads downward and feet upward. There are crows with diamond-beaks and diamond-claws that first devour their feet; the blood flows from the feet and enters their mouths. Those hell-beings then consume it themselves, yet they never die.
Why is this? Among all forms of suffering, the suffering of hunger is the greatest; it is proclaimed everywhere, known by all, and recited by all.
Those who drink their own blood undergo two kinds of suffering: having already endured great agony, they further endure the suffering of hunger.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"The suffering of being burned by a hot wind, or of fire fanned by the wind,
is not like the exceedingly heavy suffering of hunger and thirst caused by the winds of karma."

"Those hell-beings thus consume their own blood and marrow for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years, with their heads and faces downward, being scorched by the foremost fire. For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years, at all times, they are constantly burned and boiled in that hellish place. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of the karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally escape from that hellish place."
If, due to the ripening of virtuous karma from a long time past in previous lives, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;
yet if one is born among humans in a place of common karma, one will be poor and afflicted, distrusted by others, with blood constantly flowing from the nose even while chewing a tooth-stick.
Blood constantly flows from their noses and between their teeth; this is the residual karmic retribution of that hell.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the Great Screaming Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He perceives through seeing, hearing, and knowledge:
there is another place called Eleven Flames, which is the eighteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:
as for those persons who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, and drink intoxicants, their actions and their karmic results are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is false speech, namely:

when a king, one equal to a king, or a trustworthy person capable of adjudicating matters—whether as a householder or otherwise—acts as a judge in a dispute between two individuals or between two opposing factions.

Whether for the sake of seizing property, out of familiarity with someone, or driven by desire or anger, they speak falsely by making arbitrary judgments according to their own whims rather than relying on reason.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body breaks up at the end of life, they fall into an evil destination and undergo great suffering in the eleventh burning place of that hell.
As for what is called suffering, as previously described, all the agonies experienced in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are fully endured here, ten times more intense.
Associating with those who speak falsehoods is even more grave. Why is it grave?
Because of their evil karma.
In the eleven realms of heat, masses of fire arise; the ten directions constitute ten, and internal hunger and thirst constitute the eleventh.
With this internal fire of hunger and thirst, flames issue from the mouth.

That person who speaks falsehoods has a tongue that is a companion to lying; because of this evil karma, their tongue is burned moment by moment. Once burned, it grows back again, and they undergo the suffering of having their tongue burned. The suffering of being burned on the tongue is such that the suffering of the ten masses of fire does not equal even one-sixteenth part of it.
Due to their evil karma, they undergo this suffering of the tongue.

Those hell-beings endure such extreme and heavy torments from eleven clusters of flames, being constantly burned and boiled for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer without ceasing at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.
If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long time past in a previous life, one is not born into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals;

yet, if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will constantly suffer from hunger and thirst, with all parts of the body perpetually scorched by heat. One will be impoverished and short-lived, and whatever words one speaks will not be trusted by others.

By nature, one will be extremely foolish, dull-witted, and ugly, with cracked hands and feet and tattered clothing, always wandering on roads, at crossroads, or at three-way junctions, constantly begging for alms.
If one constantly engages in livelihood by selling lowly and base goods;
from birth until death, one undergoes the foremost suffering;
and amidst disputes and contention, one always falls on the side of the defeated.
This is the residual fruit of that evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the location of the Great Shouting Hell and sees that there is no other place besides this one.

Furthermore, the practitioner reflects within the mind—contemplating the course of phenomena in accordance with the True Dharma—and sees that bhikṣu desiring to enter the path of nirvāṇa, which is tranquil, free from aging, death, exhaustion, and cessation.

When the yakṣas of that earth see that bhikṣu’s diligent application of energy, their hearts are filled with great joy, and they pass the news upward to the yakṣas of the void. The yakṣas of the void transmit it in this same sequence down to the Parīttābha Heaven, where they speak these words:

"In Jambudvīpa, a person of such-and-such a clan—speaking briefly—has proceeded through the stages until attaining the tenth bhūmi; his mind takes no pleasure in dwelling within the realm of Māra, nor does he delight in acting in concert with craving, having abandoned all defiled dharmas."
Having heard this, the gods of Limited Light were filled with joy and said:
"The faction of Māra is diminished, and the assembly of the True Dharma increases.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, diligently severs the fetters of birth and death in the world, reflecting in this way:

These sentient beings undergo great suffering and affliction; deceived by craving and bound by the fetters of ignorance, they are conjoined with the mental formations and are boiled throughout the three periods of time, yet have no desire to sever the cycle of birth and death.
How could these sentient beings be without minds? If they possess minds, they must possess cognition; if they possess cognition, why do they not abandon desire?

Furthermore, if sentient beings who have long experienced superior pleasures in the celestial realms still manage to abandon desire, how much more so should those in hell, who have long endured great suffering, not abandon it?

The minds of those sentient beings are thus hardened; they undergo all such immeasurable and manifold sufferings without weariness, and they sleep through the long night without awakening. Such a mind has five kinds of faults, which are immeasurable: namely, old age, sickness, death, union with the disliked, and separation from the beloved.
"Furthermore, there are ten kinds of suffering and affliction.

These ten are: the affliction of hunger and thirst; the affliction of separation from what is loved; the affliction of strife and contention between various lands; the affliction of decline and rebirth; the affliction of being reviled by others; the affliction of seeking from others; the affliction of cold and heat; the affliction of two people hating one another and fighting together; the affliction of losing wealth; and the affliction of not obtaining that which is sought in one's thoughts."
Thus, in brief, it is said that the mind has these ten kinds of afflictions.
Although the minds of sentient beings undergo such manifold afflictions, they still do not abandon desire; these sentient beings have been deceived by a spirit of enmity since beginningless time.

Such a mind is constantly shifting and never remains still; it is without ears or heart, like a stone or a vajra. It creates obstacles even in places of great auspiciousness; it does not abide in the True Dharma, finds no joy therein, and is thirsty at all times. It is never satiated by the objects of the senses—forms, sounds, smells, touches, and tastes—which are like poison, swords, and fire. These five objects are poisons and the six sense bases are great thieves. It is unaware of the seven factors of enlightenment, does not patiently endure the eightfold noble path, and furthermore, it knows nothing of the nine abodes of sentient beings, nor even the ten paths of wholesome action.

One cannot contemplate the eleven stages (*bhūmi*); one cannot truly know the arising, abiding, and ceasing of the twelve sense bases (*āyatana*); one cannot contemplate the thirteen stages above; the fourteen mental objects (*ālambana*) constantly follow one another; one does not contemplate the seventeen defiled minds (*citta-kleśa*); the eighteen sensations (*vedanā*) flow through perforations; one cannot endure the nineteen formations (*saṃskāra*) and fifteen conditions (*pratyaya*); and the sixteen evil actions combine and correspond, flowing through perforations toward the twenty proximate locations.
"In those twenty directions, his mind constantly wanders in distraction.
Having thus observed the mind, the bhikṣu gives rise to a heart of compassion for those sentient beings and contemplates with careful scrutiny the law of karmic retribution."
Furthermore, as that bhikṣu practices with such diligence, he gives rise once more to the resolve to sever the bonds of Māra, reflecting thus:
"Might there be even more superior hells?"

He sees, hears, and knows that there are yet other even more superior great hells, ten times more terrible than the Great Howling Great Hell, characterized by the suffering of evil karma and extremely fierce power, named the Intensely Heating Hell, which consists of sixteen locations.
What are the sixteen?
First is named Mahāpradīpta;
second is named Pāṭalika.
The third is named Dragon-Spinning;
the fourth is named Red-Copper Mīṇi-Fish-Spinning;
the fifth is named Iron Cauldron.
Sixth is named Drifting in a River of Blood;
seventh is named Abounding with Marrow-Bone Worms;
eighth is named All Humans Matured.
The ninth is named Endless Descent;
the tenth is named Great Padma;
the eleventh is named Malevolent Precipice.
Twelfth is named Vajra-Bone;
thirteenth is named Black-Iron-Rope-Slicing-Blade-Unbinding-Suffering;
fourteenth is named Nāga-Worm-Pillar-Malicious-Fire-Suffering.
The fifteenth is named Darkness-Fire Wind;
the sixteenth is named Vajra-Mouth Bee.
These are the sixteen subsidiary locations of the Great Hell of Intense Heat, where the lifespan in that great hell is so long as to be beyond calculation.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that hell?
He knows through seeing and hearing:

if a person is firm and grave in their practice of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking alcohol, and speaking falsehoods; and furthermore, possesses wrong views, delighting in and frequently committing these acts, such that their evil karma is pervasive and they persist in its performance until it is complete.
Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body breaks up and life ends, they fall into the Great Hell of Intense Heat (Pratāpana).
The karmic actions of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying, along with their retributions, are as previously described.
Now, the false views are explained:
If a person holds false views, delights in practicing them, and frequently acts upon them, they will say to others:
"In this world there is no giving, no sacrifice, no merit, no evil, and no karmic retribution; there is no present world and no future world; there is neither father nor mother."

Having thus spoken such nihilistic views, one loses the fruit of one's own practice; yet one speaks to others, establishes them therein, and rejoices with them, thereby increasing their own wrong views by saying:
"There is no cause, no karma, and no path."
"Such a person, though possessing the outward form and robes [of a monk], is in fact a great thief.

Due to the causal conditions of such evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, undergoing great suffering and affliction within the Great Hell of Intense Heat."
That person who does not believe in the reality of karmic retribution for one's actions,
when approaching death and before reaching the intermediate state (*antarābhava*), already perceives evil omens; that is to say, while ill,
they see within their own eyes a perilous and dark place filled with many lions, tigers, snakes, bears, and brown bears, as large as mountains.
Having seen this, he was struck with great terror; seeing those fierce beasts swiftly approaching him, they drew near his body without ceasing their rapid advance.
Hearing the roars of those lions, tigers, and other predators, the gravely ill man was seized by great fear, and he was overcome with grief, suffering, and distress.
Furthermore, he sees other people with wrinkled faces and distorted mouths; he also sees black fire above them and hears jackals howling with various sounds.
Moreover, he again sees the henchmen of Yama assuming various terrifying forms, which gives rise to great fear.

The speech uttered by those people of false doctrine—who speak of evil causes, who speak of evil companions, who speak of evil views, who speak of evil dharmas, and who delight in speaking of those who do not believe in the ripening of karma—is that which falls into the precipice of an evil state.
Because they have deceived both themselves and others, these people have committed the greatest evil karma. Having delighted in such actions and performed them repeatedly, they have accumulated them;

when the time comes for the fruit to ripen, they see such inauspicious shadows and signs, giving rise to great terror. Their faculties tremble, their physical features manifest outwardly, and they lose control of their bowels and bladder. They may groan, yet their voices fail to emerge as they choke; or they may wrinkle their faces, gape their mouths, or clutch and drag at the bedding with their hands.
Or they may see themselves falling from a mountain peak to the ground. Having seen this, they wish to push away [the vision] with their hands. When the caregivers observe this, they speak as follows:
"Thus, the sick person is like one grasping at empty space.
In this way, the patient may see themselves about to fall, and rubs all parts of their body with their hands.

Thus, those who practice such evil deeds with wrong views do not give rise to faith in the retribution of karmic results; various signs of the retribution they will undergo in hell appear before them, like a heap of excrement whose stench is smelled even before one has reached it.

In this way, even before reaching the hells, one perceives the signs of rebirth in the evil places of hell and experiences extreme terror; all those with wrong views who lack faith are likewise struck with such dread.
Foolish people accumulate evil karma; with the price of unwholesome karma, they purchase the wealth of hellish suffering and undergo retribution there.

In such hells, there are many fierce winds, namely the slanting wind and the *bipala* wind. These winds are harsh and sharp; when they strike their bodies, they beat and split them apart. These winds are violent and malevolent, causing them to experience two kinds of suffering: those of body and mind.

As this body is about to perish and one is on the verge of entering the intermediate state (*antarābhava*), at the final moment of life, the mind is unable to take hold of wholesome phenomena (*kuśaladharma*).

Such a person of wrong views passes through the human world in vain, gaining no benefit. While in the intermediate state, before yet entering hell, the signs of hell appear—brought about by the evil karma of their own wrong views. Their minds tremble and quiver as they encounter all manner of undesirable forms, sounds, tangibles, tastes, and smells. They hear the cries of the sinners in hell, which are unpleasant, terrifying, and fearsome; they are touched by a foul wind like an extremely sharp blade; they experience an intensely bitter taste; and they see the color of foul flames and smell a putrid stench.
That person experiences great terror toward all such objects and their mind is filled with extreme alarm and fear.

Because this evil person has preached the Dharma in a perverted manner, through the power of his evil karma he perceives the forms of the hells as entirely inverted; thus, seeing the hells as adorned with exquisite beauty, he conceives an intense attachment to hell and gives rise to the longing:
"How may I now be born in that place?"

That person of wrong views does not experience suffering within the intermediate state (*antarābhava*); rather, they must be born in hell. Because they grasp the causes and conditions for birth, they are born within hell; as soon as they grasp [the new existence], they are born, with no interval in between.

Once born in that place, at the very moment of birth, they experience all the various sufferings of the Saṃjīva and other hells as previously described; yet here they undergo every one of those sufferings ten times more intensely. The four hundred and four diseases are like the most extreme evils found in the hells, beyond all comparison; among all fears, this fear is the most supreme, for the retribution of evil karma is entirely equal [to its cause].

A single spark of fire, even a wicked flame the size of a sesame seed, if placed in a mountain forest, a kingdom, or a continent, can swiftly burn up all of Jambudvīpa; how much more so the bodies of those suffering retribution in the hells?
Thus, this evil fire burns the bodies of the sinners like lumps of fresh butter; once melted, they are born again.
In that place of great darkness, there is no distinction between day and night, and this continues for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years.

Within the ocean of suffering and amidst all forms of darkness, false views are the darkest; having accumulated [karma] through such views, one obtains such a fruit as this: for incalculable years and throughout vast expanses of time, one is constantly burned and boiled, experiencing sufferings that are beyond analogy.

Experiencing such suffering at all times, they remain there until their evil karma is exhausted, their vital energy is spent, and they have completely withered and perished; only then do they escape from that hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that, they will be born among the hungry ghosts for five hundred lifetimes, known as the "yellow hungry ghosts.
Having been liberated from that state, those people will then be born among animals of great suffering and affliction for five hundred lifetimes.
Having been liberated from that place, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a floating yoke.

If, due to the ripening of wholesome karma from a long-past previous life, one is born among humans, one will be born in a frontier region among the Mlecchas; one will be constantly ill and constantly poor, blind, short-lived, and whatever words one speaks will not be trusted by others—this is the remaining karmic retribution of those wrong views.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, next contemplates the Great Hell of Intense Heat (Pratapana) to see what distinct locations it contains.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is a distinct location called the Place of Great Burning (Mahāpradīpana), which is the first distinct location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:
if a person commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, or speaking falsehoods—their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is wrong view, which one delights in practicing and frequently commits, resulting in the fruit of unwholesome karma. What is wrong view?
It refers to someone who holds such a view as this:
One may be born among the devas due to the causes and conditions of killing;
likewise, such evil karma results in an evil retribution. Why is this?
Among the various forms of suffering, the suffering of death is the most grave;
among the pleasures of all realms, celestial bliss is supreme.
Yet the karma of killing is not a cause for such bliss.
Since killing brings about suffering, it is not a cause of happiness.
Thus, having committed such karma that results in evil causes and effects, one preaches such false views to others; consequently, one reaps the fruits of evil karma and yet does not repent.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination and are born in the Great Burning Place within that hell, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies suffered in the Saṃjīva and other hells are experienced here in their entirety, ten times more intense.
Furthermore, there is something even more terrible:
due to their evil karma, fire erupts from their own bodies, and this fire is exceedingly hot.
Compared to the intensely hot great fire of this hell, the fires of all other hells constitute only a single sixteenth part.
To these hell-beings, the fires of all other hells appear like frost and snow.
While these hell-beings are already ablaze within and without, there is yet a third blazing fire: the fever of remorse in their hearts.
Thus, these ordinary beings are further tormented.

Those hell-beings recognize for themselves that this is the fruit of their wrong views, the retribution of their wrong views, and the bitter taste of their wrong views; because of those wrong views, they are thus scorched by fire, not obtaining even a single moment’s pleasure for even a brief instant.
Thus, this place within the Greatly Heating Great Hell is named the "Greatly Burning Place. Those who have practiced evil deeds through wrong views are boiled there for an exceedingly long time.
What constitutes such a long time?
No one knows their number.

Those hell-beings are at all times burned, boiled, and disintegrated; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they are incessantly subjected to suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that place of hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, they will be born among hungry ghosts for three hundred lifetimes, and among animals for two hundred lifetimes.

Having been liberated from those places, if they are born among humans in a realm of similar karma, they will show no respect toward their parents; they will be devoid of shame (*hrī*) and dread of blame (*apatrāpya*), lacking both modesty and decorum. They will eat human excrement and filth, wandering everywhere through various lands while remaining far removed from hearing the True Dharma. Despised and loathed by all people, they will eat with dogs and walk with dogs; their hands and feet will be coarse and twisted, and they will constantly depend on the food of others, passing their entire lives empty and devoid of merit.
After casting off this body, they will successively enter undesirable realms, as previously described for those of wrong views who dwell in the unlovely lower and middle states.

Having thus observed, that bhikṣu rejoices in right view and contemplates with right intention; he practices the Noble Path, attains the practice leading to nirvāṇa, and engages in corresponding contemplation.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist there.
He perceives through hearing and knowledge that there is another distinct place called Piṇḍaka, which is the second secondary location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:

if a person habitually practices and frequently commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying—their karma and its retribution being as previously described—and furthermore holds wrong views, practicing and frequently committing such things as these:

There is a person who starves himself to death in the hope of being reborn in heaven; such a person further teaches others, or rejoices in the actions of others, causing them to abide in wrong views. Bound by evil causes, with an evil mind and evil reflections, he composes evil treatises and further teaches others to abide in those evil treatises. That person thus dies of starvation.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination and are born in a specific section of that hell called Caṇḍālika, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies suffered in the Saṃjīva and other hells are experienced here in their entirety, doubled and even more intense.
Furthermore, there is something even more extraordinary:

throughout the entire body of that person, a garland of flames burns without interruption. In every part of this sinner’s body, there is not even a space the size of a mustard seed where there is no fire or where the flames do not burn. Because the cause and effect correspond to his evil karma, the heat of the fire is so intensely fierce that it is beyond all comparison; nothing can be likened to it.
Just as that wrong view is the most evil among all karmas, so too is its fire extremely hot; among all fires, this fire is the hottest.
All evil karmas yield results that correspond to them; therefore, that fire is beyond analogy, as nothing can truly resemble it.
By the power of that karma, it burns constantly at all times without ceasing.
Having been thus burned, they again see fully blossomed *campaka* flowers, immeasurable flocks of birds, and delightful pools and streams filled with pure water.
Other hell-beings speak thus:
"Run here quickly! Run here quickly!"
"In this place of ours, there is a *pāṇḍavaka* grove; the pool and forest are pure and soft, with water to drink, and the cool shade of the trees is nearby.
Those hell-beings call out to the person of wrong views to comfort him, and they follow one another as they run toward the location of the *pāṇḍavaka* pool and forest.
As they run in this manner, the path is strewn with glowing embers, and upon the road there are pits filled with blazing fire.
Once the offenders have entered, every part of their bodies is completely consumed by the flames.
Having been burned, they are born again; having been born, they are burned again.
Thirsting to drink water, they run without ceasing.

As they run thus, *vīṭaraga* staffs grow upon the path; these staffs possess flaming tongues that twist and wring the offenders, causing sores to break out over their entire bodies until the marrow is completely exhausted. Once it is exhausted, it grows back again.

Driven by heat and thirst, he still runs toward the waters and groves of the Puṇḍarīka lake; yet, due to his evil karma, there are flesh-eating insects all over his body that peck at his two eyes and devour them.
Having pecked, it grows back again; once grown, it pecks again.

That person, being sightless and tormented by heat and thirst, runs toward the Pundarīka lotus pond, its waters, and its groves of trees. Furthermore, different insects are born upon his body, and as all parts of that blind man’s limbs are devoured by these insects, he cries out with a loud scream.
Furthermore, as their eyes grow, worms again peck and devour them.
In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they eat and then the eyes grow again; once grown, they are eaten again.
If they run toward the waters and groves of the Puṇḍarīka pond, having reached that place, they hope for coolness and enter forward.

Having entered that place, there is a *tāla* tree ablaze with a towering fire five hundred *yojanas* high; deceived by their own evil karma, those hell-beings each ascend the *tāla* tree individually.
Once they have climbed the tree, their entire bodies are enveloped by many garlands of flames. Having thus ascended, they undergo the most supreme, evil, and extreme suffering.

Tormented by hunger and thirst, they are scorched by the blazing fires there, which are the color of *pāṇḍarīka* flowers; burned and roasted by those fires, they die and are revived again. All parts of their bodies are completely consumed until they resemble the color of the *cāmpeya* tree, and at all times they endure great agony.
As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decomposed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they will experience unceasing suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
Once liberated from that, they are born among hungry ghosts for four hundred lifetimes, experiencing the suffering of hunger and thirst.
Once liberated from that, they are born among animals for three hundred lifetimes.
Once they have attained liberation, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a floating yoke with a single hole.

If they are born among humans in a place of common karma, those people will be born in lands where there is fear of swords and iron, scarcity, bandits, and many wicked people; furthermore, in their place of birth, they will always be poor and constantly ill, serving as lowly slaves with incomplete faculties.
