"This is the residual karmic retribution for those wrong views, evil conduct, and evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist there."
He sees, hears, and knows:
furthermore, there is another place called Dragon-Spiral (*nāga-āvarta*), which is the third distinct location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:
if a person habitually engages in and frequently commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying—their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there are those with wrong views who delight in and frequently practice such things as these:

namely, there are people whose physical appearance is improper; some always slouch and never sit upright; some always keep their palms joined, some always rest their cheeks on their hands, and some always lick their fingers while eating. Among such various followers of external paths, there are those who say:
"To attain nirvana by severing desire, hatred, and delusion—that is not so."
"Even the faculty of tranquility cannot be attained.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person's body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination; born in the Dragon-Spinning region of that hell, they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:
in that place there are many fierce-headed, evil nāgas, full of wrath and intense venom, residing in that hell.

The bodies of those nāgas measure one *krośa* or one *yojana*; their malignant poison blazes fiercely over their entire bodies. Some possess poison in their gaze, some in their touch, and some in their fangs; they fill that hell.
Those hell-beings are born among a multitude of nāgas; the nāgas revolve around and crush them until they are ground as fine as flour balls.

Furthermore, there are those born within the mouths of the nāgas; their venomous fangs, ablaze with fire, chew rapidly and continuously—countless times, even hundreds of thousands of times. Having died, they are born again; having been born, they are chewed again; having been chewed, they die again; having died, they are born again.
Those sinful persons are burned by three kinds of fires:
first, the fire of poison;
second, the fire of hell.
Third, the fire of hunger and thirst.
Those sinners are born into these three fires and undergo harsh and rigid suffering corresponding to their own karma;
furthermore, they are boiled by a fourth fire of disease, the heavy affliction of which cannot be fully described.

Thus, these sinful persons who have committed evil deeds are constantly born within fire at all times; they are burned, boiled, crushed, ground, dried, and scattered until their evil karma is exhausted, they lose their vitality, and they rot away and perish, only then attaining liberation from that place of hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that, they are born for one hundred and fifty lifetimes among the hungry ghosts with needle-like throats;

for two hundred lifetimes they are born among animals, their bodies scorched by hunger and thirst, deprived of water and finding no water, taking on the forms of lions, tigers, bears, brown bears, and the like, dwelling in wildernesses twelve *yojanas* wide where there is no water.
Once they have escaped [that state], it is as difficult to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a floating log.
Even if they are born among humans, they become wild folk who do not even see food with their eyes, let alone eat it.
They subsist solely by eating medicinal herbs, various fruits, and the like.
This is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called the Copper-Red Mīṇi-whirlpool, which is the fourth separate section of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:
if a person delights in and frequently commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying— specifically,
claiming that all living and non-living things in the world have no life-force and that everything is merely an emanation created by Maheśvara, rather than the fruit of karma.

By reason of these evil karmic causes and conditions, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination and are born in the *Tāmra-mṛttikā-āvarta* (Copper-clay Whirlpool) section of that hell, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:

in that place of hell, molten copper with blazing flames fills the area like a sea; within it dwell many iron *miṇa* fish produced by their own evil karma, and there are also tree leaves as sharp as razors.

Those born in the various hells of the Tāmramṛttikāvarta (Copper-Clay Whirlpool) are reborn there; having been born, they die again, and having died, they are born again. All their limbs are completely shattered and decomposed, then they float up to the surface of the molten copper; having emerged, they sink back down, undergoing great torment as they run to and fro one another, crying out to each other in turn.

Those people of wrong views who preach with wrong views, having cried out and fled, are driven by their own evil karma; like the fierce Makara fish opening its jaws and rushing swiftly, they head toward the denizens of hell.
Once that fish arrives, it immediately captures and binds the sinner with a snare of saliva, causing him to enter its mouth; then, using its mechanical fangs, it grinds him to pieces.
With half of the sinner’s body inside the fish’s mouth and half outside, he is boiled in a seething cauldron of molten red copper, undergoing these two kinds of intense and agonizing suffering.
Thus that person remains half within the mouths of fish, constantly being chewed, and half in boiling molten red copper, for an incalculable period of time.
Once they have escaped from there, they enter yet another different pool of molten red copper.
Once they have entered that place, there are many malevolent insects with diamond-like beaks and extremely sharp fangs, possessing immeasurable, blazing venom.
These evil insects dwell in that dark place amidst molten red copper; they seize those sinners and chew them until they are broken apart, reducing them to powder like sand, and then devour them.
When those hell-beings, having already undergone such suffering, wish to cry out and open their mouths, molten red copper fills their mouths so that they cannot produce a sound.
That molten copper liquid fills his nine orifices; once filled, it boils intensely until all parts of his body are completely melted away.

Furthermore, in that place for a vast duration of time, he is boiled and sinks down; having sunk, he floats up again. Once he has floated up, due to the effects of his evil karma, many wind-blades, extremely venomous and sharp, crush and slice his body.

Those people who speak untruths, do not believe in the results of karma, and hold wrong views are constantly being burned, boiled, scattered, and destroyed at all times; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that, they will be born among hungry ghosts for three hundred lifetimes; those ghosts are named "Hopeful-Hopeful.

Once they have attained liberation from that, they will be born among animals for three hundred lifetimes, becoming elephants, bears, ants, and the like; they will constantly suffer from hunger and thirst, oppressed by cold and heat, blown upon by the wind and scorched by the sun, enduring what is unbearable.
Once they have been liberated from among those animals, it is as difficult for them to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a floating yoke with a single hole.

If, due to the ripening of virtuous karma from a long-past previous life, they are born among humans, they will dwell in places of constant fear and perilous evil, such as places where wood is constantly being cut or where fish are constantly caught; that they are perpetually beset by terror is the residual fruit of their former evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Iron Cauldron Place, which is the fifth secondary location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who commit killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying; their actions and the retribution thereof are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is a wrong view that one delights in practicing and frequently performing:

namely, when non-Buddhists with wrong views slaughter a man during a sacrificial rite and say, "I have now held this assembly and slaughtered this man; he shall be reborn in heaven, and I too shall be reborn in heaven."
"If he is reborn in heaven, let him serve as my witness.
Some take a turtle, kill it, and use it as a basis for their testimony that they will be reborn in heaven in a future life;
others again instruct another person, saying, "In one lifetime you were such-and-such, and your lineage was such-and-such."

Obstructing the right path and dwelling in false paths, such people of evil karma and wrong views, upon the dissolution of the body and the end of life, fall into an evil destination; they are born in that hell in the place of iron cauldrons, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering, as previously described, all the agonies suffered in the Saṃjīva and other hells are experienced here in their entirety, ten times more intense.
Furthermore, there are others who are more severe:
there are six iron cauldrons, each ten *yojanas* in measure. These six are so called because those within them undergo equal suffering, being powerless and without rescue;
their fires are perpetually boiling with heat.
The Saws-leafed Water;
the Razor-blade Garland;
and the Exceedingly Hot Boiling Water.
It abounds with many venomous snakes.
Regarding those who suffer equally in the powerless cauldron:

when the sinners enter it, they are gathered together in one place, forming a single mass like a ball of flour; being cooked, they are powerless, and as they are cooked again, they become even more powerless.

In such evil places, the body cannot save itself and the mind cannot save itself; likewise, those who are lawless in the evil realms have no dharma by which they may be saved. Being separated from those who could save them, and because there is no salvation, they are boiled for a long duration of time.
Regarding the "fire that is constantly boiling and hot iron cauldrons":

when sinners enter therein, they are boiled in the seething, molten red copper until their bodies disintegrate; even their ashes cannot be found. Once they have been entirely consumed, they are born again, and being born, they are constantly boiled.
As for those in the "Saw-Leaf Aquatic Hot Iron Cauldron":
when the sinner enters it, the water, the color of molten copper, saws his body apart; there, amidst the flames, he enters with his head downward.

Once they have entered that place, they either sink or float; they are constantly sawn apart, and their bodies are cut by boiling, molten copper which seeps through every fiber until they are split asunder. Having been thus cleft, they sink once more; having sunk, they rise again; and having risen, they sink yet again.

Thus, in this water of saws, they are constantly cut and split until they are all thoroughly cooked and rotten like ripe beans; their bodies are torn asunder, sometimes floating and sometimes sinking, being boiled, cut, and split for a long duration of time.
Regarding the "garland of extremely sharp blades" and the "hot iron cauldron":
when a sinner enters therein and undergoes suffering, there is a garland of sharp blades within that cauldron, as keen as a razor, which cleaves their body into pieces.
If one places a sinner in these two cauldrons filled with intensely boiling water and abounding with venomous snakes, the suffering endured by the sinner upon entering them is as follows:

there is boiling water that seethes violently, with froth rising half a *yojana* high. Within the froth dwell snakes with extremely fierce and sharp fangs; whether they touch or merely see them, all emit blazing fires that burn the hell-beings. To be touched is like being cut by a blade: the flesh is consumed until only bone remains. When boiled, they are cooked until their bodies are completely rotted away; as the boiling froth cooks them, their limbs and members are entirely melted.
If they are boiled in bitter poison within the water, they undergo the foremost suffering, a suffering that is rigid and heavy.
When the *yama* beings come to them, they form this thought:
"By what means can we block the opening of the cauldron so that those sinful persons cannot escape?"
The Yama-wardens then form this intention:
"We shall firmly block their mouths with vajras and press them together upon the ground so that they cannot flee; therein they shall fully undergo various kinds of suffering."

Once the Yama-wardens have formed this intention, all the iron cauldrons are turned upside down with their openings facing downward; furthermore, the flaming garlands of fire blaze twice as fiercely, and those hell-beings undergo such suffering.
The Yama-wardens, filled with extreme malice, further reflected:
"By what means can we inflict yet another distinct suffering upon them?
Having thus reflected, they again took up iron fuel that was ablaze with double-folded flames.

If those in the hells desire to move upward, they encounter boiling molten copper that clings to them one after another; some have their bodies shattered, while others have their bodies scorched by the venomous fire of snakes until they are completely cooked and rotten.

They constantly experience various kinds of suffering at all times; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they will suffer without ceasing at every moment.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally escape from within those heated iron cauldrons in that hellish realm.
Once they have attained liberation from that, they will be born among the hungry ghosts who feed on foul odors for three hundred lifetimes.
Having been liberated from there, they will be born among animals for three hundred lifetimes.
Having been liberated from that place, if they are born among humans in a realm of similar karma, they become teachers of deluded doctrines who propound false causes; their minds are inverted:
some, hoping for wealth and pleasure, do not eat for a month;
others, hoping to be reborn in heaven, do not eat for a day, bound as they are by the fetters of craving.
That person, being thus bound by suffering, undergoes further suffering in such and such ways; this is the remaining karmic retribution of that evil deed.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat (Tapana) to see what other places exist therein.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called Drifting in the River of Blood, which is the sixth secondary region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
Those sentient beings who possess wrong views and commit evil deeds are born in that place.
There they see people who violate the precepts; having committed many such transgressions, they think to themselves:
"If I practice asceticism, my sins will be extinguished and I shall gain great merit."

Having thought thus, that person enters a forest, hangs his feet from a tree with his head and face downward, and cuts his nose or his forehead with a knife so that a wound opens and blood flows; he then burns the blood with fire, hoping thereby to be reborn in heaven.
This is the conduct of the evil realms; it is like a person seeking oil from sand, who cannot obtain any oil, yet that person’s blood is exhausted until they meet their end.

Due to the causes and conditions of such evil karma, when their body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil place, remaining in that hell at the Place of Floating in Blood Rivers, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
Regarding what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies suffered in the Saṃjīva and other hells are experienced here in their entirety, five times more intense.
Furthermore, there is another superior [suffering], namely:

there, the henchmen of Yama hold flaming hammers, swords, and stones, which they scatter into powder; blood flows to form a river, and this river swiftly sweeps away other hell-beings, abounding with hair and bones.

Within that river, there is a second river of red copper called the Fearsome Putrid Water. In that river dwell worms known as Ball-Worms; their touch is like fire, and when they contact the sinners in that hell, they burn and devour them.
Thus, being swept away by the river of blood in that hell, they undergo great suffering for countless years over an immense duration of time.

In that place where they are swept by the river of blood, they constantly experience evil suffering at all times; thus, as long as the evil and unwholesome karma of those people with wrong views has not been destroyed or decomposed, and its potency has not been exhausted, they shall suffer without cessation at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish place.
Once they have attained liberation from that, for five hundred lifetimes they are born among the hungry ghosts (preta), sustaining their lives by eating smoke.

Once they have attained liberation from that, for four hundred lifetimes they are born among animals as sea-birds; or they are born on seashores or at river mouths, those birds having red heads, which is the remaining karmic fruit of their former deeds.
If they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will be poor and frequently ill; this is the residual retribution of their original evil karma.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist there.
He perceives through seeing, hearing, and knowledge that there is another distinct location, called the Abode of Marrow-Eating Worms; this is the seventh secondary region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:

if a person frequently commits evil and unwholesome deeds—unwholesome deeds of body, unwholesome deeds of speech, and unwholesome deeds of mind—and furthermore lacks correct hearing, such a deluded person hopes to be reborn in the Brahma world; yet his conduct is evil, he is devoid of precepts, and by nature he possesses no morality.
This deceitful person inflicts suffering upon others and is far removed from right precepts; he burns his own body with dry cow dung.

In this present life, that person’s body is scorched and he undergoes great suffering. Thus, burned by the fire of human beings, when his body perishes and his life ends, he falls into an evil destination—born in the hell-realm of the "Bone-Marrow Worms"—where he undergoes immense torment.
As for what is called suffering:

they are struck on their heads down to their feet with iron hammers, crying out with loud shrieks; all their limbs become like a mass of molten wax, indistinguishable from one another, yet they do not die, due to the power of that evil karma of wrong views.
That place of hell is three yojanas wide and five yojanas high; the bodies of the hell-beings there are likewise broad and long, filling it entirely to form a mountain of flesh.
In that hell region, there abound moisture-born insects, all of which are sentient beings.
By what karma are such insects produced?

If any man or any woman has had lice or other parasites on their own body or the bodies of others, and originally killed those insects—whether by killing ants, black insects, or the like, or by killing ticks—that person, through the causal conditions of this evil karma, at the dissolution of the body after death, is reborn as an insect in that place, known as a "mechanical insect" (*yantra-kīṭa*).

Thus these sinful worms are born upon that mountain; produced by their own karma and arising as the fruit of their own karma, because of their evil deeds, they are in this place of the Hell of Abundant Marrow-Bone Worms, where furthermore other Yama-wardens burn them with fire.

When that person with wrong views was formerly in the human realm, due to the karma of burning his body with dry cow dung, he is now burned together with the mechanical insects in one place, undergoing great suffering and affliction.
Once that mountain has been burned, flames rise up to a height of ten yojanas.
Due to their own karmic offenses, the inhabitants of that hell have their bodies scorched by the great fire; they are burned together with the *yantra-kīṭa* (mechanical worms) in one place.
While those worms have small bodies and thus suffer little, the inhabitants of that hell have massive bodies and consequently suffer greatly.
Those masses of flames burn one another for an immensely long duration, through countless years that can never be exhausted.
As long as that person’s karma of wrong views has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been spent, they shall suffer incessantly at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish realm.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, for five hundred lifetimes they are born among the hungry ghosts dwelling on the side of the Needle-Necked Mountains.

Having been liberated there, for five hundred lifetimes they are born among animals, taking the form of sea fish in the great ocean where the waves are vast, amidst extremely cold waters and waters of ash.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, it is as difficult for them to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a floating yoke.

If they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will constantly travel through forests and dwell within them, or subsist on their lives in overgrown thickets; such people will be burned by wild fires amidst those wilderness thickets.
This is the remaining retribution for those evil karmas.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again observes the Great Hell of Intense Heat: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called "All Humans Matured," which is the eighth secondary region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:
if a person habitually commits and frequently performs the acts of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying— their karma and its retribution are as previously described—
and furthermore holds wrong views, namely:

There are those who, being foolish and holding wrong views, hear false teachings; such deluded persons act with perversion in their bodily karma, perversion in their verbal karma, and perversion in their mental karma—thus these three types of karma are constantly performed in a perverted manner.

That person of wrong view practices the conduct of wrong view; whether in a forest, on a mountain, in a thicket, between two villages, or upon a sandbank—in such places as these—he sets fires to burn them. That person of wrong view has this thought:
"If the fire is fully satisfied, the devas will be pleased; if the devas are pleased, I shall be reborn in heaven."

Thus, because these deluded people have heard evil teachings and are deceived by those evil teachings, they form such a calculation: "By feeding fire until it is satiated, one shall be reborn in heaven," and so they set fires.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, being born in the Hell of All People Ripened, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies experienced in the Sañjīva and other hells are fully endured here, five times more intense.
Furthermore, there is something even more distressing:

once born in that place, one sees those whom one loved while still among humans—sons, daughters, wives, concubines, dear friends, or whether they be father or mother—all such beloved relatives and friends being scorched and boiled.

In that hellish realm, the men, women, wives, concubines, beloved friends, parents, and acquaintances are all created by the karmic transformations of those very people while they were in the human world. Seeing them there in hell being burned and boiled, the person feels great sorrow and grief in their heart and undergoes extreme suffering. Witnessing all those whom they held dear being scorched and cooked, the fire of craving burns within that hellish place with such heavy grief and suffering that the fires of the hells do not equal even one-sixteenth part of it; among all the afflictions experienced by those in hell, the suffering of the fire of craving is the most severe.
That fire of craving is the fire among fires;
that snare of craving is the snare among snares;
that bond of craving is the bond among bonds, binding all foolish worldlings.

Due to that person’s wrong views and unwholesome karma, while in the hell realms they see those they love, respect, and hold dear—such as friends and relatives—being burned and boiled; yet the fire of their own craving burns them from within—for the fires of hell are like frost and snow compared to the fire of the heart of craving. Hearing the wailing and loud cries of their wives, children, parents, and others, they speak these words:
"Come and save me! Come and save me!"
Those beings in hell are burned and boiled by the fires of hell and have no autonomy; how then could they save one another?

In that place of hell, they constantly and at all times undergo such burning of body and mind by fire for a vast duration of time, for countless years. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer unceasingly at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally escape from that place of hell.

Once they have attained liberation from that state, they are born among hungry ghosts for three hundred lifetimes, subsisting only on food and drink discarded by those who have recovered from illness.

Having escaped from there, they are born among animals for five hundred lifetimes, constantly becoming aquatic insects with many offspring; these offspring are perpetually slaughtered by fishermen and hunters.
Once released from that place, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a wooden yoke floating in the ocean.

Even if one is born among humans in a realm of similar karma, one will be impoverished and short-lived, with impaired faculties, neither wife nor children, and will constantly serve as a lowly person, a slave in celestial shrines, and so forth.
This is the remaining karmic retribution for those evil deeds.
*The Sutra on the Foundations of Mindfulness of the True Dharma*, Scroll Ten;
*The Sutra on the Foundations of Mindfulness of the True Dharma*, Scroll Eleven.
Translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Chapter on the Hells, Part Seven:
"Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again observes the Great Hell of Intense Heat (Pratapana); what other places are there?"
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place called *Anantāpāta* (The Endless Fall), which is the ninth distinct location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are people who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods, delighting in such actions and committing them frequently; their karma and its retribution are as previously described.

Furthermore, there are those who possess wrong views regarding the actions of body, speech, and mind; their deeds are pervasive, they carry them through to completion, and they take pleasure in performing and frequently committing them.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when their bodies perish and their lives end, they fall into that hell and are born in a distinct place called *Anantamalin*, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering, as previously described, all the agonies experienced in the Saṃjīva and other hells are fully present here, five times more intense.
The deeds of wrong view:
having heard the instructions of others through improper hearing, one harbors such a thought as this:
"If one casts insects, ants, snakes, pythons, deer, or horses into fire, and the fire is thereby pleased, I shall obtain great merit and be reborn in a superior world."
Those who are burned by fire will be reborn in the world-system of Maheśvara.
If a person burns sentient beings with fire, they shall obtain immeasurable and supreme great merit.

Thus, deceived by such foolish and false teachings, those of wrong views, upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life, fall into an evil destination. There, in that hell, they enter a specific place of no end and are born, undergoing great suffering and affliction.

As for what is called suffering: there is an iron mountain there, its flames extremely fierce, five yojanas in breadth. That mountain is entirely ablaze with the fires of hell. The *yama* wardens drive the hell-beings up that mountain, burning their feet, waists, and hips; their backs, arms, heads, and necks; their hands, feet, ears, and eyes, even unto their brains. Once burned, they are born again; once born, they are burned again. This continues for a vast duration beyond counting, until their evil karma is destroyed and decayed, and the momentum of that karma is exhausted;
at all times, the suffering does not cease. Only when the evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that place of hell.

Once that person of wrong views has escaped from that place, they will be born among the hungry ghosts who eat excrement for five hundred lifetimes; every part of their body will be ablaze with flames, and they will be seen by the public as they travel at night.

Once that person of evil karma has thus escaped from among the hungry ghosts, they are born as an animal, specifically as a firefly; with flames upon its body, it is seen by all people as it travels through the night.
Blown by the wind during the day and scorched by the sunlight, their bodies burn from within;
this is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat: what other places are there?
Through seeing, hearing, and knowing, he perceives that there is another distinct location called Mahāpadma; this is the tenth specific sub-region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees: there are people who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods, delighting in such practices and committing them frequently.
To put it briefly:
Their physical, verbal, and mental actions are pervasive and exhaustive, performed and further accumulated.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination and are born in a specific section of that hell called Mahāpadma. Their karma and its retribution are as previously described;
furthermore, they hold wrong views:
That person of wrong view has such a thought:
"If one kills a man during the Great Fast, one will attain a place to one's heart's content.

Having committed such evil karma of wrong view, when his body breaks up at the end of life, he falls into an evil destination and is born in a specific section of that hell, the Mahāpadma, where he undergoes great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:
in that place of hell, it is like a *padma* lotus situated amidst its filaments; the filaments of these vajra-thorns are five hundred *yojanas* long.

Within those vajra-thorn filaments of the *padma* lotus, the hell-beings are broken apart by the vajra-thorns in all their limbs; there is not even a space the size of a needle’s point that is not pierced, and there is no spot where the fires of hell do not burn through them, as the sores on their bodies blaze with flames.

Thus, for a long time they are constantly burned and constantly boiled; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be able to escape from that hellish place.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, they will be born among the hungry ghosts who feed on excrement for two hundred lifetimes.
Having escaped from there, they will be born among animals for five hundred lifetimes, becoming peacocks and the like, constantly consuming foul poisons.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a floating yoke.
Even if they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will be constantly oppressed by poverty and remain dependent on others.

Or, they may become performers who sustain their lives through the profession of entertainment; if they live their lives through such performances, they will remain lowly and base throughout the world until the end of their lives.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist therein.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place called the "Precipitous and Dangerous Shore," which is the eleventh location of that hell. By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees: there are those who commit killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and speaking falsehoods, with their karma and its retributions as previously described.
Furthermore, there is wrong view, which they delight in practicing and frequently perform, namely:
There are those who hold such a view:
"One who dies by entering the water has all their sins extinguished;
having died, they will be reborn in the world of the Eight-Armed One, from which place there is no falling back."
Thus, that foolish person, hoping to be reborn in that place, further teaches others and rejoices in the actions of others as they enter the water and die.
Having thus entered the water and died, that person falls into an evil state, remaining on the treacherous and perilous banks of that hell to undergo great suffering and affliction.
Having destroyed their physical, verbal, and mental actions, they are born in that place and undergo great suffering and distress.
As for what constitutes this suffering, it is as previously described: all the sufferings experienced in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are fully experienced here.
Furthermore, there is something even more terrible:

that hell is filled with extremely sharp-edged stones and many malevolent mountains; everywhere it is covered with precipitous cliffs and crags rising a thousand yojanas high, such that even birds cannot reach them by flight, let alone the sinners who might attempt to go there.
As the blazing flames pervade everywhere and burn intensely, a single inhabitant of that hellish realm says these words to all the other sinners in hell:
"Come, sirs! Once you have passed beyond this mountain, there will be no more hell."
"If we pass beyond this mountain, we shall obtain happiness.
Because of their evil karma, the inhabitants of the various hells hear and see that person speaking thus.
Having spoken these words, the inhabitants of the various hells rush toward that mountain.

Due to their evil karma, they arrive at a place of precipitous cliffs and dangerous shores where flames burn everywhere in a blazing conflagration. Having run there, they are unable to climb up; some fall down, some are intensely scorched within the fire, some, out of terror, embrace flaming rocks and are burned, and others, in their panic and fear, turn back and run away in search of rescue and refuge.
In that hell, the henchmen of Yama seize iron mallets and strike them with extreme force, beating them repeatedly.

Because the physical, verbal, and mental actions of those hell-beings were perverse, they are thus scorched and boiled for a vast duration of time; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decomposed, and its residual energy has not been exhausted, they are given suffering without ceasing at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that, they will be born for three hundred lifetimes among the blood-eating hungry ghosts (preta), being born into a realm of similar karma.
Having been liberated from that place, they will be born for three hundred lifetimes among poisonous animals; this is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.

If they are born among humans in places of similar karma, they will be impoverished and frequently ill; they will be born in an evil land with incomplete sense faculties, and will constantly live in fear within that evil land.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist there.
He perceives through vision and knowledge that there is another distinct place called Vajra-bone (Vajrāsthi), which is the twelfth location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:
there are those who commit killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and false speech, practicing these with delight and frequency, as previously described.
Furthermore, there are wrong views that one delights in practicing and frequently commits, namely:
some people harbor such a thought as this:

"All things in the world—whether sentient or insentient—arise spontaneously and perish spontaneously, like the thorns of a bramble or the colors of a peacock's feathers; they exist without causes and conditions and perish without causes and conditions, like a mirage or a city of Gandharvas."
"All phenomena are likewise thus: they do not arise from causes and conditions, nor do they cease through causes and conditions; they are naturally so.
Furthermore, he instructs others and establishes others in this view, causing them to believe thus, thereby destroying their physical, verbal, and mental karma.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body breaks up at the end of life, they fall into an evil destination and undergo great suffering and affliction in that hell known as the Place of Vajra Bones.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies endured in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are experienced here in their entirety.
Moreover, there are even more severe sufferings:
the Yama-wardens seize the hell-beings and, with sharp, polished knives, slice away the flesh from their bodies until nothing remains but bone.
They see their former enemies grasping skeletons with which they strike one another;

with those [skeletons] they strike this one, and with this one they strike that. Because of their evil karma, the bones become vajra-hard. Some have their heads shattered, some have their bodies split open, and some sinners have all their limbs and members completely shattered. Some have holes pierced through them, some have their bones dried up, and some sinners have lost their bodily parts. Furthermore, there are those who strike one another with bones, and some who strike them with flaming stones.
Due to the causal conditions of their evil karma, those hell-beings, for countless years within that hell, see their original enemies seizing them in this manner and beating one another.
As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they will experience uninterrupted suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, for five hundred lifetimes they are born among the hungry ghosts who feed on their own brains.
Having been liberated from there, for five hundred lifetimes they are born among animals as scorpions, tigers, or *gōṭas*.
Once liberated from that place, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a wooden yoke.

Even if one is born among humans in a realm of similar karma, one will be born in a frontier land or a forest kingdom, in evil countries such as Darada, Pīra, or Andhra; there, one will be impoverished, plagued by many diseases, and remain subservient to others.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called Suffering from Being Unloosed by Black Iron Cords and Swords, which is the thirteenth place within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are those who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods, delighting in such actions and performing them frequently; their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is another wrong view, namely:
some people hold such a view as this:
"All demerit and merit reside within causes and conditions; wherever the cause lies, one incurs that demerit or merit."
He delights in preaching it to others and takes pleasure in practicing and performing it extensively.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, being born in a specific place within that hell called Black Iron Rope and Knife-Slicing Suffering, where they undergo great torment.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies endured in the Saṃjīva and other hells are experienced here in their entirety, five times more intense.
Furthermore, there is another superior [suffering], namely:

there, the Yama-wardens bind their bodies with black iron chains; having bound them thus due to their evil karma, they split them open from the feet to the head with sharp iron blades, which are ablaze with fierce flames.

Once those hell-beings have been split by the shackles, they wail, shriek, cry out, and weep; yet they are further bound with iron chains, which—blazing and made of sharp iron—disintegrate them into the most minute fragments until not even a portion the size of a mustard seed remains, only for them to reunite and be born once more.
Having reunited and been born again, they are cut once more; having been cut, they are cut again.

That person thus undergoes great suffering and affliction in that place of hell for a long time; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of the karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when the evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, they will be born among hungry ghosts for five hundred lifetimes, consuming the foul water discarded by others in vessels.

Having been liberated from that place, they will be born among animals for one hundred lifetimes, becoming leeches, scorpions, dung beetles, or various other such insects; this is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
If they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will always be oppressed by hunger and thirst;
or if there are other people who violate the king’s law, they will be falsely accused and unjustly imprisoned, causing them to fall into criminal punishment.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist there.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place, called the Nagakīla-stambha-ugnāgni-duḥkha (Suffering from the Fierce Fire of the Naga-Worm Pillar), which is the fourteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods, delighting in such actions and performing them frequently; their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is a wrong view that one delights in practicing and frequently performing, namely:

some person holds such a wrong view as to say, "There is no this world, nor is there a world beyond; there are no karmic actions or their results regarding killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking alcohol, or lying, as previously described."
"This world is eternal; all phenomena are eternal, eternally indestructible.
Such is that person's inverted and false view.

That person of false views further teaches others to abide in false views, repeatedly explaining them, preaching them in great assemblies, and using evil causes and analogies to explain them to others, causing those people before him to adopt such evil and false views.
In the midst of the great assembly, regarding similar phenomena, they preached what is not the Dharma as being the Dharma.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination; in that hell, within the place of suffering from the Nagakīṭa-pillars and fierce fires, they undergo great torment.
That which is called suffering is as previously described: all the agonies endured in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are experienced here in their entirety.
Furthermore, there are even more severe sufferings, namely:
iron pillars arise there, and nails are driven into the heads of the beings; having thus emerged, half of each pillar sinks into the ground while the other half remains above the head.
Once it has been thus pierced, *nāga* worms are born throughout all parts of the sinner’s skin, flesh, and fat; they consume every limb of the sinner:
first they peck at his vessels and drink his blood until it is exhausted;

next they eat his flesh; next they break his bones; next they drink his marrow; next they sever his tendons; next they sever his vessels; next they burn his orifices; next they pull out his hair; and finally they shake his skin.
Next, he enters within the body into the mass of sinews and then breaks the heart;
having broken the heart, he drinks its juice. Next, he breaks the lungs, then enters through the back and drinks its juice, and finally disperses the vessels.

Next, with flaming tongs, he breaks beneath the jaw and pulls out the tongue; having pulled it out, he gives it to the dogs, because with that very tongue he spoke evil words, spoke the causes of perversion, and spoke by combining together unrighteous analogies.
Because of such offenses of the tongue, those hell-beings undergo this entire web of suffering.

Those people of wrong views, with crooked views, instruct others; with great malevolence, they teach and convert other people, causing them to abide in wrong views, thereby destroying their physical, verbal, and mental actions.

For a vast duration of time, they are constantly burned within the hells for an incalculable number of years that can never be exhausted; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been spent, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place in hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, they will be born for three hundred lifetimes among the hungry ghosts who feed on corpses.
Having been liberated from that, it will be difficult for them to obtain a human body, like a turtle encountering a hole in a wooden yoke.

If they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, when others commit crimes against the king's law, they will incur the calamities thereof through the power of their evil karma; they will be impoverished and frequently ill, bound to others and lacking autonomy, and though they eat human flesh, they are still called "humans."
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again examines the Great Hell of Intense Heat to see what other places exist therein.
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place called Dark Fire Wind, which is the fifteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are people who kill, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, and speak falsehoods; they take pleasure in these acts, perform them frequently, engage in them extensively, and bring their actions to completion.
Due to these evil karmas, they fall into that hell’s region of dark fire-wind; their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there are those with wrong views who delight in practicing and frequently committing them, namely:
there are people who hold such a view:
"All dharmas are both permanent and impermanent.
That which is impermanent is the body;
that which is permanent is the four great elements."

Those people of wrong views, holding these two views, explain them to others using evil causes and evil analogies, causing them to abide in wrong views and further giving rise to approval; they speak what resembles the Dharma within the midst of the great assembly and amidst what is not the Dharma.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, undergoing great suffering and affliction in that hellish place of dark fire and wind.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies suffered in the Saṃjīva and other hells are experienced here in their entirety, five times more intense.
Furthermore, there is another superior [suffering]:

once they have escaped from the torments inflicted by the *yama-rākṣasas* and are freed from that ordeal, they subsequently enter again the place of suffering characterized by dark fires and violent winds, produced by their own evil karma. Blown by fierce winds, those hell-beings are suspended in mid-air without any support; they revolve as rapidly as a wheel, their bodies becoming invisible.

After that person has thus undergone such cycles of transmigration like a wheel, a different wind of knives arises that shatters and cuts their body, causing it to disperse in the ten directions like a handful of sand; yet it is born again, and having been born, it is scattered once more, and having been scattered, it is born again.

Thus they endure such harsh and intense suffering constantly, without any reckoning of years, until their evil karma is neither destroyed nor decayed and its residual force is not exhausted; at all times they are subjected to unceasing pain.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that hellish realm.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, they will be born among the hungry ghosts who feed on vomit for five hundred lifetimes.
Having been liberated from that place as well, they will again be born among hungry and thirsty animals; this is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, again observes the Great Hell of Intense Heat: what other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct place called the Vajra-beaked Bee; this is the sixteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who commit killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, and lying, practicing these with delight and frequency; their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is a false view, namely:
some people hold such a view as this:
"The world has a beginning; it arises from causes and conditions; it is both eternal and non-eternal; everything is produced by causes and conditions."

Those who speak untruths, employing false causes and analogies, and preaching what appears to be the Dharma within what is not the Dharma, cause other people to abide in false teachings and fall away from the True Dharma; they obstruct the True Dharma and give rise to wrong views.

That is an incorrect teaching: that permanent phenomena are not causes, that permanent phenomena are immovable, that permanent phenomena do not change, and that the permanent cannot act, being like space; such people of false views engage in unreal conceptualization.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body disintegrates and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, being born in that hell at the place called "Diamond-Mouthed Bee Armor," where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
The bodily, verbal, and mental actions of that person with wrong views are ruined.
Such a base individual is the lowest among sentient beings;
they obstruct the True Dharma and abide in unwholesome states.

Out of ignorance, they commit actions leading to evil realms; yet, claiming to possess wisdom, they rely on that wisdom with arrogance, making conceptual distinctions according to their own whims and speaking untruths, thereby undergoing great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies endured in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are experienced here in their entirety, five times more intense.
Furthermore, there is another even more grievous suffering:

the Yama-wardens there use extremely fine tongs to pull out their flesh bit by bit, down to the size of a hair root; having pulled it once, they pull again, pulling it continuously in this manner and placing it into their mouths, driving them to eat it themselves.

In that place there are many diamond-beaked bees; when they touch the bodies of those who have committed offenses, hot blood flows forth, salty in taste like salt. The Yama-wardens take that salty blood and place it in the mouths of the offenders, driving them to consume it. Once they have eaten it, their hunger and thirst increase tenfold, burning their bodies and minds.
Deceived by their own evil karma, they further eat their own flesh; having eaten it, it grows back again.

Deceived and deluded by the causes and conditions of their accumulated evil karma, they undergo great suffering and affliction for countless years. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish realm.
Once they have attained liberation from that state, they will be born among hungry ghosts for four hundred lifetimes, consuming impure food.
Having been liberated from there, they will be born among animals for five hundred lifetimes, becoming creatures such as earthworms and dung beetles, their bodies consumed by hunger and thirst.
This is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, again contemplates the Great Hell of Intense Heat; having contemplated it thus, he no longer perceives a seventeenth location.

Such is the Great Hell of Intense Heat; such are its various locations and its ultimate extent. It is there that those people of wrong views, having performed such karmic deeds, dwell as a result of their evil karma.
That bhikṣu thus observes the six great hells and knows them as they truly are.
That practitioner reflects within his mind—contemplating the course of dharmas in accordance with the True Dharma—and having seen this, joy arises in his heart, and he speaks these words:
"This bhikṣu is foremost in diligence; he has attained the eleventh stage, and such a person is able to sever the path of birth and death."
When the yakṣas of that earth learned this, they rejoiced and in turn informed the yakṣas of the air, following the sequence previously described up until the Śubhakṛtsna devas, who spoke as follows:

"In such-and-such a country, in such-and-such a village, a certain son of good family—as previously described—has attained the eleventh stage. He does not dwell in the same place as Māra; his mind takes no pleasure in sporting with the afflictions (*kleśa*); he has departed from the realm of birth and death and its desires, and refuses to remain within the boundless sufferings of all worlds."

"Furthermore, that bhikṣu, having observed Sañjīva, Kālasūtra, Saṃghāta, Raurava, Mahāraurava, Tapana, and their respective subsidiary hells, examines once more: 'Are there still other hells remaining?'"
Through seeing, hearing, and knowing, he perceives that there is a great hell named Mahātapana (Great Heat).
By what karma are sentient beings born in that hell? He sees:

There are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; delighting in such practices and committing them frequently, they fall into that hell. Their karma and its retribution are as previously described. Furthermore, they cause the downfall and ruin of pure-practice *kumārikās* (virgins) who maintain their precepts without transgression, who are complete and flawless, and of virtuous *bhikṣuṇīs* who have never indulged in desire, have never broken the precepts, and act in accordance with the Dharma within the Tathāgata’s teaching.
Such a person does not believe in the Buddha’s Dharma, and with such thoughts they say:
"The Buddha is not an omniscient one.
Since the Buddha is not omniscient, how much less could his disciples—the bhikṣuṇī saṃgha—possess pure conduct?"
All such things are false speech, deceptive and unreal.
Thus, this Buddha-dharma is a place of evil; it is not by giving that one can produce merit, nor is it by giving that one can attain nirvāṇa.
"This is but an ordinary assembly of monks; if a bhikṣuṇī or a bhikṣuṇī of such a harmonious group violates the prohibitions, she incurs no offense.
Having thus harbored such evil thoughts, that person destroys the precepts of that girl or bhikṣuṇī, causing her to fall away from the monastic conduct and to commit transgressions.

Because that person committed evil and unwholesome deeds of body, speech, and mind, at the dissolution of the body after death, they fall into an evil destination and undergo great suffering and affliction within the Great Intense Heat Great Hell.

Their bodies are one yojana in height, yet their bodies are extremely soft, softer than fresh butter; their eyes are even softer than their bodies, and thus all five sense organs are exceedingly delicate. Even sounds, touches, forms, and scents can kill them—how much more so other forms of suffering?
Just as they committed evil, because their evil karma was so heavy, both their body and mind become utterly broken and weakened.

Due to the power of their evil karma, those people of evil deeds undergo extreme suffering and affliction. As they approach death, they experience the retribution of their present actions; they endure great agony and suffering, experiencing every kind of torment found within the Saṃjīva Hell, exactly as previously described.

When such a sinner is about to die, for three days prior to the end of life they undergo suffering in this manner until their life expires; they lose their voice and cannot speak, they perceive great terror, and their conduct becomes debased while their consciousness is agitated. Thus, in succession, the four elements become enraged, and they experience extreme agony and distress.

The earth element becomes rigid, and the body becomes stiff and agitated; the sinews, veins, and marrow throughout all parts of the body become constricted, and as they are all destroyed, great suffering arises—just as when fresh butter is kneaded, pressed, ground, and beaten, such is the nature of the earth element.
Furthermore, as for the water element:

it causes all the tendons and veins that bind the various parts of the body—which were originally firm and dry—to become rotted and flaccid; it produces the stench of decaying insects and completely blocks all the orifices of leakage; the throat becomes constricted and impassable, the tongue shrinks back into the gullet, all the apertures suffer pain, and sweat breaks out over the entire body.
Furthermore, regarding the fire element:

all the sinews and veins throughout the entire body are scorched and boiled, causing great suffering and affliction. The skin of the body becomes the color of red copper; both internally and externally there is heat, the mouth is parched with great thirst, and the heart is scorched by intense fever.
Furthermore, as for the wind element:

its characteristic of lightness increases further; because the body has become parched, it feels as if one is ascending into empty space, yet then falls back down to the ground. All parts of the body become completely dry, and the wind moves incessantly through all the limbs and all the channels.

There is a wind named Vipula-śūcī (the Great Needle), which, like a needle piercing a flame, penetrates throughout the entire body down to the pores of the skin, even drying up and burning away the marrow and essence.

The Vipula wind can cut through the skin, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, and essence as if with an axe; it blows upon all the sense organs, causing all parts of the body to become constricted. The excretions of feces and urine are obstructed and do not pass; the breath becomes irregular, the throat is distorted, and the eyes deteriorate. Within the ears, one hears unpleasant sounds; the nose no longer perceives fragrance, and the tongue loses the sense of taste. The bridge of the nose collapses, the male organ shrinks inward, and the anus suffers pain as if struck by fire, resulting in great agony. The skin swells, and the hair and body hair become loose.

These [teachings] speak only of those who have practiced evil deeds; when such a person is about to die, for three nights and three days, their four great elements become violently agitated, and they are oppressed by intense suffering.

When life comes to an end, the signs of the next world appear; specifically, one sees all houses as if they were black curtains and perceives black flames, like forms seen in a dream—such evil omens do not remain for even a moment.

Furthermore, they see unpleasant sights such as lions, tigers, and other unlovely forms; they behold all manner of extreme horrors. Hearing the evil roar of a tiger, they give rise to great terror, and their iron-grinding skin is nearly worn away.
That wind moves upward, beginning at the toenails; having left the toenails, it next moves to the insteps;
having left the insteps, it next moves to the calves;
likewise, having left the calves, it next moves to the knees.
Thus, having moved away from the knees, he next proceeded to the thighs;
thus, having moved away from the thighs, he next proceeded to the hips;
thus, having moved away from the hips, he next proceeded to the abdomen.
Thus, once the stomach has been removed, they next proceed to the heart;

thus, once the heart has been removed, the throat becomes constricted, the mouth dries up and saliva is exhausted, one eye sinks in, and they see within the empty space the hand of a *yamala* demon holding an iron club.
Having seen this, he rubs his chest with his hand. When his kinsmen and acquaintances see him do so, they all say, "This man is rubbing empty space.

His breath becomes obstructed; as he blows it throughout his body, his life-force is severed. Just as a lamp wick is extinguished after being burned, he departs from this world and is born in the intermediate state (*antarābhava*), obtaining a result that corresponds to its cause.

That person of evil karma, while in the intermediate state (antarābhava), undergoes the sufferings of the intermediate state; he perceives his own body as being like that of a long-lived human being with a lifespan of eighty-four thousand years, yet appearing in the form of an eight-year-old child.

One sees oneself, yet all other people do not see one; the four great elements are so subtle that they are invisible and intangible. One can pierce and pass through Mount Sumeru without obstruction; neither one's own body nor Mount Sumeru poses any hindrance, let alone any other mountains.
Within that intermediate state, they see for themselves a dark iron city and enter it.
Due to their evil karma, they perceive every hair upon their own bodies as being ablaze with flames.
Furthermore, he sees himself being bound by the henchmen of Yama with black iron cords; they bind his hands and likewise bind his feet.
Those black iron cords are harsh, hard, and painful to the touch, and their color is terrifying.
Next, within the wrappings that encircle their bodies, the entire frame is bound so tightly that not even a hair’s breadth remains.

As the practitioner of evil karma sees this for himself, once he has been firmly and tightly bound by iron cords, there appear objects of the five senses—forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures—that are utterly unlovely. Because of his evil karma, his eyes behold hideous forms that are most terrifying; the *Yama* hell-wardens have eyes ablaze with fire and various foul colors, and with arms outstretched in extreme rage, they are loathsome to behold.
Furthermore, when one hears unpleasant words with the ear and finds them disagreeable to hear—namely, being told:
"This person is a practitioner of evil deeds; their bodily, verbal, and mental actions are unwholesome, and they have committed evil conduct."

In this jewel-island land of the excellent human realm, they deceive themselves through improper reflection upon the ten paths of wholesome action; performing unwholesome deeds and constantly engaging in falsehoods, they fail to obtain the jewels of virtue.
All sensual pursuits are like knives, fire, and poison; they cause one to fall into a precipice.
Such a person is thus deceived by desire and deceived by another's wife, committing such evil deeds.

This person, failing to observe correctly in this way, has committed three kinds of unwholesome and evil karma. Since this deluded person has performed evil karma for himself, I shall now cast him into the Great Avīci Hell of Intense Heat and inflict upon him all manner of sufferings; I shall bestow all the countless hundreds of thousands of various afflictions so that, in the future, he will never again commit evil conduct or evil karma.
The Yama-wardens, in order to rebuke those in the intermediate state who have been separated from their wives and children and are filled with great sorrow, speak these verses:
"Women are perceived as kinsmen, yet they are as unbeneficial as enemies;
they destroy the human world and lead one to the dark places of hell."
Among all enemies and evils, there is none like the enemy of karma;
bound by the three types of unwholesome karma, I now send you to hell.
Having alone created evil karma, you shall alone receive its evil retribution.
One goes alone to a miserable realm; in this world, there is no companion.
If one commits many evils, the causes and conditions are directed toward others, yet what one has done oneself, one must receive back oneself; that other person cannot save one.
Why are you so foolish, deceived by wife and children?
Out of delusion and deception regarding the bhikṣuṇīs and others, you have committed evil.
In this world and in future worlds, enmity will always follow after you.
The greatest of all enemies is the enemy within, who points out every place of evil.
The evil karma you have created for yourself is like poison, like a blade, or like fire;
having created this evil karma yourself, you shall consume it in this very way.
It is not that one person performs the action while another receives the retribution;
it is neither in the beginning, nor in the middle, nor in the end, neither in this world nor in another world.
If a person has a distracted mind and does not observe with right attention, [they will not see the truth].
Because of craving for the flavor of pleasure, one performs unwholesome deeds.
A person of deluded and distracted mind increases unwholesome dharmas;
not knowing how to observe correctly, they perform various evil karmas.
The mind can deceive sentient beings; the mind can cause people to crave and lead them toward hell, departing into the darkness of dark places.
Enveloped by darkness within the cycle of birth and death, it is difficult to encounter the Buddha’s True Dharma.
If a person does not love the Dharma, they go from suffering to the place of suffering.
If a person’s mind is tranquil and their sense objects do not destroy them,
that person reaches a good destination— such as you have now reached.

"Thus, when those who have committed evil deeds—having performed unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind—have been rebuked by the Yama-wardens, they are sent away to the Great Intensely Burning Great Hell."

The nose shall smell impure, putrid, and foul excrement; the tongue shall taste hard, hot, impure, and loathsome flavors; one shall encounter forms with undesirable odors and fragrances; and the body shall experience the most grievous and evil tactile sensations, as malevolent winds blow like knives and like fire.
These five objects of experience are extremely evil and terrifying; because the mind is filled with dread, fear and timidity arise.
Having already seen the signs of the great hells, the henchmen of Yama bind their throats tightly; driven by the winds of karma, they are led toward hell, deprived of all autonomy.
The Yama-wardens have hideous countenances, and their hands and feet are intensely hot; they contort their bodies and bulge their bellies, causing the sinners to feel extreme terror upon seeing them.
The voices of these Yama-wardens are like the roar of thunder, and when the sinners hear them, their fear increases even further.

The Yama-royal messengers hold sharp swords in their hands; their bellies are vast like the color of black clouds; their eyes blaze like lamps and their canine teeth are sharp as blades; their arms and hands are all long, brandishing them with threatening gestures; their shoulders are broad and their long claws are sharp and flaming; their arms are thick with bulging veins, and every part of their bodies is coarse and protruding. With such various terrifying forms, they seize those who have committed evil deeds and lead them away. They pass over sixty-eight hundred thousand *yojanas* of land, sea, islands, and cities, reaching the outer edge of the ocean. From there, they travel another thirty-six billion *yojanas*, gradually descending ten billion *yojanas* further, driven by the winds of karma, thus departing to that great distance.
In that place, they are blown by the power of karmic winds; it is beyond the scope of mental calculation and cannot be illustrated by analogy.
Regarding the realm of that place, neither the sun, the moon, nor the power of the wind can reach it—only the power of karmic winds prevails.
Among all winds, the wind of karma is foremost; there is nothing that surpasses it.
Thus, the wind of karma leads those who possess evil karma to that place, and once they have arrived, King Yama rebukes them as previously described.

Having been thus rebuked by King Yama, the person, bound by the noose of evil karma, is led toward hell. Because of their evil karma, they perceive the Yama-wardens there as sentient beings, who then lead the person of evil karma away to the Great Intensely Burning Great Hell.
Thus, from afar in the darkness, those sinners see that great Saṃjīva (Great Heat) Great Hell ablaze with flames everywhere.
That hell measures five thousand yojanas, neither more nor less.
Three thousand yojanas from that hell, one hears the sounds of the denizens of hell wailing; moved by this, one becomes distressed, terrified, and overcome with extreme grief and affliction.
They have already endured immeasurable and manifold sufferings, which are harsh, evil, and unbearable.
In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of countless years, they heard the sounds of the hell-beings wailing within the Great Intense Heat Great Hell.
Having heard the wailing, their spirits are tenfold more terrified; with hearts struck by fear and dread, the *yama* beings thus lead them away toward the Great Intensely Burning Great Hell.
Because the Yama-wardens rebuked him, they spoke this verse:
“Hearing the sounds of hell, you are already so terrified;
how much more so when hell burns like dry wood and grass being consumed by fire?”
Fire does not truly burn; it is evil karma that burns.
While fire can be extinguished, the burning of karma cannot be extinguished.
Fire does not burn in hell, nor does fire follow one wherever one goes.
The fire of the evil karma you have committed shall burn you in an instant.
If you commit the fire of evil karma, it will burn you in the burning hells;
if you abandon the fire of evil karma, then you will not fear hell.
If a person cherishes their own body and also fears hell,
that person will abandon evil and not undergo great suffering.
One who has abandoned unwholesome karma observes with a mind that is constantly discerning.
When body, speech, and mind are all virtuous, one is not far from nirvana.
If a person constantly harbors an evil mind and a deluded mind always reigns supreme, they will consequently fall into the evil hells; why then need their eyes shed tears?
By creating suffering, one receives the retribution of suffering; by extinguishing suffering, one receives the retribution of happiness.
Those whose karma is evil in the beginning, middle, and end—such sentient beings do not experience joy.
You have committed evils among men; you have already performed many such unwholesome deeds.
Such are the fruits of evil karma; now one is about to experience them.
If a person commits evil deeds, they will go toward an evil destination;
if a person performs virtuous deeds, they will go toward a good destination.
One does not obtain a pleasant fruit by performing evil deeds;
a pleasant fruit is not obtained through evil, for it is received without inversion.
Since beginningless time in the world, by performing good one obtains a pleasant fruit.
If one performs evil deeds, such bitter fruits will be obtained.
Causes and conditions are similar; they do not correspond to what is inverted.
Having already performed the cause in the past, one thus receives the retribution.
"Thus, having been harshly rebuked by the *yama-rākṣasas* within that intermediate state due to the evil karma committed by the sinner, they are led toward hell.
When those people of evil karma hear this rebuke, their hair stands on end with terror; how much more so when they see it with their own eyes?"

Among them, there are beings who, having seen the blazing flames of the hell and perceiving that the various aggregates such as form are undergoing extreme suffering from cold, tremble with unbearable distress.
Toward those hot flames and fierce fires of the hell, they conceive a mind of craving and attachment; as soon as the thought arises, they seize them.
With grasping as condition, existence arises; all factors of existence are likewise produced with conditions as their cause.

That person of evil karma, due to unwholesome karmic causes—namely, killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, false speech, and wrong view—further commits a perverse act: he forcibly compels a bhikṣuṇī who is pure in conduct, free from desire and defilement, and endowed with pure precepts, to engage in sexual intercourse against her will.

Having committed and accumulated those unwholesome karmas, their power becomes firm and rigid. The retribution they receive is a great mass of fire, five hundred yojanas in height and two hundred yojanas in breadth. With its flames blazing fiercely, the force of the evil karma created by that person violently hurls their body into that mass of fire, like a great mountain cliff pushed over a precipice, where there is no ledge, foothold, or place to grasp.

Thus these sinners enter directly into the great fire. In that hell, those who have committed evil deeds are driven by such force into the blazing fires of the great hell; because of their evil karma, hot iron hooks first hook their feet, causing them to enter the fire with their heads downward.
That person of evil karma, having thus entered the blazing fires of hell, first has their eyes burned; once the eyes are burned, next the scalp is burned;
once the scalp is burned, next the skull is burned;
once the skull is burned, next the cheekbones are burned.
Having burned the cheekbones, he next burns the teeth;
having burned the teeth, he next burns the jawbone;
having burned the jawbone, he next burns the neck bone.
Having burned the cervical vertebrae, he next burns the vertebral column;
having burned the vertebral column, he next burns the sternum;
having burned the sternum, he next burns the trachea.
Having burned the throat tube, he next burns the heart;
having burned the heart, he next burns the stomach;
having burned the stomach, he next burns the large intestine.
Having burned the large intestine, he next burns the small intestine;
having burned the small intestine, he next burns the hips;
having burned the hips, he next burns the organ.
Once the roots have been burned, he next burns the thigh bones;
once the thigh bones have been burned, he next burns the calves;
once the calves have been burned, he next burns the ankles.
After burning the ankles, they next burn the toes.

In this manner, due to their evil karma, those people of evil deeds first enter the great fire-basin; thus they are intensely burned across all their limbs. Once burned, they are reborn, and their suffering continues without interruption. Just as they performed the most extreme actions among humans, so too do they undergo the most extreme suffering.
