Those hell-beings thus undergo the full torment of flaming garlands and fire basins; being thus intensely scorched, they subsequently fall onto a ground of diamond-fire. Out of terror, they stretch out their hands and exert their arms, yet once they have fallen to the ground, they are immediately cast upward again—like a ball striking the earth, rising up without pause.

Thus they rise and fall rapidly, stretching out their hands and straining their arms, wailing and crying out as they fall to the ground and rise again. As they thus shriek and call, a great wreath of flames completely envelops their bodies; they are established in mid-air and are constantly being burned, just as those previously mentioned were cast into the midst of the flames.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, within that great cauldron of the great hell, they are burned and burned again, burning continuously without ceasing; all their limbs are burned and then grow back again, until the end of time.

If they emerge from the fire pit, due to their evil karma, they again see the henchmen of Yama; though these are not sentient beings, the offenders perceive them as such, holding flaming iron tongs in their hands.
Those tongs are extremely hot, twice as hot as that mass of fire.
For what reason are those tongs so extremely hot?
Because of the taking of life, they are scorched by the fire-basin.
Due to the two evil karmas of killing and stealing, those tongs become extremely hot, twice as hot as before; by this cause and condition, those flaming iron tongs become twice as hot.

The Yama-wardens are not sentient beings; with such tongs, they seize the sinner and place him upon a floor of glowing iron. They lift him up onto flaming iron hooks and force him to sit. The flaming iron hooks enter through the anus and emerge from the back, or from the crown of the head; the details are as explained previously.
Once he has sat down, he experiences threefold suffering: hot, blazing, sharp iron cuts his male organ, cutting it together with the testicles.
For what cause and for what reason does he experience this threefold suffering?
That is to say, through the causes and conditions of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct, one undergoes threefold suffering.
It is like a blacksmith or his apprentice at a forge: when the bellows are blown, the air fills the leather bag, and as that wind blows, the flames of the fire blaze up.
In this way, in this manner, because a person who commits evil deeds has brought those evil deeds to ultimate completion, they are called an "evil-doer.
Because the evil-doer and their followers of evil deeds are pervasive in every action, it is called "wind," namely the "karma-wind.
Engaging in sexual intercourse with women is called "boiling heat within a forging furnace."

This refers to the denizens of hell who cry out and shriek; thus they are greatly blown upon, thus they are greatly burned, and by their many unwholesome karmas, those people of unwholesome karma are greatly scorched, undergoing extreme suffering and affliction.

By reason of these causes and conditions, they suffer threefold torment within that hell; one should know that this is the fruit of having habitually practiced and frequently committed killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct.
The Yama-wardens question those people of evil karma who are in that most terrifying hell, whose faces are contorted with cries of distress as they are being boiled by the great fire, saying:
"What is your affliction?"
"What is it that you suffer?
The person undergoing suffering then replies to the Yama-rodha wardens, saying:
"I am now experiencing such extreme and great suffering."
"Such great suffering as this may yet be endured, but the suffering of thirst is unbearable.

When the Yama-wardens have heard this, there is further a river named Bhīṣmavīci (Terror-Wave); that river is filled with a mixture of extremely hot, violently boiling molten copper and tin, and it also contains many glowing iron blocks; furthermore, the banks of that river are treacherous.
If they see that river, they feel extreme terror;
if they hear its sound, they give rise to intense fear.
The Yama-wardens take hot copper and molten white tin in heated iron bowls and, holding them toward the offenders, say to them:
"Drink this! Because that person was thirsty, they grasped it with both hands, thinking it was water, and having taken it, they drank.

Due to their evil karma, that hell-being first has their lips burned; once the lips are burned, the tongue is burned next, and so on until the throat-pipe is entirely consumed by fire. Proceeding in succession, the fire burns the entire body until it emerges from below.
Thus these sinners blaze four times more intensely and suffer four times more severely.
What is the karmic retribution for this?
It is namely: killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and the consumption of intoxicants.

If one who observes the precepts drinks [alcohol] themselves and further gives it to others who observe the precepts or to ordained bhikṣus, the retribution for this karma will be that within the hells, suffering from parching heat and craving water, they must drink boiling, red-flaming molten copper.
In this way, a bhikṣu who upholds the precepts, being among the Saṃgha, does not recognize it as alcohol, thinking it is a pure drink when in fact it is alcohol.
Alcohol is poison; once he has taken it in his hand, he is unable to discard it, and out of fear of the Saṃgha, he drinks it himself.
As for the retribution of this karma: in the hells, one is unable to abandon the glowing red flames and molten copper, yet out of desperate thirst one drinks them; this is the fruit of alcohol.
Specifically, when a śramaṇa is in the home of a donor, out of regard for the donor’s feelings, he cannot refuse it and instead drinks it; this is the karmic retribution of that act.
The Yama-wardens asked the hell-being once more,
"What is your affliction? The hell-being then replied:
"I am now afflicted by hunger.
Among all the sufferings I endure, the suffering of hunger is the most severe.
Having answered thus, the Yama-wardens take iron balls from the terrifying river of boiling, scorching flames—blazing with fivefold intensity—and say to the sinner:
"This is food. Because of their evil karma and delusion, those hell-beings give rise to this thought:
"Now the food has arrived."

He immediately takes it and eats it; first his lips are burned as previously described at length, continuing in sequence until it emerges from below. Due to the power of his evil karma, he does not die; because of the karma he has accumulated, his tongue grows back again, becoming even softer than a lotus petal, and his body grows back again, becoming tender and supple—such is the retribution for his evil karma.
As that bhikṣu observes in this way, he considers: "What karmic fruit leads to a newborn being being more supple?
Through seeing, hearing, and knowing, he perceives:
"The Tathāgata is like a lamp; thus he has spoken:"
"If a person kills living beings, commits theft, engages in sexual misconduct, drinks alcohol or gives it to others, and further utters falsehoods—such is the karmic fruit and retribution.
If a person violates the precepts yet proclaims with a voice like a conch shell:
'I maintain the precepts.'"
"Thus, a bhikṣu with such a state of mind who eats the food of the Saṃgha obtains such a fruit.
Then the Yama-wardens further questioned the hell-being, saying:
"Is your tongue burning?"
Those hell-beings, people of evil karma and delusion, pull out their tongues and show them.
Their tongues are extremely soft like lotus petals and measure half a yojana in width, due to the karma of false speech.
The Yama-wardens plow their tongues with plows; they are wounded, shattered, and split apart hundreds of times over, crying out in lamentation due to the karma of their false speech.

For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of years—beyond calculation and for an exceedingly long duration—they undergo great suffering and distress as the retribution for the evil karma they have accumulated. Having experienced this, they still do not attain liberation from hell.
The Yama-wardens further rebuked him with these verses:
"Just as you cherish and protect your own life, so do others cherish their own lives.
Yet you have killed living beings; because of the evil karma you have created, you have come [to this state]."
People would rather give up their lives than amass wealth;
why then do they seize the property of others and claim it as their own?
All people love their wives more than they love themselves.
You who are a person defiled by delusion and desire, why do you so forcefully invade and oppress?
For one who drinks alcohol, delusion arises toward the Buddha;
this is the foremost transgression among all dharmas—why, then, do you drink alcohol?
From the midst of your tongue you emit poisonous venom; all people do not believe you.
You who are a person of false speech, why do you not abandon it?
These five kinds of evils are what your mind delights in.
Now you ought to endure it; to give rise in vain to such grief and affliction is useless.
The nature of evil karma is like poison; because you did not abandon it, you have arrived at this hell, a place of great terror known as Jvālāmāla.

"Thus do the Yama-wardens rebuke the hell-beings; having rebuked them, because of the karma they themselves have created—which acts like a seal—they constantly undergo great suffering day and night without ceasing, in various ways that are harsh and of immeasurable kinds."
Just as there are immeasurable kinds of unwholesome karmic actions, so too are there immeasurable varieties of suffering experienced; as the cause is, so the corresponding fruit is obtained.
Because such fruits of suffering resemble their seeds, one fulfills one's evil karma within the Great Intense Heat Great Hell.
Those who perform unwholesome deeds experience the retribution of suffering;
those whose goodness is fulfilled experience the fulfillment of happiness.
Those people of evil karma suffer in this manner for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years. Such evil karma is no different from an enemy, bringing great harm.
In this manner, those hell-beings are burned and boiled.

When such sinners escape from that place, seeking rescue and seeking refuge, they run toward another location. From afar, they see a forest of extreme darkness; in such dark places there are many large dogs, and those dogs are named "The Great-Mouthed Powerful Ones."
Such dogs are able to run with great speed; their mouths are adamantine, and the sound of their barking is most terrifying.
Such powerful dogs with gaping mouths are found everywhere throughout that forest.

When those hell-beings see that forest, they run toward it in haste and enter. All those wicked dogs come running after the sinners, first biting their testicles, flesh, skin, tendons, genitals, veins, and the openings of the vessels, as well as their bones and joints; they devour every part of their bodies until not even a portion the size of a mustard seed remains. Thereafter, the body is born again, and for a vast duration of time, they are devoured by the wicked dogs.
What is the karmic fruit of this?
It is the karma of taking life.
For the sake of eating meat, one kills sentient beings and thus obtains such a fruit.
The Sutra on the Foundations of Mindfulness of the True Dharma, Scroll Eleven.
The Sutra on the Foundations of Mindfulness of the True Dharma, Scroll Twelve.
Translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Chapter on the Hells, Part Eight:
"Furthermore, as for the fruit of stealing:
due to their evil karma, those in that hell see their own possessions being plundered by others, whereupon they immediately run after them."
As they flee in this manner, the Yama-wardens seize them with sharp iron blades and hack and slice them; every vessel is severed, yet once severed, it grows back again.

Furthermore, other hell-beings come running swiftly, and the Yama-wardens likewise seize them, striking, piercing, and beating them with spears, tridents, pestles, and hammers, all of which are ablaze with flames; this is the karmic retribution for their evil deeds of theft.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, until the fruit of that unwholesome karma of stealing has been exhausted—its power destroyed, its substance rotted away, and it utterly extinguished—that person will finally be liberated from that place.
Furthermore, as for those who practice wrong conduct:

they see their former wives being swept away by the River of Ashes, crying out in extreme distress as they are driven by cruel waves—some emerging and some sinking—and call out to the denizens of hell, saying:
"I am now here in this evil place of the River of Ashes, without a guide or a savior; can you now come and rescue me from this calamity?"

Having heard those cries, that hell-being, driven by the deluded mind of his evil karma, enters the River of Ashes. At the very moment of entry, all parts of his body are rotted away by the ash until not even a grain of mustard seed remains; only the residual bones remain, after which flesh grows once more.
Once the flesh has grown back, he again sees that former woman further away than before, wailing within the River of Ashes, saying these words: "Save me! Save me!"
That man immediately stepped forward, and the woman ran swiftly toward him. Having reached her, he sought to embrace her;

she embraced him, but her body was entirely of glowing red-hot iron, blazing with flames. With sharp iron claws, once she had him in her grasp, she tore at his body until it was shattered and destroyed, such that not even a space the size of a mustard seed remained intact, leaving only bones behind.
Thus, the bodies of these sinners are entirely covered in blood, with nothing remaining but a network of sinews.

Overwhelmed by lustful desire, those hell-beings see those women and run toward that River of Ashes. There they remain for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of years, thus being violently tossed about and thus being violently scorched. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer unceasingly at all times. Only when their karma in that place is exhausted will they finally attain liberation.

Thus they are born again, their bodies scorched by hunger and thirst; they run aimlessly everywhere until they see a river, a pond, or a pool of clear water. In the hope of reaching that cool water, they rush toward it with great speed.

Having arrived there, that river, pond, and so forth are entirely filled with molten white tin, and it is everywhere teeming with fierce, venomous snakes. Those hell-beings, suffering from intense heat and thirst, immediately drink this mixture of venomous snakes and molten white tin.

That evil venomous snake is produced by the karmic offenses [of the sinner]; it is extremely subtle when it enters the mouth of the offender, yet once it has entered the belly, it immediately becomes coarse and large. The stomach of the hell-being likewise expands, and as this evil snake remains within his body, it bites everything throughout it entirely; first it bites the small intestine and devours it—this is the transgression of the precept-breaker who drinks alcohol.

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, deceived by their evil karma, they are bitten by those snakes and scorched by white tin; being thus burned and bitten, they die only to be born again—this is the transgression of a person of precepts who drinks alcohol and breaks them.

Furthermore, as a result of the evil karma of lying, their tongues are bitten by snakes; thus they undergo great suffering for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years. As long as that evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times. Only when that karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated.
"Once they have escaped from that place, they wander aimlessly here and there, yet again they encounter the fruit of their lack of compassion.
Those hell-beings, who were created by their own karma, speak thus:
'Why do you burn though you are innocent? Is there no other place for you to dwell than this?'"
"I shall show you a place where you may find happiness.

After the Yama-wardens have spoken thus, they take the hell-being from that location within the hells and place him in another; there, they inflict upon him various and manifold additional sufferings.

The Yama-wardens thus inflict various further torments upon the hell-beings; that is to say, they are burned by great fires in every direction and place, undergoing manifold sufferings as steep precipices surround them and are set ablaze everywhere.

Furthermore, they enter again the place of great bodies, evil roars, and dread, where they are constantly burned and constantly boiled; thus they undergo suffering, their bodies being immense and extremely soft, measuring ten yojanas in size.

Furthermore, they enter again the place named Fire-Tuft (*Jvālāmukha*). There they are born and undergo great suffering and affliction; in that Fire-Tuft place, the great fire is more intensely hot than all other fires, and this fire is supreme, with nothing comparable to it.
In that place called Jvālāmukha (Fire-Crest), fire-sand rains down constantly, burning and boiling [the beings] there; that sand is thick and heavy like summer rain.

Furthermore, there is another place named Antaraprapācana (Internal Boiling Heat); in that place, dark fires constantly burn and boil them, causing the bodies of those offenders to swell up like leather bags.
Furthermore, there is another place called Tāṭatāṭacimi; in that region of hell, all the sinners rub and slash one another with their various limbs, undergoing great suffering and distress.

Furthermore, there is another place called "Universally Enduring All Suffering of the Requisites of Life. In that place, they are wickedly boiled and undergo great torment. In such a place, there are many terrifying and malevolent dogs, lions, crows, vultures, pigs, and snakes, all of whom inflict suffering.

Furthermore, there are evil rivers; that river is named Vaitaraṇī. It burns and sweeps away with violence; those who are burned and boiled therein are completely decomposed and cooked to maturity. The hot ashes, red copper, and white tin of that river boil and seethe with flames, violently sweeping away, burning, and boiling them in hundreds and thousands of ways. Thus they are burned and boiled.
Furthermore, there is another place called Uninterrupted Darkness (*ānantamandha*); when sinners enter therein, they are burned and boiled by dark fires, undergoing various kinds of suffering.

There is yet another place called the Place of the Garland of Suffering (*duṣkaramaṇḍala*); when sinners enter therein, they are burned and boiled, experiencing agony as a wheel of hot flames revolves upon their heads, while all their limbs are sawn, cut, split, and torn apart.

Once they have escaped from that, they enter another place called *Vṛṣṭisragdhūta* (Shaken by the Rain of Garlands), where they are repeatedly burned and boiled until their entire bodies are ablaze with flames; having been thus scorched, the *Yama-rākṣasas* strike and cut them with flaming knives hundreds and thousands of times.

Once they have escaped from that, they enter again the place called Mālākūṭa (Garland-Pile) where they are burned and cooked. There, their skeletal bodies become like snow, and fire arises from within their own bodies; the hell-beings there each seize sharp knives and hack and carve one another in this manner for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years.

Even after they have attained liberation, they enter once more into the Place of Sorrowful Howling; in that evil place, they are constantly burned and constantly boiled. As they are thus boiled, they let out a great roar; such a roar as this is not found among all the other hells.

"Once they have escaped that, they enter again what is called the Place of Great Compassion (*mahākaruṇā-sthāna*). Those people of wrong views—those who praise what is not the Dharma and what is evil as being the Dharma—because of their evil karma, see those they love, whether father or son, elder brother or younger brother, being burned and cooked in the Place of Great Compassion. With their bodies twisted and suffering, they wail and cry out:
'I am now all alone; will you come to save me?'"
Those fathers and sons, overcome with extreme great sorrow and suffering, stretch their arms upward and cry out in a loud voice.
When those hell-beings see this, the fire of grief arises within them, burning the fuel of craving; the heat of the fire of grief makes the fires of hell seem like ice and snow.
Thus, scorched by these two kinds of great fires and undergoing extreme suffering and distress, they cry out and lament.
The *Yama* wardens then address them with verses, rebuking them as follows:
"The fire of craving is hotter than fire; All other fires are like ice."
Among these, the fires of hell and the fires of craving within the three realms—
the fires of hell are but minor and not worth mentioning;
yet the fire born from the cause of craving possesses fierce flames and is most poisonous and hot.
Those in the hells of evil conduct may yet find liberation once their karma is exhausted;
but as for the fire of craving that burns the three realms, there is no time when one can escape it.
Craving binds people within the beginningless cycle of birth and death.
The fire of craving is hell; it is not from hell that fire arises.
Though the fires of hell are hot, they can burn only the body;
the fire of craving burns sentient beings, scorching both body and mind.
Craving is the fire born of conditions; it is the most supreme among fires.
The fires of hell are not all-pervasive, but the fire of craving pervades everything.
Through three causes and three bases of activity, the three types of karma manifest.
Born within the three times, all are the fires of the fire of craving.
In the heavens, one is burned by the fire of desire; among animals, one is burned by the fire of hatred;
in hell, one is burned by the fire of delusion; the fire of craving burns them all.
Thus the fire of craving’s affection causes all three realms to blaze;
seeing this, why do you not find joy in the Dharma?
Now, with such a mind, I repent.
"Thus do the Yama-wardens rebuke the hell-beings in that place of great compassion within the hells.
Having thus rebuked them, they further inflict upon them various kinds of suffering."

When such a sinner is released from that place, he is again boiled in the hell of the Compassionless Darkness; there, the universal fire burns the hell-beings, their color resembling that of the *kiṃśuka* tree.

If such a sinner is released from that place, he is further boiled in the Wood-Turning Hell (*kāṣṭhabhramana-naraka*). That person in hell is boiled in sixteen locations within that hell due to being possessed by wrong views, having violated a bhikṣuṇī through the transgression of evil karma.

That person shall be burned for an incalculable number of years over a vast period of time; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hell.

Even after escaping that place, they are reborn among hungry ghosts and animals; for immeasurable thousands of lifetimes, they are tormented by hunger and thirst and cook in suffering, devouring one another, consuming hundreds of thousands of bodies.

Thus, those who are animals, having committed evil and false views and further violated the precepts of a bhikṣuṇī of pure conduct, will find it as difficult for such persons to obtain a human body as a turtle encounters a hole in a floating yoke.

If they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will become eunuchs for five hundred lifetimes as the remaining retribution for the unwholesome and evil karma of having violated a bhikṣuṇī.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, contemplates the Great Intense Heat (Mahātapana) great hell.
He sees, hears, and knows:

if a person commits the acts of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, lying, or holding wrong views—the karmic results of which are as previously described—and furthermore, if a person violates the pure upāsikā precepts, then at the dissolution of the body after death, they fall into an evil destination. They are born in that hell, in the region of Intense Heat in every direction, and undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering:
in that hellish realm, everything from the Uninterrupted [Avīci] up to the very sky is ablaze with flames, such that there is not even a space the size of a needle's eye that is not burning.

That person reaches his hand upward from within the fire, crying out with the most urgent and terrible voice; scorched by powerful, firm, and blazing flames, he cannot even find ashes, yet he is born again, being burned incessantly in this manner for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years.

If they escape from that place, hoping for rescue or seeking refuge, they flee toward another location; yet as they thus run away, the Yama-wardens seize them once more, wrapping glowing iron cords around them from their feet up to their heads, binding them tightly in succession until the blood flows upward and collects within their heads. Thereafter, they further drive flaming iron hooks into the crowns of their heads, which then emerge from beneath their chins.

Furthermore, they seize them with iron hooks, twisting and wringing them violently; then, drawing them out and pulling, the blood flows forth like molten red copper, with hot flames blazing intensely, drenching their bodies.
In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, their bodies are drenched in blood and subjected to burning and boiling; they die and are reborn, die and are reborn again.

Due to the power of their evil karma, they are thus constantly burned and boiled at all times until their evil karma is destroyed and decomposed, and its residual force is exhausted. At all times, their suffering does not cease;

only when their evil karma is exhausted are they finally released from that hellish place, whereupon they are reborn among hungry ghosts and animals for further immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years.
If born among the hungry ghosts, one undergoes the suffering of hunger and thirst;
within the animal realm, one suffers from devouring one another, being killed and eaten by others for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of lifetimes.
After those people of evil karma have undergone such suffering, it is as difficult for them to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a wooden yoke floating in the ocean.

Even if they are born among humans in a place where their karma is similar, they will be impoverished and frequently ill; they will constantly suffer from feverish distress at the hands of others, their minds will remain in unceasing turmoil, and they will not live long, remaining eunuchs for four hundred lifetimes.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, contemplates the location of the Great Intense Heat (Mahātapana) Great Hell.
He sees, hears, and knows:

If a person commits the karmic acts of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, lying, and holding wrong views—the fruits of which are as previously described—and furthermore, if that person violates the pure śrāmaṇera precepts, then at the dissolution of the body after death, they will fall into an evil destination, being born in that hell in the place called "Great Body, Evil Roar, Terrifying," where they undergo great suffering and affliction.

As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies experienced in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are fully endured in that place known as the Great Body, Fierce Roaring, and Terrifying.
Furthermore, there is another superior [torture]:

the body of that sinner is one *yojana* in size and is as supremely soft as a lump of fresh butter. The *Yama-rodha* (Yama’s henchmen) seize his body and, using fine tweezers, pull out every hair; they pull them out along with the flesh, from the feet to the head, pulling them all out until there is not even a space the size of a mustard seed that has not been plucked.

As that person undergoes such extreme agony of being crushed, they let out a great cry; hearing this, the hearts of the other hell-beings break, split open, and scatter. Deceived by the resentment in their own minds, they had created evil karma; thus, deceived by their own karma, these words emerge from them.
"As the hell-beings suffer in this manner, the Yama-wardens, for the sake of rebuking them, speak these verses:
'From a mind of desire, sweet words emerge; Hearing sweet words, desire is aroused.
Desireful speech is a great evil, And now one receives such a fruit.'"
Sensual speech is the sharpest blade; that blade cuts one's own body.
It would be better to cut out one's own tongue than to utter words of lust.
Sentient beings deceived by desire have their hearts ablaze with the fire of anger.
Because they are gripped by a deluded mind, they speak sweet words of lustful desire.
The pleasure of lust is minimal, yet the evil karma created is vast;
the deluded person, gripped by a lustful heart, goes from suffering to further suffering.
The pleasure of desire lasts but for a single moment; it is neither true happiness nor permanent.
One undergoes extreme suffering in a future body; thus, one should renounce desire.
Those covered by desire dwell in the house of hell.
If one is not subject to desire, then one does not fear hell.
If a person commits evil deeds, they will certainly suffer affliction;
why do you, a pitiable and base person, now cry out in lamentation?
Those in the hells of evil conduct may find release only when their karma is exhausted;
yet there is no principle by which one can gain liberation through much crying out.
If a person desires autonomy, they should not perform unlovely, evil deeds.
The foolish person now suffers; what benefit is there in wailing?
If one sees the fruits of the future and finds joy and goodness in the present, that person does not wail, as you do this very day.
"Thus do the Yama-wardens rebuke those who have practiced evil deeds.

Having thus rebuked them, they further inflict upon them various and immeasurable sufferings; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall be subjected to unceasing suffering at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be released from that hellish realm."
Once they have attained liberation from that, they will be born among hungry ghosts and animals for immeasurable thousands of lifetimes.
Having escaped from those states, it is as difficult for them to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a floating yoke.

If they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, they will be short-lived and impoverished, their minds distracted and incorrect, and all their words will be disbelieved; for four thousand lifetimes, they will be incapable of male function.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, contemplates the location of the Great Intense Heat Great Hell.
He sees, hears, and knows:
Furthermore, there is another place named Fire-Crest (Jvālā-śikha), which is the third distinct location within that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
There, they see:

There are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they take pleasure in practicing these acts and perform them frequently. The karma and its retribution are as previously described. Furthermore, there are those who commit unrighteous acts against women who maintain dignified deportment and correct conduct by engaging with them through improper paths.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination and are born in the Fire-Tufted section of that hell, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies suffered in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are experienced here in their entirety, ten times more intense.
Furthermore, there is something even more terrible:

in this place of the Hell of Flaming Hair-tufts (*Jvālā-śikhā*), due to their evil karma, there are many malevolent insects called *Śikhā-sadṛśa* (Hair-tuft-like). They dwell within the hell, being as long as bowstrings; their venom is extremely fierce and their teeth are exceedingly sharp.
The Yama-wardens seize the hell-beings, bind their hands and feet, and lay their bodies upon a ground of intensely heated iron with glowing iron hooks.
Thus those hell-beings undergo suffering; they cry out and wail as their backs are first scorched, experiencing extreme agony.

The Yama-wardens seize the *keśarāja* worms and place them at the anus; those *keśarāja* worms are shaped like bowstrings. Entering the body, they inflict the most intense, hard, and agonizing pain; their touch is like fire, first burning the anus, and having burned it, they devour it.
Having devoured the anus, they next move upward into the *pakvāśaya* (receptacle for digested food); having burned it, they devour it.
Having devoured the *pakvāśaya*, they next move upward into the *āmāśaya* (receptacle for undigested food), where they immediately burn the *āmāśaya* and devour it as well.

Having eaten thus, they then enter the small and large intestines in succession, burning and gnawing them as they eat; having consumed everything in this way within the body, they run everywhere throughout the interior of the offender’s body like young white pigeons, yet he still does not die.
Thus these evil insects run toward the throat-tube; before they have even reached it, they burn and cook the heart, and having burned it, they devour it entirely.

The person in that hell undergoes such suffering, wailing and crying out; thus that person is burned by two fires: within the body there are the *śikhā-ākāra* (topknot-like) insects that devour, and outside the body there is the great fire of the hell.
Once that keśarāśi-worm has finished devouring the pharynx-tube, it proceeds toward the face; having reached the face, it first burns the root of the tongue;
having burned the root of the tongue, it bites and devours it;
having devoured it thus, it proceeds toward the ear-organ and devours the ear as well.
Having devoured the ear-faculty, it runs toward the skull and next devours the brain;
once it has finished eating, it breaks through the head and exits.

Yet that person in hell still does not die, due to the power of their evil karma. There are holes throughout their entire body, and these same evil insects enter within those holes; furthermore, they are burned by the great fires of hell, with flames blazing everywhere throughout their body, both inside and out, because of the performance of their evil karma.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they eat and eat again; having eaten, they are born again; having been born, they are eaten; and having died, they are reborn. Thus do these sinners undergo great suffering and distress, which is the power produced by the accumulation of their evil karma.

Once those hell-beings have escaped from that place, they run toward another location; there they see a multitude of great serpents coming all at once, and upon seeing them, they become utterly terrified and flee toward yet another place.
These multitudes of snakes, produced by their evil karma, rush toward those sinners as swiftly as the wind.

Upon arrival, they coil and constrict their entire bodies; their fangs are extremely sharp and possess potent, lethal venom. They bite those sinners, who then undergo hundreds of thousands of kinds of most extreme suffering.
Those hell-beings are thus scorched by three fires:
first, the fire of hunger and thirst;
second, the fire of snake venom; [and third, the fire of their own karma].
Third, the fires of hell.

Thus they are constantly burned in this manner for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years; there is no counting the years, as the duration is so vast. Until their evil karma is destroyed and decayed, until the potency of that karma is exhausted, they shall suffer without ceasing at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.

Once they have attained liberation from that state, for immeasurable thousands of lifetimes they are born among hungry ghosts and animals; within the realm of hungry ghosts, they are utterly consumed by hunger and thirst;
and throughout their births among all manner of animals, they are constantly killed and eaten by others.
If one is released from that place, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a wooden yoke.
If one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, for five hundred lifetimes one will be the "third person," namely, a eunuch.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the location of the Great Intense Heat (Mahātapana) Great Hell.
He sees, hears, and knows:
Furthermore, there is another place called Rain of Sand and Fire, which is the fourth distinct sub-region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? They see:

There are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they delight in practicing these acts and perform them frequently. Their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is another form of misconduct:
having committed an evil act against a śrāmaṇerī, one feels joy in one’s heart and continues to take pleasure in it.

Because of these causes and conditions of such evil karma, when that person’s body breaks up at the end of life, they fall into an evil destination and undergo great suffering in that hell, in the place called "Rain of Sand and Fire."
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies experienced in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are fully endured here.
Furthermore, there is something even more severe:

that place is filled with great fires five hundred yojanas deep, with flames blazing everywhere; it is strewn with diamond sand as soft as water, yet it can burn people, inspiring fear even in those who dread being submerged, let alone those in hell with their heavy and evil karma.
When those hell-beings enter it, they sink as if into water; due to the cause of their evil karma, having sunk, they emerge again.

Those vajra-sands consist of three-cornered fragments with blades of fire that are extremely sharp; they rub against the bodies of the sinners until even the bones are completely worn away. Once exhausted, the flesh grows back again;
once grown, it is rubbed away once more, and once rubbed away, it is worn away again.
Having perished, they are born again; having died, they are revived, with no one able to save them.
Falling into the midst of flaming sand, they wail and cry out, sighing and weeping; because of their evil karma, they cannot free themselves from that place of suffering, for a vast duration of time.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted do they finally escape from that hellish realm.
Even after escaping that place, they will be born among hungry ghosts and animals for immeasurable thousands of lifetimes.
If born among hungry ghosts, they will be scorched and boiled by hunger and thirst;
among animals, they will devour one another, and for a thousand lifetimes they will constantly be killed by others.
If one is released from that place, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as for a turtle to encounter a hole in a floating yoke.
Even if one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will be constantly poor and constantly ill, untrusted by others, and become a eunuch.
This is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the Great Intense Heat Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called Inner Boiling Heat, which is the fifth secondary region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they delight in practicing these acts and perform them frequently, with karma and its retribution as previously described.
Furthermore, there are those with wrong views and wrong conduct who,
against an upāsikā who observes the five precepts, forcibly commit unrighteous acts, defiling her celibate life and causing her precepts to be broken and ruined.
He forms this thought: "Breaking the precepts incurs no sin; one does not believe in the results of karma.

Because of these evil intentions and the causal conditions of such evil karmic actions, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, undergoing great suffering and affliction in the "Boiling Heat" section within that hell.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies experienced in the Saṃjīva and other hells are fully endured here.

Furthermore, there are even more severe ones, namely: five volcanic mountains in that place which are internally hot and boiling; these five mountains pervade the entire hell, all of which are hot and boiling. Their names are: first, Universal Incineration; second, Utterly Deep and Bottomless; third, Mass of Dark Fire upon Contact; fourth, Severing and Cutting; and fifth, Testimony of Karma. These extend throughout that hell for a thousand yojanas.

These five mountains are situated at an immense distance from Mount Universal Wheel (Samantacakra) and Mount Great Wheel (Mahācakra). When the inhabitants of that hell see those five mountains adorned with blue lotuses (*utpala*) and fully endowed with groves of trees and ponds, they long for those places and, desiring to find peace and happiness, run toward them with great haste.
Due to their evil karma, within that mountain, fire is fanned by an evil wind; once blown upon, it blazes fiercely, burning the hell-beings so that their entire bodies writhe and twist.
Having been thus burned, they again see a mountain, blue and vast; suffering from the burning, they run toward it once more, hoping for rescue and seeking refuge.

Once they reached that mountain, their momentum caused them to fall into its midst, just as an iron arrow released from a bowstring shoots into an anthill; having entered thus, they do not know where they are.
In this way, in this manner, those hell-beings are submerged without any place of refuge within the intensely boiling volcanic mountains.

Having been thus scorched, boiled, and roasted there, those hell-beings further enter into the midst of dark masses of fire and touch the evil mountains; their sensory faculties are obstructed as they undergo every suffering, like arrows piercing a target, fully experiencing the retribution of all their evil karma.

Thus, these sinners, having accumulated evil karma, find themselves amidst a mass of dark fire that touches upon a mountain of woe. There they undergo the bitter suffering of such results—intense, violent, and cruel—with no protector, no savior, and no companion. Consuming the fruits of their own karma, they endure extreme agony for a long time, constantly burned and constantly boiled, blown by the winds of karma; in those places of seething heat, their entire bodies are cooked.

Having emerged from that place, because they lack the strength of feet, they are unable to run away; the *Yama* messengers seize them once more and place them upon the Mountain of Slicing. With iron saws ablaze with fire, they cut their male organs; once cut, they grow back again, and as soon as they are newly grown, tender and soft, they are cut yet again. In this manner, they undergo immeasurable hundreds of thousands of cuts from the saws, enduring great suffering and affliction.
Furthermore, he again entered the Karmanirvartana mountain to undergo great suffering and distress, crying out in verse:
“As I myself have committed these deeds, So do I now receive their fruit;
Because the enemy of desire has scorched me, I have now arrived at this hell.”
Heedlessness is unwholesome; the fire of desire burns the human body.
Bound by its snare, I have come to this place.
Previously, I did not know that the fruit of desire is such suffering.
Deceived by ignorance, I now experience what I myself created.
This pitiless and evil person has brought me here to this shoreless ocean of suffering; how can I ever be liberated?
"Karma is the most bitter among all sufferings; I now undergo it in this way.
I have never seen any happiness, for the suffering of hell is inexhaustible.
Thus did that person in hell, undergoing the foremost suffering in the Ash-Fire Hell, cry out in lamentation.

Those hell-beings constantly experience great suffering and affliction at all times; as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they will be subjected to uninterrupted suffering at every moment.
Only when their evil karma is fully exhausted can they finally escape from that place in hell.
Once they have attained liberation from that, they will again, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, be born in the realms of hungry ghosts and animals:
among the hungry ghosts, they will see one another and their bodies will be consumed by hunger and thirst;
among the animals, they will devour one another, dying and being reborn again and again for hundreds of thousands of lifetimes.
Once that person has escaped from that place, it is as difficult for them to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a floating yoke.
Even if they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, due to the power of their evil karma, they will be impoverished, frequently ill, and physically incomplete.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the Great Intense Heat Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place called Tāṭatāṭacici, which is the sixth distinct sub-region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are people who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they take pleasure in practicing these and perform them frequently, with karma and its retribution as previously described.
Furthermore, there is misconduct, namely:

engaging in unchaste conduct with a woman who has correctly received the precepts; doing so perhaps once, twice, thrice, four times, or five times. Such a person engages in this improper conduct, whether with a sister, or one of the same clan, or a fellow disciple, or the wife of a fellow disciple, or the wife of a spiritual friend, seducing them into misconduct.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, being born within the specific hell of *ṭaṭataṭacici*, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies experienced in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are fully endured here.
Furthermore, there is something even more severe:

a most violent wind makes contact with them, blowing and lashing with extreme force, causing the bodies of those hell-beings to break apart piece by piece like cotton wool, violently shaking them as if flinging out wool.

Thus, by the force of an extremely violent and fierce wind, the bodies of these offenders are blown apart, piece by piece and fragment by fragment, until they are scattered like fine hairs, such that even the hairs themselves can no longer be seen.
What are the hairs? They are the hairs of the *karpāsa* (cotton) plant.
Just as those hairs, once scattered, come back together again, so too does the body of that sinner.
Blown by fierce winds, they are scattered in the ten directions.

Within that hell, those sinful persons are subjected to winds as sharp as knives, which cut, split, and pulverize them like sand until not a single thing remains visible; even their body parts and hairs can no longer be seen.
Due to their evil karma, all their limbs and members are born again; once born, they disintegrate once more, for such is the power of desire.
Desire is as previously described.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, as long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience uninterrupted suffering at all times.

If they escape from this suffering, there are further fierce diamond rats in that place which devour their sexual organs, tearing them apart until they are as small as mustard seeds, while the beings cry out in agony.
Having devoured the human root, they next devour the intestines;
having devoured the intestines, they next devour the large intestine;
having devoured the large intestine, they exit through the back and next devour the back.
Having finished eating the flesh of the back, they next eat the backbones.

Due to their evil karma, those people of evil deeds undergo such hellish suffering for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years; after a long period of time, they finally obtain release from that place of torment.

Once they have escaped, they run toward another place, where black insects further wrap and constrict their bodies; first wrapping around the male organ, they burn and devour it, causing them to experience extreme agony as they cry out with loud screams.

Thus these black insects constantly coil around and constantly devour them; as long as the evil karma they have accumulated has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that place of hell.

Once they have attained liberation from that state, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, they are born among the hungry ghosts who eat their own flesh, consuming the flesh of their own bodies.

Although they consume their own flesh, they do not die; because during the time they committed their karma they engaged in unchaste conduct with their own sisters and others for their own pleasure, they must now consume the flesh of their own bodies while among the hungry ghosts.

If they escape from that place, they will be born among animals as female pigs who eat their own offspring, because during their time as humans they committed the karma of sexual misconduct toward their own relatives.
Once that person has been released from that place, it is as difficult for them to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a wooden yoke.

If they are born among humans in a place of similar karma, that person will constantly suffer from a malignant disease of the male organ; because of the urgency of this malignant disease of the organ, they will cut off their own organ.

Due to the causal conditions of that karma, even if one has a wife of one's own, one may be violated and coerced by low-born persons, engaging in sexual misconduct with unsuitable partners; this is because, when performing those actions, one committed adultery with another’s wife.
Among all evils, wrong views and wrong conduct are the most profound and grave; these unwholesome karmas are incompatible with both the mundane and the supramundane.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, contemplates the Great Intense Heat Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place, called "Universally Receiving All Suffering of the Means of Subsistence," which is the seventh distinct location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they delight in practicing these acts and perform them frequently. Their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is misconduct, namely:

out of a mind of lustful attachment, a bhikṣu engages in improper conduct by using alcohol to entice and deceive a virtuous woman; having corrupted her mind, he subsequently engages in sexual intercourse with her or gives her wealth.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination; there, in that hell, they experience all manner of suffering regarding the necessities of life and undergo great torment.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies suffered in the Reviving Hell (*Saṃjīva*) and other such hells are experienced here in their entirety.

Those people constantly cultivate the seeds of suffering, abandoning virtuous conduct and practicing the path of evil. Such practitioners of unwholesome and evil karma, habituated to the unwholesome path and delighting in its practice, undergo even more severe suffering in that hell due to the causes and conditions of their evil karmic actions—extremely urgent, harsh, and heavy agonies. All the sufferings experienced in the Reviving Hell and others are experienced here in their entirety, namely:

There, from the tips of the toes up to the head, flaming knives flay all the skin of the body without piercing the flesh; thus they strip away every part of the body, inflicting great agony. Having flayed the skin, which remains attached to the body, they spread it upon the hot ground and burn it with fire.

Since their bodies are already devoid of skin, the Yama-wardens fill hot iron basins with boiling ashes and pour them over their bodies; thus scorched, steamed, and boiled, those people undergo great suffering, crying out loudly, groaning, and wailing.

Thus they undergo great suffering for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years; for countless ages they cannot be liberated, constantly enduring such harsh and rigid torments. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall suffer without ceasing at all times.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be released from that hellish place.

If, in a past life long ago, there was ripening of wholesome karma, one will not be born in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals; obtaining a human body is as difficult as a turtle encountering a hole in a floating log.

If they are born among humans in places of similar karma, they will always be poor and always sick, suffering from most grievous illnesses. Beings born on the seashore through similar karma will have incomplete human forms—namely, having only one foot, one eye, or one arm; their bodies will be uniquely stunted and their lives will not be long, perhaps lasting only a single day. Such are the places where they are born.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the Great Intensely Heating Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is yet another distinct location, namely a river called Vitaraṇī, which burns and sweeps away with violence; this is the eighth separate sub-region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place? He sees:

there are those who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they delight in practicing these acts and perform them frequently. Their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is another form of misconduct, namely:

there are those who, having burned incense and sought a wife, take her hand in marriage; yet though that wife has committed no fault, they conceive feelings of loathing and contempt, yet forcibly commit transgressions with her, and even after having committed such transgressions, they still continue to take pleasure in engaging in sexual desire together.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination, to the place of the great river of fierce burning and violent tossing in the Vaitaraṇī hell, where they undergo great suffering and affliction.

As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies experienced in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are fully endured here. Furthermore, there are even more severe sufferings, namely:

within a mass of darkness in the void, hot iron clubs rain down, produced by one's own evil karma. These clubs are extremely sharp; they pierce into the bodies of the hell-beings, and once inside, they burn intensely, boring holes throughout every part of the body. They split, cut, burn, and boil, causing every limb and member to be completely severed. As fire burns both internally and externally, they undergo extreme agony and distress.

Having been split thus by flaming iron clubs, they undergo extreme great suffering; that pain is so harsh and intense it is beyond analogy. Having undergone such great suffering, those hell-beings run hither and thither until they fall onto a precipitous bank. Beneath the bank is a river named Vaitaraṇī, which fiercely burns and violently sweeps away.

Due to their evil karma, the place is filled with venomous snakes; when the sinners see them, they are struck with terror and extreme suffering. These evil snakes have flaming fangs and virulent poison; they crush the sinners' bodies into pieces as small as dust and devour them. They undergo immense agony, wailing and crying out in lamentation.
As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times for countless years.
Only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be released from that place of hell.

If they do not fall into the realms of hungry ghosts or animals—where it is as difficult to obtain a human body as for a turtle to encounter a floating log with a single hole—and instead are born among humans of similar karma, they will be constantly poor and constantly ill, perpetually beset by sorrow and suffering, and subject to the commands of others. Their faculties will be incomplete; they will be born in frontier lands amidst frozen mountains and snow mountains, their faces being extremely ugly like those of mules, subsisting only on roots and fruits to preserve their lives, never having known such foods as rice or millet.
This is the residual karmic retribution of their original deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the Great Intensely Hot Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called Uninterrupted Darkness (*anantāndhakāra*), which is the ninth specific sub-region of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are people who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they delight in practicing these and do them frequently, and their karma and its retribution are as previously described.

Furthermore, there may be those who, having abandoned the bonds of external defiled objects and the three afflictions of greed, hatred, and delusion, are persons who practice virtue with mild diligence; yet, women are sent to entice and persuade them so that they fall away from their resolve.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination, undergoing great suffering and affliction in the dark region of that Avīci Hell.
As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the harsh and evil sufferings experienced in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are all fully experienced here.
Furthermore, there is something even more severe:
in that hell there are earth-worms whose mouths and snouts are so extremely sharp they can shatter even vajra into water-foam.

Due to the evil karma of the offenders, such worms exist there; the suffering obtained from those wicked insects is more intense than the suffering of the hell itself, such that when one undergoes the suffering of the worms, the suffering of that hell becomes like great bliss by comparison.

In that place, the *bhūmipāta* worms break the bones of the sinners and eat their marrow; the combination of all the various sufferings within that hell does not equal even one hundredth part of the suffering from these worms, nor one thousandth part, nor even one hundred-thousandth part.
Unable to escape from those evil insects, they run about everywhere, yet in every place they go, they cannot find liberation.

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they are constantly burned and boiled; they undergo such suffering, which is the most evil and most heavy of all the afflictions suffered by the sinners in other hells.
At all times, they are thus burned and boiled in that hellish place yet do not die.

By the power of the accumulation of their evil karma, they are constantly burned and constantly boiled in that confluence of hells; as long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they shall suffer incessantly at all times.
Only when the evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish place.

If, in a past life long ago, there were matured roots of wholesome karma, one would not be born in the realms of hungry ghosts or animals; obtaining a human body would be as difficult as a turtle encountering a hole in a floating log.

If one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will be born into the household of a courtesan and become her slave; one’s complexion will be unsightly, the hands and feet will be cracked, and one will constantly carry water.
This is the residual karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the Great Intensely Hot Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another distinct location called the Place of the Garland of Suffering (*Duḥkhamālā*), which is the tenth secondary division of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are people who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they delight in practicing these and do them frequently, with karma and its retribution as previously described.
Furthermore, there is the evil of sexual misconduct:
there may be a virtuous bhikṣu who upholds the precepts and practices correctly, remaining unoffended by the Vinaya.

Because of some matter concerning his family lineage, he becomes fearful and enters the house of a person he trusts; however, the mistress of that house is a woman of illicit conduct, and she says to him:
"A bhikṣu has engaged in sexual desire with me.
If he refuses, I shall report it so that the bhikṣu will certainly be punished by the king.
Or I shall tell my husband, saying these words:"
“The bhikṣu has violated me.

“If he desires me, I shall give the bhikṣu much solid food (*khādaniya*) and various delicious drinks; then the two of us, the bhikṣu and I, will experience supreme pleasure, and no one else will know.”
I said to others: "This bhikṣu is foremost in observing the precepts.
He has many bedding and requisites, and is fully provided with donors for medicines and medical necessities; I am able to instruct him so that he will surely obtain everything he needs."
"In this way, that person deceives the virtuous bhikṣu and causes him to retreat from the true path.

Due to the causal conditions of such evil karma, when the woman’s body perishes and her life ends, she falls into an evil destination; born in that hell in the place called *Duḥkhamālā* (The Garland of Suffering), she undergoes great torment."
Regarding what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies endured in the Reviving Hell and other such hells are experienced here in their entirety.
Furthermore, there are even more severe ones, namely:

the Yama-wardens seize those women and, with sharp iron brushes, scrub their skin and flesh until the flesh is gone and only bone remains; yet it grows back again, and being soft and tender once more, they brush it yet again.
Once they have been brushed, the flesh grows back; once it has grown back, it is brushed again.

The Yama-wardens seize those women; as the flesh grows back even more profusely, it becomes tender and soft once more, and they brush their bodies all over with flaming iron brushes, which are then set ablaze.
Thus these women undergo extreme suffering; wailing and weeping, they have accumulated evil karma and constantly experience such suffering at all times, running hither and thither.
Due to their evil karma, they see the original bhikṣu coming toward them; deceived by their lustful desires, they run forward swiftly, for the enmity of their karma is difficult to abandon.
In such a place of suffering, their lustful mind still persists; seeing that bhikṣu embrace their bodies, they enter a pit of fire, which blazes with flames on all sides.

In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, they undergo the foremost of all intense sufferings at the Place of the Garland of Suffering. As long as their evil karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and the potency of that karma has not been exhausted, they shall experience unceasing suffering at all times;
only when their evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish realm.
Even after escaping that place, one will be born among animals for five hundred lifetimes.
If one escapes from there, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as a turtle encountering a hole in a floating yoke.
If one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, one will become a woman who constantly clears away excrement and filth within the city.

Among all the people within the city, he was the most base and lowly: poor, ugly, with cracked hands and feet, a hare-lip, and an extremely foul complexion. He had no father, no mother, and no kinsmen, brothers, or sisters; he constantly lived by begging food from others. His clothes were tattered, filthy, and impure, and his body was missing one side.
In his exposed parts, his flesh was scarred and broken; he was beaten and pelted by children, living in constant suffering.
This is the residual retribution of that evil karma.
*The Sutra on the Foundations of Mindfulness of the True Dharma*, Scroll 12 [and] Scroll 13.
Translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Chapter on the Hells, Part Nine:
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the retribution of karma, observes the Great Intense Heat Great Hell; what other places are there?
Through seeing, hearing, and knowing,
he perceives that there is another distinct location called the Place of Raining Garlands and Shaking, which is the eleventh location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are people who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they delight in practicing these and perform them frequently, and their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is sexual misconduct, which is defined as follows:

to violate a virtuous bhikṣuṇī; or, during times of upheaval when the land is in turmoil, to forcibly assault and defile a maiden bhikṣuṇī who maintains right conduct and observes the precepts, taking advantage of the instability of the times to corrupt her pure practice.

Due to these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and their life ends, they fall into an evil destination and are born in that hell at the place called "Shaking the Rain of Garlands," where they undergo great suffering and affliction.

As for what is called suffering, it is as previously described: all the agonies experienced in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are fully endured here. Furthermore, there is something even more severe:

in that place, there are immeasurable sharp diamond blades forming a net that covers everywhere. As one moves about, the body is sliced whenever it stirs; the entire body is cut all over. Thus, the net of diamond-edged threads binds the sinner. Just as a fly might be caught within fine wool, the sinner there is born and dies again within that net, dying and being reborn repeatedly.
The Yama-wardens shoot their bodies with flaming iron arrows, piercing them everywhere.

Thus, these sinners, bound by diamond nets and struck by flaming arrows, undergo the most rigid and supreme suffering; they shriek, groan, wail, and weep, enduring great agony as their entire bodies are shattered and held in total bondage.

If that sinner manages to escape from that place, having endured extreme suffering due to the causes and conditions of his evil karma, he flees in every direction and enters again a mass of blazing, universal burning coals; his body melts away, and as his body burns, he cries out in lamentation, solitary and without companion.
Seeing a great gate from afar, with light emanating from it, he runs toward it with all his might.
Having reached it, there is a great python whose venom is exceedingly fierce; he enters its mouth, and that person in hell is burned within it, unable to cry out.

Thus, by the serpent of karma, as that evil karma revolves, the person in hell has all their limbs shattered like sand; they cannot cry out, and all their sinews and veins are completely crushed and destroyed. In this manner, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya years, they are scorched, writhed, and destroyed within the belly of the serpent.

When such a sinner emerges from the mouth of the python, all the sinews and veins throughout his body become slack; he runs about everywhere, yet again sees the henchmen of Yama coming to seize him, who cut and hack every part of his body with sharp iron knives, as if mincing eels.

Thus, for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, beyond calculation, they constantly experience great suffering and affliction at all times. As long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its residual force has not been exhausted, they will continue to suffer incessantly at all times;
only when that evil karma is exhausted will they finally be liberated from that hellish realm.
Even after attaining liberation from that state, one will be born among hungry ghosts and animals for five hundred lifetimes.
Having escaped from those realms, it is as difficult to obtain a human body as it is for a turtle to encounter a hole in a floating wooden yoke.

If they are born among humans in places of similar karma, they will be impoverished and constantly ill; their physical appearance will be unsightly, and their bodies will always be afflicted with foul sores and toxic ulcers, perpetually undergoing suffering and distress.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, contemplates the Great Intensely Heating Great Hell.
What other places are there?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place called Hair-Confessing Crows (Keśa-vilajjā-kākā), which is the twelfth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?

He sees: there are people who kill living beings, steal, engage in sexual misconduct, drink intoxicants, speak falsehoods, and hold wrong views; they delight in practicing these and perform them frequently, with karma and its retribution as previously described.
Furthermore, there is sexual misconduct:
whether due to intoxication from alcohol or because of excessive lust, one commits adultery with one's elder sister or younger sister.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when that person’s body perishes and life ends, they fall into an evil destination and undergo great suffering in that hell known as the *Keśakambala* (Hair-Covered) region.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies endured in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are experienced here in their entirety.
Furthermore, there are even more severe sufferings, namely:

one falls into a copper cauldron of blazing flames, where the body melts away; yet it re-forms and melts once more within that cauldron. Thus, having been born, one dies again; having died, one is born again, constantly undergoing great torment.

Thus, within that furnace, the Yama-wardens blow upon it with two bellows; the furnace fire and the sinner cannot be distinguished. In this manner, they are boiled within the furnace for immeasurable hundreds and thousands of years, no different from smelting gold among men. In such a way, they are thus scorched and boiled in that hell.

When those who have committed evil deeds escape from that cauldron and emerge from the copper furnace, the *yama-puruṣas* place them upon an iron spike and strike them with an iron mallet, just as a blacksmith strikes a lump of iron. While being struck in this manner, they die at each blow, yet when the mallet is lifted, they return to life.
Those hell-beings are constantly being burned and boiled at all times for countless years.

If they escape that place, the Yama-wardens place them inside a drum; once placed within the drum, due to their evil karma, the drum emits a terrifying sound. Upon hearing it, their hearts shatter. Having scattered, they are born again; having been born, they scatter once more. In this way, those people die and are revived, and having been revived, they die again.
As long as the accumulated evil and unwholesome karma has not been destroyed or decayed, and its karmic force has not been exhausted, suffering will continue without ceasing at all times;
only when that evil karma is exhausted will one finally be liberated from that place in hell.
Even after escaping that place, one will be born among animals for six hundred lifetimes.

If one is born among humans in a place of similar karma, the mind is constantly filled with alarm and fear; like wild deer, the mind is startled and restless, always dreading being unjustly bound by officials, having an extremely short lifespan, and never finding peace of mind from the outset.
This is the remaining karmic retribution of those evil deeds.
Furthermore, that bhikṣu, knowing the fruits of karma, observes the Great Intense Heat Great Hell: what other places are there within it?
He sees, hears, and knows:
there is another place called Sorrowful Howl (Karūṇāraṭa), which is the thirteenth location of that hell.
By what karma are sentient beings born in that place?
He sees, hears, and knows:
if a person delights in and frequently commits killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, drinking intoxicants, lying, and wrong views, their karma and its retribution are as previously described.
Furthermore, there is sexual misconduct, namely:
there are those who, regarding their own sisters, see wicked and heterodox teachings within a ritual assembly and engage in sexual desire with them.
They hear these heterodox teachings from a Brahmin:
"If a woman desires a man and he does not accept her, she incurs a great sin.
That brāhmaṇa then devised this plan:
"If it were not so, one would break the law and incur guilt."
Thus, deceived by hearing such false and evil teachings, they engage in unwholesome conduct.

Because of these causes and conditions of evil karma, when their bodies perish and their lives end, they fall into an evil destination; they undergo great suffering and affliction in that hell known as the Place of Wailing and Howling.
As for what is called suffering: as previously described, all the agonies suffered in the Reviving Hell and the other hells are experienced here in their entirety.
Furthermore, there are even more severe ones, namely:

there, the minions of Yama use red-hot flaming iron pestles to pound and crush them with extreme force, destroying their entire bodies until not a spot remains intact, even as small as a grain of rice or a bean. Their whole bodies become covered in sores; every part of their person is a wound, and they universally endure the agony of heat. Alone and without companion, they suffer harsh and rigid torment for an immeasurable duration of years.
When the causes of their karma are exhausted, they escape from such blazing iron pestles and run hither and thither, only to enter the iron ground again.
That iron ground is ablaze with flames; having entered, they fall upon it and undergo great suffering, crying out and wailing.
He further saw a great forest not far away, its color like blue clouds, peaceful throughout, and filled with the songs of birds; not far from it was a large pond of water, pure and lovely.
Those hell-beings give rise to this thought:
"That is the foremost forest of tranquility and the pure waters of a pond; there, I shall obtain peace and happiness."

Seeking rescue and seeking refuge, they run toward a forest; yet it is a place where masses of flames gather and the ground is of glowing-hot iron. Amidst this, the offenders see that forest not far away, filled with many birds. Those hell-beings rush toward the forest, hoping for peace, seeking rescue, and seeking refuge.

Having endured such extreme great suffering, that person arrives at the grove; everything he sees is different from what he saw before, and all is evil and utterly terrifying. That is to say, there is a great-mouthed, wicked dragon there with a thousand heads, its eyes blazing with flame and its venom most fiercely burning—all these are the very trees he previously saw.
The sounds of the various birds he previously heard are now entirely the cries of hell-beings whose bodies are ablaze with flames.
